features.title: Model Version Registry — One Row Decides What Is In Production
features.description: Give a Model a versioned, staged history so that promotion and rollback are row changes. Nothing here serves anything; this is the pointer everything downstream reads.

tasks.title: ModelVersion entity
tasks.detail: Shape depends on MODEL-SERVE-000-T02. Fields: modelId, version, the artifact pointer and checksum, feature spec reference, framework + version, sourceRunId, sourceDatasetId, metrics, stage, timestamps, promotedById. A version row is IMMUTABLE except for stage — same discipline as MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's adopt-by-pointer: the row records what happened, it is not a workspace.
tasks.detail_addendum: REVISED 2026-08-24: the artifact reference is NOT optional and NOT derivable later. Because the run directory holds no feature spec (see findings), ModelVersion must record the fitted DatasetArtifact's id and its featureSpecKey explicitly, alongside the model object pointer. Resolving it at serve time by walking to the dataset's CURRENT artifact would be silently wrong for any model whose dataset was edited after training — and it would be wrong in the direction that still returns a number.
tasks.audit_2026_09_01: MODEL-SERVE-000 confirmed the run row already stores exactly this (ModelTrainingRun.goldArtifactId/goldObjectKey/artifactChecksum/featureSpecKey, verified non-null on 73/73 runs) — this task copies those four fields onto ModelVersion at promotion-worthy points, it does not invent them. Also: decisions.open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_bytes is now open and must be resolved as part of this task — does ModelVersion reference the source artifact by pointer (per MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's adopt-by-pointer rule) or copy its bytes into a version-owned prefix (per DS-LAKE-025's adopt_artifact precedent)? Record the choice in that decision with its rejected alternative.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. `ModelVersion` model + `ModelVersionStage` enum added to schema.prisma (migration 20260901090000_model_serve_001_model_version), migrated and verified against the live dev DB. decisions.open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_bytes resolved POINTER with rejected alternative recorded (see that decision). FOUND AND FIXED DURING IMPLEMENTATION, NOT PART OF THE ORIGINAL SPEC: (1) the migration's `ModelVersion_sourceRunId_fkey` was originally `ON DELETE RESTRICT` — verified live (rolled-back transaction, then a real cascade-delete of a seeded Model+run+version) that this breaks `deleteModelService` (`model.authorized.service.ts`'s bare `prisma.model.delete`), because a Model delete cascades onto BOTH ModelTrainingRun and ModelVersion in one statement and RESTRICT is checked immediately per-row rather than deferred to end-of-statement. Changed to `NO ACTION` in both the migration and schema.prisma, migration dropped and cleanly reapplied (table was empty, zero data loss) since it had already been applied by an earlier session with the broken FK. Re-verified live: a real `DELETE FROM "Model"` with a full Model+run+version chain now cascades cleanly. (2) `model_sha256` — needed for `ModelVersion.modelChecksum` — was NOT actually a `ModelTrainingRun` column despite three docstrings (RunManifestRequest, RunManifestResponse's router description, get_run_manifest) all claiming it was; verified against schema.prisma and fixed at the source: `get_run_manifest`/`RunManifestResponse` now read and return it from run_manifest.json (same honest-legacy-null policy as framework_versions), all three stale docstrings corrected in place. Live-verified against a real run's manifest: `model_sha256` now returns `'b5d52d61150a161...117065'` where it previously silently returned nothing. Save Model (T03) now populates version 1's `modelChecksum` from this.

tasks.title: Stage machine and the single-production constraint
tasks.detail: STAGING -> PRODUCTION -> ARCHIVED. Enforce at most one PRODUCTION per modelId AT THE DATABASE, with a partial unique index, not in service code. Application-level uniqueness under concurrent promotes is the same class of hole MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's 409 guard closes for double-save, and the same reason MODEL-FLOW-002-T07 used a CHECK constraint rather than a service check.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. `ModelVersion_one_production_per_model`, a partial unique index (`ON ("modelId") WHERE stage = 'PRODUCTION'`), same hand-written-migration precedent as `ModelFineTuningJob_one_live_per_draft` — Prisma's schema DSL cannot express a partial index. The pure stage-transition predicate lives at `apps/backend/src/lib/model-version-transitions.ts` (`isPromotable`), mirroring `dataset-version-transitions.ts`'s shape but a DIFFERENT graph: ARCHIVED -> PRODUCTION is legal here (a rollback is a promote), which the dataset side's strict forward line does not allow — documented in that file's own doc comment. Live-proven under real concurrency in V01 (see verification).

tasks.title: Save Model creates version 1 in STAGING, never PRODUCTION
tasks.detail: Saving is not deploying. A wizard whose last click puts a model in front of live traffic has no step at which someone decides it should be. This is additive to MODEL-FLOW-007-T04's transaction, inside the same transaction — a Model with no version row is a state nothing downstream can interpret.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. `ModelDraftAuthorizedService.saveDraftService` (model-draft.authorized.service.ts) now creates `ModelVersion` version 1 inside the SAME `$transaction` as the `Model` create and the `ModelTrainingRun`/`ModelDraft` updates — no separate write, no window where a Model can exist without a version row. `version: 1` is hardcoded (not max()+1: `created` is a brand-new Model in this same transaction, so no other version can exist yet — a future retrain minting a later version needs DS-LAKE-009-T03's max()+1 allocation, this path does not). `stage` is never set on create, so it takes the schema's `STAGING` default — verified live via V01's seed rows (queried back as STAGING before any promote). Fields are copied one-hop from the adopted `ModelTrainingRun` row's own pinned columns, never re-derived through the dataset's current artifact.

tasks.title: Promote and rollback endpoints
tasks.detail: POST .../versions/:v/promote and POST .../rollback, both recording who and when. Rollback is promote pointed at the previous PRODUCTION — not a distinct mechanism, so it cannot rot separately. Envelope per the findings.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. New module `apps/backend/src/api/v1/model-version/` (mirroring the model-run/model-draft/model-draft-cleanup convention of one module per feature despite tight coupling to Model), registered in `app.module.ts`. `POST authorized/model/:modelId/versions/:version/promote` (`:version` is the integer version number, not the row id — a human-operable natural key given `@@unique([modelId, version])`) and `POST authorized/model/:modelId/rollback`. Both funnel through one private `promote()` method — rollback resolves the most-recently-`archivedAt` ARCHIVED row and calls the SAME gate (T05 object check, T06 r2 floor), per the feature's own 'not a distinct mechanism' decision. Both record `promotedById`/`promotedAt`. Standard `{statusCode, message, type, data}` envelope, editor-level access (`assertModelAccess`, same rule as every other mutating Model route). An already-PRODUCTION promote is an idempotent no-op, matching `isLegalTransition`'s own documented policy split on the dataset side. TIGHTENED DURING ADVISORY REVIEW: rollback's lookup originally read `where: { stage: 'ARCHIVED', archivedAt: { not: null } }` — correct only BY ABSENCE, since only `promote()` writes ARCHIVED today, not by construction. Added `promotedAt: { not: null }` (set only by `promote()`'s own transaction) so a version that reaches ARCHIVED through some future path without ever having been PRODUCTION cannot become a rollback target. Also: the override's `actorName` was `user.email` — changed to the same firstName/lastName-then-fallback resolution `updateModelService`'s `editorName` already uses, so a promotion override records the same identity string as the rest of the Model audit trail rather than a login email.

tasks.title: Refuse to promote a version whose artifact cannot be loaded
tasks.detail: Verify object existence and checksum BEFORE flipping the stage. A promote that succeeds against a missing or altered object turns a deploy into an outage discovered by the first request, and the rollback path is then also untested. This is the one place a slow check is worth it.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. No existing primitive covered this — `/artifacts/presign` is hard-restricted to committed dataset artifacts (`is_committed_artifact_key`) and refuses `model.joblib` outright, so a new endpoint was added rather than reusing it: `POST /v1/preprocess/models/runs/verify-object` (`artifact_service.verify_model_object`, guarded by the same `is_draft_run_key`/`is_model_run_key` structural check `run_predictions`/`get_run_manifest` already use) returns `{exists, checksum}`, checksum computed from the object's own bytes via `store.checksum_of`. Backend wrapper `verifyModelObject` in `python-preprocess-client.ts`. `promote()` calls it BEFORE the transaction: refuses (422) if `!exists` unconditionally, and refuses (422) on a checksum mismatch ONLY when `ModelVersion.modelChecksum` is non-null. NAMED EXPLICITLY, NOT LEFT IMPLICIT (flagged in advisory review): `modelChecksum` is null for any version whose source run predates the manifest recording `model_sha256` — MODEL-SERVE-000-T04's own servability census found the ledger's own most-cited example run is exactly this shape — so for those versions the checksum half of this task's acceptance criterion does not apply; only existence is checked. This is the same honest-legacy-null policy `frameworkVersions` already established, not a gap introduced here, but the acceptance criterion 'promoting a version whose checksum does not match fails' holds unconditionally only for versions created after this change (i.e. every version going forward, since T01 now populates `modelChecksum` on every save whose manifest has it). LIVE-VERIFIED end to end against real MinIO (not mocked) for the primitive itself: wrote a real object, confirmed `exists:true` + a real sha256 checksum, deleted it, confirmed `exists:false, checksum:null`, and confirmed the structural guard refuses a non-run-shaped key (e.g. a dataset artifact path) by name rather than silently accepting it. See V02.

tasks.title: Refuse to promote a version whose metrics fail a floor, unless overridden on the record
tasks.detail:
OPENED 2026-08-24 after observing r2 = -2.4068 on a run this project's own live verification recorded as successful. A negative R² is not a marginal model, it is a model with no predictive value, and there is currently no boundary at which anyone is asked whether it should go to production.

The floor must be a REFUSAL, not a warning. A warning at promote time is read once by the person who already decided to promote, which is the moment it has least effect. Make r2 <= 0 a hard block; anything above that is a judgement call and belongs to the human, not to a threshold this task invents.

An override must be possible — a deliberately weak model has legitimate uses (a baseline to beat, a smoke test of the serving path) — but it must be RECORDED on the ModelVersion with an actor and a reason, so that 'why is this in production' has an answer six months later. An override that leaves no trace is the same as no floor.

DO NOT PUT THIS IN THE WIZARD INSTEAD. Step 4 Evaluation showing a negative R² prominently is good and separate; MODEL-FLOW-004 owns it. The promote boundary needs its own gate because promotion is reachable without the wizard — see MODEL-SERVE-001-T04's endpoints.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED, WITH TWO GAPS THE TICKET DID NOT SPELL OUT MADE EXPLICIT DURING IMPLEMENTATION (per this feature's own advisory review): (1) an UNREADABLE r2 (no `metrics`, or `metrics.r2` not a finite number — `extractR2`, mirroring `extractRmse`'s existing narrowing convention in model-candidate-job.authorized.service.ts) is treated the SAME as a failing score, never as a silent pass — an unknown r2 is not evidence the model is good. (2) `PromoteOverrideSchema.reason` is `z.string().trim().min(1)` — REQUIRED and non-empty, enforced at the DTO boundary, not just documented as should-be-required. `promotionOverride` is `{actorId, actorName, reason, at}`, written only on the ARCHIVED->skip path (never when r2 > 0), and is part of the same atomic promote transaction so an override is never recorded without the promote it justifies actually taking effect.
tasks.client_2026_09_14: THE FLOOR HAD NO UI, AND THAT MADE IT LOOK LIKE A DIFFERENT BUG. T06's override has existed server-side since 2026-09-01, but the only client caller of promote was the create wizard's final screen (phase-6-deploy.tsx), hardcoded to version 1, create-mode only, and ending in a bare `catch {}`. So a Save & Deploy whose promote was refused by this floor reported 'deployment could not be started' with no reason, left the version in STAGING, and never reached putSchedule -- and the Model Detail page then refused Start with a hardcoded toast blaming a missing PRODUCTION version. Live DB check 2026-09-14: ZERO models anywhere had a PRODUCTION version; the only three with a version at all sat in STAGING with r2 -0.20, -0.49 and -4.76, i.e. every one of them refused by this floor, exactly as designed and invisibly. Added hooks/model/use-model-promote.ts plus a Promote control and override dialog on the Model Detail header. The floor itself is UNCHANGED: the first attempt never carries an override, the dialog opens only on the server's own 422 and quotes its message verbatim, and an empty or whitespace reason is refused before any request.

tasks.title: Retain the trainer image digest a live version names
tasks.detail: OPENED 2026-08-24. run_manifest.json pins provenance by image_digest, which is the strongest form available — and worthless once that image leaves the registry. Establish whether the registry has any GC or tag-expiry policy, and if so, exclude digests named by a non-ARCHIVED ModelVersion. This is the same class of problem as MODEL-FLOW-011-T05 and MODEL-SERVE-000-T07: a reference held in one system to an object another system is free to delete. Third instance of the pattern in this project, which is the argument for stating it as a rule rather than fixing it three times.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED AS DOCUMENTATION, PER THE TASK'S OWN SHAPE — this is an audit-and-record task, not a build task. CORRECTED DURING ADVISORY REVIEW: an earlier draft of this result claimed no `.github/workflows` directory exists, which is false — verified live: `.github/workflows/` holds `ci.yml`, `release.yml`, `_build-image.yml`, `_deploy.yml`, `security.yml`. Grepped all five for `retention|expire|gc|prune|cleanup|delete`: the only hits are `actions/upload-artifact`'s `retention-days: 7` (CI test-log artifacts) in ci.yml — unrelated to container registry images. So the CONCLUSION stands (no image garbage collection runs today) but the evidence is now the actual grep, not an absent-directory claim that was never checked. `ModelVersion.imageDigest` already retains exactly the fact a future GC policy would need to consult (a non-ARCHIVED ModelVersion's digest must be excluded from deletion) — this task's deliverable, per its own wording, is establishing that fact and recording the rule, not building a GC exclusion for a GC process that does not exist. RULE RECORDED (fourth instance of the pattern the task itself calls out as recurring — MODEL-FLOW-011-T05, MODEL-SERVE-000-T07's two exposures, and this one): if a registry GC/retention workflow is ever added to this repo, it MUST query `ModelVersion` for `imageDigest` values where `stage != 'ARCHIVED'` (STAGING and PRODUCTION both — a staged-but-not-yet-promoted version's digest must survive too) and exclude those digests, the same way `artifact-cleanup.admin.service.ts`'s cleanup query already excludes FINAL-type artifacts unconditionally.

tasks.title: The create wizard promotes version 1 by number, and what makes that safe is a UI branch rather than a fact
tasks.detail:
FILED 2026-09-14 FROM THIS FEATURE'S OWN implementation NOTE, WHICH FLAGGED IT AND DID NOT FIX IT. phase-6-deploy.tsx:142 calls promote(modelId, 1) with a literal. The flag's own words were 'untriggerable today since Save Model always mints version 1, but unguarded' -- and the FIRST HALF OF THAT SENTENCE IS THE WRONG REASON, which is why this is a task rather than a comment.

THE PREMISE IS ALREADY FALSE AT THE LAYER IT NAMES, AND WAS FALSE ELEVEN DAYS BEFORE THE FLAG WAS WRITTEN. Save Model mints version 1 (T03, hardcoded, correctly -- a brand-new Model in the same transaction can hold no other version). But MODEL-SERVE-004-T04 mints max(version)+1 via nextModelVersionNumber, and MODEL-SERVE-004-V01 LIVE-VERIFIED it on 2026-09-03: 'The new version came out as version 2, stage STAGING, sourceRunId = the job's bestRunId'. Versions above 1 exist in this system and have since a retrain first ran. So 'Save Model always mints version 1' is true and does not support the conclusion drawn from it.

WHAT ACTUALLY MAKES THE LITERAL CORRECT TODAY is a different fact, recorded in a different feature: MODEL-SERVE-006's pass_b_result states 'promote (create mode only; edit mode changes no version)'. In create mode the Model was committed in the same flow, so version 1 IS the only version and the literal is right. THAT IS A UI BRANCH. One edit widening Save & Deploy to edit mode, or a retrain UI reaching this component, removes it -- whereas the flag's stated reason reads as a structural guarantee that would survive both. VERIFY THE GATE FROM SOURCE before anything else; if promote is NOT in fact create-gated, this task is a live defect rather than a latent one and its priority changes.

WHAT IT COSTS IF IT EVER FIRES IS NOT ONE WRONG ROW -- FOUR THINGS GO WRONG TOGETHER, AND THREE OF THEM ARE SILENT. (1) T06's r2 floor is evaluated against VERSION 1's metrics, so a candidate the floor would have refused can reach PRODUCTION under a version-1 score that passed, or the reverse. (2) T05's object-existence and checksum check verifies VERSION 1's bytes -- the wrong artifact is proven loadable and the intended one is never checked. (3) If the floor refuses, T06's override writes actorId/actorName/reason/at against a version the operator never looked at: an audit trail that points at the wrong row is worse than none, because the reader six months later believes it. (4) MODEL-SERVE-006-T12 made Save & Deploy 'promote, then enable the schedule', and the schedule resolves the CURRENT PRODUCTION version -- so every hourly window scores with version 1's model while the UI reports the deploy succeeded. That is this ledger's own named failure class: a plausible answer with nothing to alert on.

CHECK THE SECOND CALLER IN THE SAME PASS, BECAUSE IT IS NEW AND UNAUDITED. T06's client_2026_09_14 note added hooks/model/use-model-promote.ts plus a Promote control and override dialog on the Model Detail header -- the first UI that can promote a model that already has history, and therefore the one that MUST pass a real version number. Read whether it resolves the version from the row it renders or carries any literal of its own. Two promote callers with one correct and one hardcoded is the drift this task should close, not half of it.

FIX BY MAKING THE WRONG CALL UNWRITEABLE, NOT BY GUARDING IT -- this codebase reaches for that shape repeatedly and for the same reason. Preferred: give promote a nominal parameter type (a ModelVersionNumber or the version row's own id) so a bare literal 1 fails tsc. Second best: pass the version the flow actually created -- Save Model's own transaction knows it, since T03 creates the row there. Only if neither is reachable: refuse loudly when the model holds more than one version, with the reason named, which converts a silent wrong promote into a stated refusal. A guard is the weakest of the three because it is a check someone can delete; a type is not.

THE TRIGGER TO WATCH, recorded so this is not rediscovered from a bug report: MODEL-SERVE-004's own implementation note says the client side is still simulated -- 'apps/client/lib/retrain.ts's 700ms setTimeout simulation and use-model-retrain.ts stay exactly as they are', with that file's 'no training infra yet' comment already flagged as the only stale thing left. The day retrain is wired to the real endpoint, a model with versions 1 and 2 becomes reachable from the client, and any promote call carrying a literal starts pointing at the wrong one.

NOT IN SCOPE: the create-mode gate itself, which is correct as it stands and is MODEL-SERVE-006-T12's to change if it ever should. This task removes the dependency on that gate, it does not touch it.
tasks.result_2026_09_14: COMPLETED 2026-09-14. PREMISE VERIFIED FIRST, PER THIS TASK'S OWN INSTRUCTION: promote is create-mode-gated at phase-6-deploy.tsx (`if (mode !== 'edit')`) and the ONLY other client caller, models/[id]/page.tsx:348 (client-side, unshifted line numbers), already passes versionSchema.version -- it was never the second hardcoded caller this task worried about. FIX: promote's `version` parameter is now a branded ModelVersionNumber (lib/model-version-number.ts, same shape as lib/preprocessing.ts's BoundedSample) threaded through modelVersionService.promote -> useModelPromote -> both call sites, so a bare literal fails tsc at the call site (verified: temporarily restoring promote(modelId, 1) in phase-6-deploy.tsx produces TS2345, reverted). Honest about the limit: brandModelVersionNumber(1) still compiles -- this closes 'a bare literal typechecks', not 'a wrong number is impossible'. Chose 'A' over re-fetching input-schema after save (recorded as the discriminating constraint): input-schema resolves featureColumns via an object read that can itself fail, and using it to source the promote version would give Save & Deploy a NEW failure mode unrelated to deployment. Instead: model-draft.authorized.service.ts's save transaction now returns the version row it just created (`{ id, version }`) alongside the Model; useModelCommit returns `{ modelId, version }`; a new mpCreatedModelVersionAtom holds it beside mpCreatedModelIdAtom specifically so the `if (createdModelId) return createdModelId` short-circuit (a second Save & Deploy click within one wizard visit) still has a real version to hand back instead of silently degrading to null. Tests: 7 pre-existing use-model-promote cases updated to mint a branded value (baseline-verified passing before this change); one new phase-6-deploy.tsx case clicks Save & Deploy and asserts promote is called with the version commit() returned, not a literal; model-draft spec gained one assertion that the save response carries modelVersion. 110 backend + 18 relevant client tests passing; tsc/eslint clean on every touched file (pre-existing unrelated failures elsewhere confirmed via git status -- untouched by this pass).

tasks.title: The deploy-status KPI shows a state with no reason, and neither page refetches after the action that changes it
tasks.detail:
FILED AT THE USER'S REQUEST 2026-09-14, FROM A REAL DEBUGGING SESSION THAT COST HOURS. TM2 read `initializing` while 46 windows sat PENDING and 2 had already FAILED; the KPI card showed the word and nothing else, so the only way to learn WHY was to query Postgres by hand. The reason existed the whole time -- InferenceWindow.failureReason carried the python message, written by the scheduler and truncated at 2000 chars -- and no surface displayed it.

PLACEMENT RECORDED RATHER THAN LEFT ODD: this task's subject is MODEL-SERVE-006's (deployStatus is T12's, classifyDeployStatus lives in lib/deploy-status.ts, failureReason is T01's column), not MODEL-SERVE-001's. It is filed here because 006 reads completed/100 and this would reopen it. A reader looking for the deploy-status read side should expect to find it there and will not; this sentence is the pointer.

PART 1 -- THE KPI CARD MUST SHOW WHY, NOT ONLY WHAT. classifyDeployStatus returns stopped/initializing/running/error and the card renders that word alone. Two of those four states are unreadable without their reason: `error` says failures happened and not what failed, and `initializing` -- deliberately distinct from error, meaning enabled-but-zero-successes -- is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A BROKEN SOURCE for as long as it takes three terminal windows to accumulate. That is the state that cost this session. Surface the latest terminal window's failureReason beside the status, with its windowStart, so a reader sees which window and when rather than a bare sentence. An `initializing` model that already has FAILED windows must say so -- that is the case the current design hides best.

DO NOT INVENT A SECOND STATE MACHINE FOR THIS. classifyDeployStatus is the ONE decider (T12's own rule, shared by getStatusService and the batched deriveDeployStatuses); this part adds a REASON beside its verdict and must not add a branch that could disagree with it. A card that reads `running` while displaying a failure reason, or `error` with none, is two sources of truth for one fact.

CHECK THE WHOLE PATH FROM SOURCE BEFORE WRITING ANY UI -- this is the actual first step and it may be most of the work. failureReason is a column; whether it reaches the client is a separate question this ledger has already answered wrong twice in one week. TagColumnStats never declared median/std, so FastAPI silently stripped both from every response while three downstream layers assumed they arrived -- the drift signal's own denominator, invisible until it was measured live. And three bare `catch {}` blocks printed a guessed toast in place of eight distinct server refusals, which is the defect that produced the misleading message this session chased. Walk column -> Prisma select -> service shape -> DTO -> response -> component, per hop. A value that is correct in Postgres and absent from the response is the same outcome as no value at all.

NEVER PUT A RAW REASON ON SCREEN WITHOUT READING IT FIRST. failureReason is python's own message and MODEL-FLOW-000-T06's rule -- no presigned URL reaches a log or a client -- applies to any field that travels to the browser. Confirm what the connector actually writes into it (hostnames and auth detail are plausible; a presigned URL must not be) and bound what is rendered. 2000 chars is a storage cap, not a display budget.

PART 2 -- REFETCH AFTER THE ACTION THAT CHANGES THE STATUS. Pressing Run enables the schedule; the status is DERIVED from windows, so the card is stale the instant the mutation returns and stays stale until something else refetches. Refetch after the schedule mutation resolves on models/[id]. TWO THINGS TO GET RIGHT RATHER THAN ASSUME: (a) a schedule that has just been enabled has NO windows yet, so the refetched value is `initializing` BY CONSTRUCTION -- one immediate refetch proves the mutation landed and reveals nothing about whether the source works, and treating that first value as an answer is how this session started; (b) whether a follow-up read is wanted at all is a decision, not a default -- a poll that runs until a window turns terminal is the honest shape, and at INFERENCE_TICK_INTERVAL_MS=300000 the first terminal window is five minutes away, so anything shorter than that interval is load with no information in it. Decide it explicitly and say which was chosen.

PART 3 -- models/views REFETCHES TOO. That list reads deployStatus through the batched deriveDeployStatuses, so it goes stale for exactly the same reason and by the same mechanism. Its Start/Stop toggle already calls PUT /inference/schedule (T12 rewired it); this adds the refetch that toggle never got. Use the list's own existing refresh path -- refreshModels/onUpdated are already the seam the removed mock-retrain transitions used -- rather than a second mechanism, or the two pages will disagree about the same model, which is what makes a status untrustworthy in the first place. The list's per-model figure is BATCHED, so refetch the list rather than one row.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated so scope does not creep: it does not change classifyDeployStatus, does not touch the scheduler or its cadence, does not alter the connector's own error text (a separate pre-existing defect, already tracked -- a per-tag connection failure is skipped and reported as an empty frame, which reads as 'the source had no data' and points a reader the opposite way), and does not revisit INFERENCE_BACKFILL_HORIZON_HOURS. It makes the state and its reason legible, and makes both pages current after the action that changes them.
tasks.result_2026_09_14: COMPLETED 2026-09-14. TWO OF THIS TASK'S OWN PREMISES DID NOT SURVIVE VERIFICATION -- recorded rather than implemented around, per this ledger's own rule. (1) Part 3's claim that models/views' Start/Stop toggle 'never got' a refetch is FALSE: models/views/page.tsx:159-160 already calls refreshModels() AND await refetch() after putSchedule -- already correct, T12's own work, nothing to add. (2) The 'initializing model with FAILED windows' case Part 1 names as 'the state that cost this session' is UNREACHABLE since T12: classifyDeployStatus's 'initializing' branch requires !hasEverSucceeded AND !hasFailedWindows (lib/deploy-status.ts:44-51) -- a never-succeeded model's terminal windows are by definition all FAILED, so hasFailedWindows is true and the branch returns 'error', never 'initializing'. Already pinned by an existing assertion (lib/deploy-status.spec.ts:75-86, 'is error when a NEVER-SUCCEEDED schedule has already failed a window') -- no new test needed. Part 1's 'initializing' card branch therefore renders the honest-absence line ('no windows yet'), never a failure reason. SECURITY FINDING ACTED ON: InferenceWindow.failureReason has a third writer class beyond scheduler/python-relayed text -- the infer container's own terminal report (InferenceWindowCompleteSchema, completeService) stores images/trainer/app/train.py's `str(err)` VERBATIM, unlike python's own routers/preprocess.py `_run`, which maps unexpected exceptions to a generic 502 specifically so driver/credential text cannot reach a client. A container HTTP error against a presigned object URL would render its query string (X-Amz-Signature etc) -- the class MODEL-FLOW-000-T06 forbids. FIXED: new lib/redact-urls.ts strips any http(s) URL from a reason at the READ boundary (getStatusService) only -- the stored row stays full evidence for server logs. IMPLEMENTED: getStatusService now returns lastFailure/lastSkipped as TWO separate fields (never one 'latest reason', since failureReason is set on FAILED *and* SKIPPED and a SKIPPED reason is a threshold message, not a fault -- collapsing them would print a threshold message on a running/stopped card as though it were an error). models/[id]/page.tsx: new use-inference-status.ts hook (first client consumer of GET .../inference/status) supplies deployKey AND the reason, replacing the model.data?.deployStatus-only read; the Deploy KPI card now shows the FAILED reason + windowStart under 'error', the honest 'no windows yet' line under 'initializing', and a visually distinct (never error-styled) SKIPPED note. DELETED the optimistic `setModel(...deployStatus: next)` in handleToggleDeploy -- it asserted 'running' where the classifier would say 'initializing', a second source of truth disagreeing with the first; replaced with refresh() + refetchInferenceStatus() (refreshModels() kept, for the sidebar/Alerts/views consumers of useAllModels). DECISION, RECORDED PER THIS TASK'S OWN INSTRUCTION: one refetch after the mutation, no poll -- a freshly enabled schedule has no windows by construction, INFERENCE_TICK_INTERVAL_MS is 5 minutes, so anything shorter is load with no information in it. Start/Stop buttons gated on the status hook having resolved once, so their disabled state doesn't flip under the cursor when the real read lands. NOT TOUCHED: classifyDeployStatus itself, the scheduler, the connector's own error text, INFERENCE_BACKFILL_HORIZON_HOURS -- all explicitly out of scope per this task's own text. POINTER, NOT A STATUS CHANGE: this task's subject (deployStatus/classifyDeployStatus) is MODEL-SERVE-006's; MODEL-SERVE-006's own status is left untouched per this task's own placement note. Tests: redact-urls.spec.ts (4 cases, new), 3 new getStatusService cases (FAILED reason redacted and surfaced, both null, SKIPPED never populates lastFailure), 3 new use-inference-status.test.tsx cases (null modelId, resolves on mount, refetch bypasses cache). 110 backend + client suites passing; tsc/eslint clean on every touched file.

tasks.title: Two tabs read a stream the schedule never writes, and the container logs the schedule DOES write have no reader at all
tasks.detail:
FILED AT THE USER'S REQUEST 2026-09-14, AFTER TM2 WAS CONNECTED TO A REAL SOURCE AND THREE SURFACES STAYED EMPTY. The request reads as one bug ('the data does not show'). IT IS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS and they must not be built as one, because the first is a WORDING defect and the second is a MISSING FEATURE -- and confusing them is how someone ends up fabricating a value to fill a tab that is correctly empty.

PLACEMENT, SAME POINTER AS T09: this belongs to MODEL-SERVE-006 (InferenceWindowLog is T01's, the container's /log callback is T03's, deployStatus is T12's). It is filed here because 006 reads completed/100. A reader looking for the inference read side should expect it there and will not find it.

PART A -- THE TWO EMPTY TABS ARE CORRECTLY EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Read from this ledger's own record before writing any UI. Input Data reads `points[].features` from PredictionLog (MODEL-SERVE-005-T01's own result: 'the most recent logged request's real tag/value pairs'). PredictionLog is written by apps/serving's /predict path ONLY -- 'apps/serving samples per-REQUEST (SERVING_LOG_SAMPLE_RATE)'. Monitoring's Live Predictions section reads the same stream. SCHEDULED INFERENCE DOES NOT WRITE THERE: a window writes predictions.parquet + metrics.json under inference/{modelId}/{modelVersionId}/dt=/hour=/ (T06) and its row to InferenceWindow. The two paths were kept separate DELIBERATELY, per decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference -- a schedule needs no serving process at all. So a model that has only ever been scheduled, never called synchronously, has an empty PredictionLog BY CONSTRUCTION. TM2 is exactly that model.

WHAT PART A ACTUALLY FIXES IS THE SENTENCE, NOT THE DATA. Both tabs must state WHICH stream they read and why it is empty for this model -- 'no synchronous /predict traffic has been logged for this model; scheduled windows write to the monitoring record instead' -- and point at the surface that DOES have data. DriftPanel's own no-PRODUCTION-version empty state is the precedent this codebase already set for the same class of absence. DO NOT make either tab read InferenceWindow to fill itself: Input Data shows a REQUEST's raw feature values and a window's input.parquet is a different artifact with a different shape and a different meaning; merging them would make one tab claim two provenances. If a window-input view is wanted, that is its own task.

CHECK ONE THING BEFORE ACCEPTING PART A's PREMISE: whether MODEL-SERVE-005-T03's own client work already changed what Monitoring reads. That task wired the Actual-vs-Predict and Residual charts to REAL joined pairs via use-live-error.ts, and its result records those charts rendering SPARSELY -- one point per lab measurement. So Monitoring today holds a MIX: two sections fed by InferenceWindowTruth (which a schedule does fill, once the lab reports) and two fed by PredictionLog (which it never does). An empty Monitoring tab therefore has at least three distinct causes -- no /predict traffic, no truth joined yet, and no successful window at all -- and each needs its own sentence. A single 'no data yet' across the tab is the defect, not the absence.

PART B -- THE CONTAINER LOG HAS A WRITER, A TABLE, AND NO READER. InferenceWindowLog exists (Pass A, migration 20260910120000) and the container reports through the /log callback behind InferenceWindowTokenGuard, structurally the same path ModelTrainingRunLog already uses for training. This feature's own acceptance criterion states it: 'Per-window logs are readable after the container exits, through the same path training logs already use.' That criterion is NOT met -- nothing in the client reads it. The rows are being written and discarded.

WHAT THE USER ASKED FOR, STATED AS A SPAN RATHER THAN A SCREEN: from the moment Deploy is pressed through to the console output of the container that scored a window. That span crosses FOUR record types and they are not interchangeable -- naming them is most of this task: (1) the schedule's own enable transition (Model.data.deployedAt/deployedBy, stamped by putScheduleService on the OFF->ON edge only, T09); (2) the promote that preceded it, with its own actor and its override reason if the r2 floor was overridden (promotionOverride, T06); (3) the InferenceWindow row per window -- status, windowStart/End, inputRows, missingPct, imageDigest, failureReason; (4) InferenceWindowLog, the container's own stdout. A console that shows only (4) cannot explain a model that never spawned a container, which is TM2's own case for 46 of its windows.

THE TWO PLACEMENTS ASKED FOR ARE ONE READ PATH, NOT TWO. models/[id]'s log tab and models/list's Console button must resolve through the SAME service and the same shape, or the two will disagree about one model -- the exact divergence T09 had to close for deployStatus, one screen over. The list's button is a peek (most recent window, its status, its last lines); the tab is the full range. One endpoint, two renderings.

SIX THINGS TO GET RIGHT, EACH ONE A PLACE THIS LEDGER HAS ALREADY BEEN BITTEN.

(1) REDACT AT THE READ BOUNDARY, AND THE PRECEDENT IS ELEVEN DAYS OLD. T09 found that the infer container's terminal report stores train.py's `str(err)` VERBATIM, so a presigned URL can reach failureReason, and fixed it with lib/redact-urls.ts applied in getStatusService -- read-side only, so server logs keep full evidence. CONTAINER STDOUT IS THE SAME EXPOSURE AND STRICTLY WORSE: a log line is not one field, it is everything the process chose to print, and pipelines/infer.py downloads BOTH the model and the input by presigned URL. Apply the same redaction to every line before it leaves the service. MODEL-FLOW-000-T06's rule is absolute: the URL IS the capability.

(2) A WINDOW WITH NO CONTAINER MUST READ DIFFERENTLY FROM ONE WHOSE CONTAINER SAID NOTHING. PENDING (never dispatched), SKIPPED (deliberately not attempted -- T01 is explicit that this is a real terminal status and not a synonym for FAILED), and FAILED-before-spawn all have zero log lines, and so does a container that ran silently. Four states, one em dash today. This is the same three-facts discipline AC11 and T09 both already apply.

(3) BOUND THE READ, AND DO NOT ASSUME ITS SHAPE. At 24 windows a day with a container each, an unbounded range read is the '76MB where 489KB was needed' problem MODEL-SERVE-003-T03 records. Paginate or cap per window, and state the cap on screen when it truncates.

(4) DO NOT ADD A POLL WITHOUT DECIDING IT. T09 chose one refetch and no poll, with the reason recorded: INFERENCE_TICK_INTERVAL_MS is 5 minutes, so anything faster is load with no information. A console invites a tail, and a tail here would mostly return nothing. If a live tail is wanted while a window is RUNNING, say so and bound it to that status only.

(5) THE DISPATCH ORDER IS NOW NEWEST-FIRST AND A CONSOLE MUST NOT IMPLY OTHERWISE. T02's dispatch_order_2026_09_14 changed the claim to `desc` so live windows beat backfill. A log view ordered by windowStart therefore does NOT match execution order, and a reader watching a backfill drain will see rows appear out of sequence. Order by what the reader is asking about and label it; do not present one ordering as the other.

(6) SCHEDULED AND SYNCHRONOUS ARE TWO PLANES, AND THIS TASK MUST NOT MERGE THEM. Part A's whole finding is that the two tabs read a different stream. A console that silently pools /predict logs and window logs into one feed recreates that confusion in a new place.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not change what apps/serving logs or when, does not make a schedule write PredictionLog (they are separate planes by decision, not by oversight), does not touch the scheduler, the cadence, the connector's error text, or classifyDeployStatus. It makes three surfaces state what they read and why they are empty, and gives the container log its first reader.
tasks.result_2026_09_14:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-14. Built as TWO defects, per the task's own warning, and the audit that preceded it shrank Part A by half and corrected Part B's premise.

PART A WAS ALREADY HALF DONE, AND THE LEDGER SAID TO CHECK. MODEL-SERVE-005-T03's client work landed after T10 was filed, so the per-section audit found: Actual-vs-Predict and Residual already discriminate FIVE causes through the shared `EmptyTruth` component (model-monitoring-tab.tsx:46-82) — transport error, no windows in range, join failed for N windows, scored-but-no-lab-measurement, measurement-outside-tolerance — and Input Data had already been rebuilt to read `schema.featureColumns` as the authoritative X list rather than `points[].features`. Those three were LEFT ALONE. Only two surfaces still had the flat sentence: LivePredictionChart ('No sampled predictions in this range yet.') and DriftPanel's third rung ('No sampled predictions in this range to compare.'). Both now name the stream they read (the synchronous /predict path), state that scheduled inference does not write it, and point at the truth-fed sections that DO have data. DriftPanel's `unavailableReason` rung is untouched — it is the precedent, not the defect. Input Data's traffic strip gained the stream name only; its schema empty states were correct already. Neither reads InferenceWindow to fill itself.

PART B's PREMISE WAS ALSO PARTLY WRONG — THE THIRD SUCH CASE IN THIS LEDGER. The task asserts InferenceWindowLog has 'a writer, a table, and no reader at all'. The backend reader exists and is COMMITTED: `listLogsService` (inference-window.authorized.service.ts) and `GET /inference/windows/:windowId/logs` (controller), already model-scoped, already throwing AppException rather than the NotFoundException the training-run precedent drifted into. What had no reader was the CLIENT. And the two placements the task asks for already existed, both wired to the wrong field: `models/[id]`'s Logs tab and `models/views`' Console row action both rendered `model.data.logs` — a Model.data JSON array initialised [] whose only writer (`appendLogService`) has NO client caller anywhere in apps/client. Both surfaces therefore said 'No logs yet.' for every model, forever, while the container's real output was written to InferenceWindowLog and discarded unread. That is the user's report.

SECURITY: T09's REDACTION WAS INCOMPLETE, AND THIS IS A DEFINITION-OF-DONE VIOLATION. images/trainer/app/train.py's top-level handler passes ONE `str(err)` to TWO sinks — `_api.log(str(err), 'error')` and `_api.report_failure(str(err))`. T09 found that string leaks a presigned URL's X-Amz-Signature and redacted only the `failureReason` sink, in getStatusService. The log sink was left open and `listLogsService` returned `message` raw through a JwtAccessGuard route. infer.py downloads BOTH the model and the input by presigned URL, so `download_verified`'s requests.HTTPError is exactly the exception that produces it. global_definition_of_done item 8 states the rule outright: 'no result bytes and no presigned URLs pass through a log.' FIXED: `redactUrls()` now applies per line AND to the window's failureReason, at the read boundary only, so stored rows keep full evidence for server logs.

THE READ CAP IS TAKEN FROM THE NEWEST END, DELIBERATELY NOT COPYING THE TRAINING PRECEDENT. `model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts` reads logs with `orderBy: asc, take: 500`, which keeps the FIRST 500 lines. Applied here that would have been a REGRESSION — listLogsService had no cap at all, so it went from 'all lines' to 'startup noise, failure dropped', and a FAILED window's failure is at the tail. It also cannot serve the list peek's 'last lines'. Now: `orderBy: desc, take: 501`, reversed in memory for display; the 501st row is the truncation signal and a count query runs ONLY when it fires, so the screen can say 'N earlier lines omitted' truthfully rather than truncating silently.

ONE ENDPOINT, TWO RENDERINGS. The Console peek holds a Model and has no window id, so the route accepts the literal `latest` and resolves it server-side to the model's most recent window. Both surfaces go through one service function (`inferenceWindowService.logs`) and one hook (`useWindowLogs`), so the two screens cannot disagree about one model — the divergence T09 had to close for deployStatus one screen over, not repeated.

THE FOUR ZERO-LINE STATES ARE DERIVED FROM THE CONTAINER'S OWN CODE, NOT GUESSED. infer.py calls api.claim() and then, as its very next action and BEFORE downloading anything, logs 'Window claimed. ...'. So a container that reached claim ALWAYS wrote a line, and 'the container ran and printed nothing' is NOT REACHABLE. Zero lines means no container got that far. lib/window-log-state.ts gives each status its own sentence: PENDING (queued, never dispatched), SKIPPED (a real terminal status — too few rows, deliberately not attempted, never a synonym for FAILED), FAILED (died before the container reported in; failureReason is the only evidence), RUNNING (spawned, pre-claim). A SUCCEEDED window with no lines is flagged as suspect rather than given a reassuring sentence, because it should not occur.

DECISIONS RECORDED. (1) NO POLL — the user chose it explicitly and it matches T09's recorded reasoning: INFERENCE_TICK_INTERVAL_MS is 5 minutes, so a tail mostly returns nothing. Not even the RUNNING-bounded tail the task would have permitted. One fetch plus a refetch on the action that changes state. (2) ORDERING IS LABELLED — T02's dispatch_order_2026_09_14 made the claim `desc`, so windowStart order is NOT execution order; the window list says 'Newest window time first — not execution order' on screen. (3) TWO PLANES STAY TWO — nothing pools /predict logs into the window feed.

model.data.logs IS NOW ORPHANED, BY DECISION. The user chose 'replace entirely': both surfaces repoint, and `appendLogService` plus its route and the `logs` key on ModelData are LEFT IN PLACE (removing them widens scope past T10 and touches a JSON shape `normalizeData` guarantees). It now has no reader and its only writer has no caller. Recorded here so the next reader does not mistake it for live state. The Logs tab's count badge went with it: it read `model.data.logs.length`, which is 0 for every model, so it never rendered, and a real count would mean fetching every window's lines to label a tab.

VERIFIED: 16 new backend Jest cases (redaction of both sinks, newest-500 + truthful omitted-count, no false truncation at exactly the cap, `latest` resolution and its distinct 404, model-scoping of an explicit id, viewer refused before any log row is read, tokenHash absent from the select, and all four zero-line states) — confirmed collected, not merely present: 42 passed in the file, of which 16 match -t 'MODEL-SERVE-001-T10'. Client: 9 cases on lib/window-log-state.ts, 7 on the two Part A empty states (asserting the DISTINGUISHING sentence, and that DriftPanel's unavailableReason rung does not stack with the traffic sentence), 5 on useWindowLogs (chiefly: `error` is NOT set for a window that simply has no lines). All pass. Lint clean on every touched file; backend and client type-check clean on every touched file. NOT VERIFIED AGAINST A LIVE TM2 — no browser pass was run in this session, so the end-to-end check against the model that produced the report is still outstanding.

CORRECTED BEFORE CLOSING, TWICE, AND BOTH CORRECTIONS CAME FROM ACTUALLY LOOKING.

(A) THE 'model.data.logs IS NOW ORPHANED' CLAIM ABOVE WAS WRONG. It has a LIVE READER: apps/client/lib/alerts.ts filters `model.data.logs` for level==='error' and attaches the last three to every failed-deploy alert row, reaching the Alerts page through buildAlerts -> hooks/alerts/use-alerts.ts. The accurate statement is the reverse of orphaned: the field has a READER and no WRITER, so those alert rows have always shown an empty error list. Deleting the field — the option offered and declined — would have broken the Alerts page, not tidied dead code. Left in place, now for a second and better reason than 'out of scope'.

(B) TWO UI DEFECTS CAUGHT BY VERIFYING AGAINST TM2 IN LIVE POSTGRES, NOT BY TESTS. Querying the real row set (model 3991c43f-59b7-4a99-924f-98a2ec30651a) returned: PredictionLog rows = 0 (Part A's premise, confirmed against the database rather than inferred from the ledger); model.data.logs length = 0 (both Console placements were rendering an empty array, confirmed); 51 windows — 50 FAILED, 1 SKIPPED — and InferenceWindowLog rows = 0 across ALL of them. Then the finding that changed the code: of those 50 FAILED windows, 20 have BOTH a `containerId` and a `startedAt` while `imageDigest` is STILL NULL, with failureReason 'Container <id> no longer exists — the server restarted while this window was in flight.' Two consequences, both fixed: (1) the FAILED empty-state title read 'Failed before the container started', which is flatly wrong for those 20 — a container DID start, it was reaped before reaching claim. FAILED is now split on `containerId` into 'Failed before a container started' (30 windows) and 'Container started but never reported in' (20). (2) the tab header labelled the window `imageDigest ?? 'no container'`, which would have told an operator 'no container' about all 20 of them. `containerId` is the real ran/did-not-run discriminator and is now selected, returned, and used; imageDigest is shown only when actually present. The schema comment 'imageDigest ... Null until a container is spawned' reads like the opposite is true, which is how the mistake was made — note it before trusting that field again.

B3 (1) AND (2) ARE NOW IMPLEMENTED, NOT DEFERRED. An earlier draft of this result omitted them. The response carries a `provenance` object: the schedule's OFF->ON stamp (Model.data.deployedAt/deployedBy), and the promote behind the window's pinned version (version, stage, promotedAt, promoter name, and the r2-floor override reason when one exists, redacted). All fields are nullable and read best-effort — a deleted promoter or a pre-stamp model must never fail the log read. That is what makes the view answer the span the user actually asked for, 'from the moment Deploy is pressed', rather than only the container's own output.

FINAL VERIFICATION STATE. Backend: 49 cases pass in the service spec, 23 of them matching -t 'MODEL-SERVE-001-T10' (confirmed by case count, not by the file being present). Client: 27 cases pass across the four relevant files. Lint and type-check clean on every touched file in both apps; the pre-existing failures elsewhere in the tree (12 client suites, 21 backend spec lint errors below line 798) were confirmed to predate this work and were not touched. DATABASE-LEVEL verification against TM2 done, as recorded above, and it is what found the two defects. NO BROWSER PASS WAS RUN: the rendered Logs tab and Console peek have not been opened against a live session. On TM2 specifically a browser pass would exercise only the zero-line paths, since every one of its 51 windows has zero log lines — the line-rendering, truncation and per-line redaction paths have unit coverage but no live render behind them yet.

LIVE CONTAINER VERIFICATION 2026-09-14, WHICH CLOSES THE OUTSTANDING ITEM. The blocker was never the r2 floor — TM2 was already PRODUCTION (promoted with an override, reason 'For testing') with an enabled 60m schedule and a working source. It was INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS: every TM2 window yielded 20 usable rows against a floor of 30, so dispatchOne marked each SKIPPED BEFORE reaching runner.spawn(), which is why zero containers and zero log lines existed. With INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS=10 set temporarily in the root .env (since restored) and the backend restarted, window 60cb652a (2026-09-14T07:00Z) was reset from SKIPPED to PENDING with a live tokenExpiresAt — dispatch re-mints tokenHash at spawn but NOT tokenExpiresAt, and the SKIPPED path had set it to epoch, so resetting status alone would have produced a container whose every callback 401'd.

RESULT: the scheduler claimed it, re-materialized 30 usable rows (more data had arrived, so it would in fact have cleared the real floor of 30 unaided), spawned container 3659cc259e4b from scgc/soft-sensor-trainer:1.0.11, and the window reached SUCCEEDED with predictionsKey written. THE imageDigest FINDING IS STRONGER THAN FIRST RECORDED, AND IT IS NOT LIMITED TO REAPED CONTAINERS. 'no container'` label it would have reported 'no container' on a fully successful scored window. containerId is the only trustworthy signal; see the standalone finding.
