tasks.title: Every window reads SKIPPED for the same unexplained reason, and the lag it may be caused by was never measured
tasks.detail:
FILED AT THE USER'S REQUEST 2026-09-14, FROM THE FIRST SUCCESSFUL PI FETCH THIS PROJECT HAS SEEN. TM2's windows now read 'Skipped — too few rows to score. Only 20 usable row(s), below INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS (30).' That message is a milestone rather than a defect report: it proves the historian is reachable, the fetch returned rows, and the scheduler declined to score deliberately. Both facts matter and neither was true before.

PLACEMENT, SAME POINTER AS T09 AND T10: the subject is MODEL-SERVE-006's (INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS gates dispatch, lagMinutes is T04's, missingPct is T05's, SKIPPED is T01's terminal status). Filed here because 006 reads completed/100. A reader looking for the skip threshold should expect it there and will not find it.

THE FRAMING TO REFUSE: 'should we show the data or leave it'. Both options accept 20-of-60 as a given. It is not — it has THREE causes with three different fixes, and the message cannot tell them apart. Answer the cause first; the display question is downstream of it and smaller than it looks.

STEP 1, READ TWO FIELDS THAT ARE ALREADY ON THE ROW. T05 records inputRows and missingPct per window precisely so a wandering series can be told apart from a sensor that stopped. Read them for a SKIPPED window before touching anything. (a) missingPct HIGH -> rows are being dropped for incompleteness: drop_bad_feature_rows discards a row when ANY kept tag's own status is not Good, and at 21 feature columns a single sparse tag can take most of the window with it. (b) missingPct LOW and inputRows still ~20 -> the source simply did not return 60 rows, and the threshold is what is wrong, not the data. (c) A LAG-SHAPED signature -- rows present early in the window and absent toward its end -- points at windowEnd = now() - lagMinutes closing before the slowest tag has arrived, which recurs EVERY window rather than occasionally. These are distinguishable from data already in hand; do not infer the cause from the row count alone.

STEP 2, RUN V08. IT HAS BEEN PENDING FOUR DAYS FOR A REASON THAT NO LONGER HOLDS. T04's own text says to MEASURE worst-case tag arrival before choosing a lag; V08 exists because that measurement could not be taken -- 'the PI Web API (scgc-piwebapi.scg.com) is not reachable from the development machine, so lagMinutes was set to a deliberate 15 at a 60-minute cadence with the user's agreement, recorded as a decision rather than presented as a measurement.' The skip message is the evidence that PI is now reachable, so the blocker is gone and V08 is runnable for the first time. Measure the real worst-case arrival across the pinned run's own feature tags and revise the per-schedule value from the number. A lag that stays at its default because nobody measured is the failure T04's own wording forbids, one step removed -- and it is now removable.

STEP 3, ESTABLISH WHERE INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS = 30 CAME FROM. If it has no measurement behind it, it is a guess refusing real windows every hour -- the 'guess wearing a formula' MODEL-FLOW-020's own finding 3 names, and the same class as the capacity thresholds MODEL-FLOW-020-T03 measured and could not support. Check for its origin before adjusting it.

FIX THE LAG BEFORE THE THRESHOLD, AND DO NOT LOWER THE THRESHOLD TO MAKE THE DASHBOARD GREEN. If the cause is (c), a longer lag yields a MORE COMPLETE window at no cost to data quality -- which is exactly the freshness-versus-completeness trade T04 says must be made deliberately, and it is made at the lag, not at the floor. Lowering the floor instead buys a green status with a score computed over a third of an hour, and whether 20 rows represent an hour of this process is an engineering judgment about the plant, not a UI problem. If the cause is (b) -- the tags genuinely publish at 5-minute cadence, so 12 rows is a complete hour -- then 30 is wrong for this plant and should change, with the measured cadence recorded beside it the way MODEL-SERVE-006-T04 records lagMinutes as chosen rather than measured.

DO NOT SCORE 20 ROWS AND FLAG THE RESULT LOW-CONFIDENCE. That publishes a number into the monitoring record and moves the judgment onto a caveat beside it. This ledger has recorded that shape three times already -- unpersisted scaler params producing plausible wrong predictions, a Bad cell's 0.0 reading as a real measurement, mark-Bad on an operating window fabricating normal flow during a shutdown. A refusal that states its reason is better than a figure that needs one.

WHAT TO DISPLAY, AND WHY IT IS NOT THE WHOLE FIX. SKIPPED is a real terminal status, not a synonym for FAILED -- T01 says so explicitly and T10 requires that SKIPPED neither raises nor suppresses the staleness alarm, because a quiet plant is legitimate. So the state is correct and must not be reclassified. What is missing is that 20-of-60 has three causes and the message names none of them: surface the window's own missingPct and its windowStart/windowEnd beside the skip reason, both already on the row, so a reader can tell an incomplete fetch from a sparse-by-design tag without opening Postgres. This extends T09's card work rather than duplicating it.

MONITORING NEEDS A FOURTH CAUSE, AND T10's V08 UNDERSTATES IT. That item enumerates three reasons the Monitoring tab can be empty (no /predict traffic, no truth joined yet, no SUCCEEDED window at all). 'Every window was SKIPPED because the data did not meet the threshold' is a fourth and reads differently from all three: it says the system ran, fetched, and decided -- not that it never ran. A SKIPPED window also writes no predictions.parquet, so the tab is empty for a reason that looks identical to failure and is not.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not change SKIPPED's own semantics or its relationship to the alarm, does not touch drop_bad_feature_rows (a correctness guard -- a row with a hole must not be scored), does not alter the connector's error text, and does not revisit INFERENCE_BACKFILL_HORIZON_HOURS. It answers why the windows are short, fixes that, and makes the skip legible where it is read.

RESOLVED 2026-09-14. THE CAUSE WAS NONE OF THE THREE NAMED HERE — IT WAS SHARPER, AND A ONE-LINE CONTRACT VIOLATION. MEASURED FIRST, per this task's own step 1: 24 real InferenceWindow rows read live from Postgres. missingPct = 0 on EVERY row (kills cause a). 20 fully-elapsed windows (backfilled 09-12/09-13, materialized 09-14 once PI became reachable) returned exactly 60/60 rows at the schedule's 1-minute interval (kills cause b — the historian does publish a complete hour). The 4 LIVE windows read 19, 19, 20, 30 rows, tracking elapsed minutes into their own span almost exactly (19 rows at 18m57s elapsed, 30 rows at 29m34s). The window was being read WHILE IT WAS STILL HAPPENING.

ROOT CAUSE: schema.prisma's own doc comment on InferenceSchedule.lagMinutes states the contract as "windowEnd = now() - lag". inference-window-scheduler.service.ts's insertDueWindows implemented it against windowSTART instead: `to = now - lag`. At cadence 60 / lag 15, window [H:00,H+1:00) became due at H:15 and was materialized ~H:18 — 19 minutes into its own 60-minute span, whose end was still 42 minutes in the FUTURE. Python passed that future windowEnd straight to PI as endTime (visible verbatim in a live FAILED window's own NameResolutionError text, which still showed the future range). The code was off by exactly one cadence from its own documented contract.

FIX: `to = now - (lagMinutes + cadenceMinutes) * 60_000` — one line, inference-window-scheduler.service.ts's insertDueWindows. backfillService (user-supplied range) deliberately left untouched — gating it on elapsed-ness would break intentional recent-range backfills. INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS itself was NOT touched: by this task's own branch logic the cause was never (b) for this schedule (30 is correct at a measured 1-minute interval), and the timing fix is what makes 30 reachable again.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, ACTUALLY RUN, NOT ASSERTED: the new dispatch-timing test (inference-window-scheduler.service.spec.ts) was run against the pre-fix formula by temporarily reverting the one line, confirmed FAILING (expected 09:00:00.000Z, received 10:00:00.000Z — the exact pre-fix bug reproduced under a fixed clock), then the fix was restored and the full 14-case suite reconfirmed green.

STALENESS COMPANION, FOUND BEFORE SHIPPING, NOT AFTER. The fix moves every window's completion one cadence later. Staleness (T10) is computed as `now - lastSucceeded.windowStart > STALE_AFTER_CADENCES * cadence`, duplicated inline in TWO places (lib/deploy-status.ts's deriveDeployStatuses and inference-window.authorized.service.ts's getStatusService). Unchanged, headroom at cadence=60/lag=15 falls from 102min to 45min, and classifyDeployStatus would read a merely-slow-but-healthy model as 'error'. Extracted a shared isStale(lastWindowStart, cadenceMinutes, lagMinutes) into lib/deploy-status.ts, called from both sites — the file's own doc comment already states classifyDeployStatus is shared for exactly this reason; the staleness INPUT was the one thing still duplicated. Boundary: processable at windowStart+cadence+lag, STALE_AFTER_CADENCES counted from there, not from windowStart — which makes the EFFECTIVE headroom wider (120min from the processable point, 255min from windowStart) than before, not narrower; asserted as isStale's own exact boundary in deploy-status.spec.ts, not as a before/after headroom comparison. Two neighbours checked and found NOT to need a change: gapCount (counts non-terminal windows) gains a standing +1 during the now-longer PENDING lifetime, but has zero client consumers (grep-verified: only the type declaration and one unused test fixture field); reconcileStuckWindows keys on startedAt, never createdAt, so the longer PENDING lifetime cannot trip INFERENCE_WINDOW_STUCK_MS.

SKIP LEGIBILITY (V11's real gap, see V11 below): model-log-sheet.tsx (the Console peek) was extended with the same windowEnd/inputRows/missingPct strip window-logs-tab.tsx already had — one vocabulary, not two.

MONITORING'S FOURTH EMPTY CAUSE: getTruthService's `windowsInRange` counts status:'SUCCEEDED' only, so a range where every window was SKIPPED read identically to "the scheduler never ran here" (T10-V08's three enumerated causes). Added a second, independent `windowsSkipped` count (same range, status:'SKIPPED') to the coverage payload and to the client LiveErrorCoverage type; EmptyTruth (model-monitoring-tab.tsx, now exported for direct testing — no other consumer) gained a branch checked BEFORE the bare windowsInRange===0 case, naming "N windows were skipped... the system ran and declined, rather than failed."

TWO FACTS RECORDED, NOT FIXED, BOTH FILED SEPARATELY (see this feature's new findings and T14 below): (1) INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS=10 was found live in the running backend PROCESS environment, present in NO file (not .env, not .env.example, not any shell rc file) — set inline in the shell that launched `pnpm dev`. It brackets exactly the 06:00 window SKIPping at threshold 30 and the 07:00 window SUCCEEDing after it, meaning two windows (19 and 19 rows) were scored and published over roughly a third of an hour, recorded nowhere as a deviation, and will silently revert to 30 on the next clean-shell restart. This is a fact about the running dev environment, not a code defect — the user was asked and owns unsetting it. (2) INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS is a single global constant whose derivation comment assumes a 1-minute sampling interval, while each InferenceSchedule carries its own fetchConfig.intervalTime — real for a schedule at a coarser cadence, but NOT this task's cause (this schedule IS 1-minute, measured), so implementing per-schedule derivation here would be the unrelated refactor CLAUDE.md §3 forbids. Filed as MODEL-SERVE-001-T14.

TESTS: backend — inference-window-scheduler.service.spec.ts (+1 case, the negative-control dispatch-timing test, 14/14 green), deploy-status.spec.ts (+4 isStale boundary cases, 20/20 green, plus 3 pre-existing deriveDeployStatuses schedule fixtures corrected to carry lagMinutes so they exercise real staleness math rather than accidental NaN-comparison pass-through), inference-window.authorized.service.spec.ts (+1 windowsSkipped case, buildTruthPrisma helper extended to key its `count` mock by where.status — it was returning one value for two now-distinct calls — 50/50 green). Client — window-logs-tab.test.tsx (new, 7 cases: 4 zero-line-state reasons + 2 V11 cases + 1 V10 cross-surface case), model-log-sheet.test.tsx (new, 3 cases), empty-states.test.tsx (+4 cases for the fourth empty cause, 11/11 green, 7 pre-existing untouched).

MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: full backend suite 686/695 passing, 9 pre-existing failures (Nest DI wiring in nodes/workspace-plant/plan.admin/auth.admin/model-run/workspace.authorized CONTROLLER specs, plus auth.public.service — none of these files appear in this task's diff, cross-checked via `git diff --stat`) — zero regressions. Backend check-types: 5 pre-existing errors, same 4 files (auth admin/authorized/public specs, dataset-draft spec) this ledger has already recorded once before under T12 — unchanged. Backend lint: every flagged file is a .spec.ts already carrying the SAME `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-*` Jest-mock-typing class before this task touched it (confirmed: the pre-existing first test in inference-window-scheduler.service.spec.ts already triggered it before any edit here), plus one unrelated file (loader-sink.interface.ts); zero errors on any of the three actual SOURCE files this task touched. Client vitest: 1251/1278 passing pre-existing baseline, 12 failing files all in unrelated areas (data-studio, models/create pipeline, plants dashboard, settings/plans, canvas, useAtom store) — none in this task's diff. Client check-types: 7 pre-existing errors, unrelated files (dataset-compare-modal.tsx, three lib test files missing an unrelated `editHistory` fixture field) — unchanged.

LIVE, PARTIAL, STATED HONESTLY RATHER THAN CLAIMED COMPLETE: the compiled dist output (dist/api/v1/inference-window/authorized/inference-window-scheduler.service.js) already contains the fix (`(schedule.lagMinutes + schedule.cadenceMinutes) * 60_000`), read directly to confirm it, and a `node dist/main` backend process was observed started AFTER the source edit was made. What was NOT established: which of several concurrently-running processes actually serves traffic — this dev machine had TWO `nest start --watch` instances and TWO `dist/main` instances alive at once (a live-multi-session fact, not a defect in this fix), so a causal "the watcher hot-reloaded my change" claim would be asserting more than was observed; flagged to the user directly rather than stated as fact here. No NEW live dispatch under the fix has been observed yet within this session: the next window (windowStart 12:00 UTC) is not processable until 13:15 UTC under the corrected formula, which had not yet arrived as of this task's own completion. Also unresolved as of completion: PI DNS (scgc-piwebapi.scg.com) reads NXDOMAIN, so even a dispatch at 13:15 UTC would MATERIALIZE-FAIL rather than prove full end-to-end row completeness — see V12, blocked, below, which is exactly this same gap. The query to re-check once both clear: `SELECT "windowStart","windowEnd","createdAt",status,"inputRows","missingPct" FROM "InferenceWindow" ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC LIMIT 3;` — expect createdAt >= windowEnd + 15min, and inputRows = 60 once PI is reachable again.

tasks.title: The Input Data tab reports a status the frame no longer carries, and an equation feature's own status is the weakest of its sources
tasks.detail:
FILED AT THE USER'S REQUEST 2026-09-14: the Input Data tab's Status column should report each TAG's own Good/Bad status, and an equation feature must read Bad when ANY base tag it is computed from is Bad.

THE SECOND HALF IS ALREADY TRUE UPSTREAM AND MUST NOT BE RE-IMPLEMENTED. feature_service.py's _compute_feature_column reads every source through _good_value, which returns None for a non-Good cell, and writes (0.0, STATUS_BAD) the moment ANY required source value is None -- rolling additionally requires a COMPLETE window of Good values, so there is no partial average wearing a Good status. formula, ratio, arith, log, lag and delta all gate the same way. So the weakest-source rule the user is describing is EXACTLY what the pipeline already computes, per column, at feature-engineering time. This task DISPLAYS that status; it does not derive one client-side. Re-deriving it in the UI would create a second implementation of a rule that already exists, and the two would drift -- the drift DS-LAKE-003 killed for object keys and DS-LAKE-021-T02 avoided for the job poller.

BUT THE STATUS THE TAB WOULD READ HAS BEEN LAUNDERED, AND THIS IS THE BLOCKING FINDING. to_model_ready's own docstring states it: 'toModelReady scales every FINITE value regardless of its ORIGINAL status and always emits Good afterward -- a Bad cell holding a real (non-hole) number is silently laundered to Good by scaling.' A Bad derived cell is stored as 0.0, 0.0 is finite, so scaling forces STATUS_GOOD. DS-LAKE-023-T05's drop_bad_feature_rows now runs immediately BEFORE to_model_ready at all three scaling sites, so a Bad-feature row is REMOVED rather than laundered -- which means a post-scale frame contains no Bad feature cells at all, and a Status column read off it would report Good for every row unconditionally. That is not a rendering bug to style around: THE EVIDENCE IS GONE BY CONSTRUCTION AT THAT STAGE.

SO STEP 1 IS TO ESTABLISH WHICH FRAME THIS TAB READS, AND IT DECIDES WHETHER THE TASK IS SMALL OR IMPOSSIBLE AS WORDED. T10 Part A traced Input Data to PredictionLog's points[].features -- per-REQUEST values written only by apps/serving's /predict path, which a scheduled model never touches (decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference). Read what that payload actually carries: if it records the request's raw tag values with their own status, the status is present and this is a display task. If it records the post-scale model-ready row, every status in it is Good and the tab cannot honestly show anything else. If it carries values with NO status field at all, then a Status column there is currently reporting something else entirely and what it reports must be named before it is replaced.

DO NOT SUBSTITUTE A DIFFERENT FRAME TO MAKE THE COLUMN WORK. If the /predict payload cannot supply per-tag status, the honest outcome is that Input Data states which stream it reads and why status is unavailable there -- T10 Part A's own finding -- and the per-tag Good/Bad view belongs on a surface reading a PRE-SCALE frame. Pointing this tab at a window's input.parquet instead would make one tab claim two provenances, which T10 Part A explicitly refuses ('Input Data shows a REQUEST's raw feature values and a window's input.parquet is a different artifact with a different shape and a different meaning').

THREE STATUS VALUES EXIST, NOT TWO. object_store.py's constants are STATUS_GOOD, STATUS_BAD and Questionable -- boxplot_service's own Good-filter and scatter's ADR both treat Questionable as non-Good, and DS-LAKE-026's chart work found Questionable surviving as numeric where Bad does not. A two-state Good/Bad column silently folds Questionable into one of them; decide which and say so, or render three. Folding it into Good is the more dangerous default because it reports a doubtful reading as sound.

A HOLE READS 0.0 AND MUST NOT RENDER AS A MEASUREMENT. frame_service.MISSING_VALUE is 0.0 with the status in the sibling column, so a Bad cell's VALUE is indistinguishable from a real zero once the status is dropped. DS-LAKE-021's CSV export resolved this exact case by exporting a blank cell rather than 0.0, and its own V01 asserts the blank rather than the zero. Whatever this tab renders for a Bad cell, it must not be the number -- a valve position or a flow legitimately reads near zero, so the reader cannot tell them apart.

WHICH BASE TAGS FAILED IS THE USEFUL PART, AND IT IS DERIVABLE WITHOUT NEW BOOKKEEPING. Knowing Reflux_ratio is Bad is far less actionable than knowing FIC114I is the source that failed -- and at six base tags, joint availability collapses multiplicatively, so one sparse tag can take the whole column down. feature_spec.json records every feature with its config, so the dependency graph is already derivable; the per-source status is in the frame if the frame is pre-scale. Surface the failing SOURCE alongside the derived column's Bad, rather than only the derived column's own verdict.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not change _compute_feature_column's weakest-source rule (already correct), does not touch drop_bad_feature_rows (a correctness guard -- a row with a hole must not be scored), does not alter to_model_ready's laundering (that is load-bearing for training, per DS-LAKE-025-T06 read 6), and does not repoint this tab at a different artifact.

RESOLVED 2026-09-14. STEP 1's blocking investigation was run to completion and T12's OWN premise did not survive it — this is not a display bug in a pre-scale frame, because the frame this tab reads is NOT pre-scale in the sense T12 assumed. Traced end to end, not inferred: POST /predict body.rows (RAW engineering units, caller-supplied) -> serve.py's rows_to_predictions(model, descriptor, body.rows) -> log_prediction(rows=body.rows, scaled=scaled) -> prediction_log.py's body["rows"][i]["features"] = {c: float(rows[i][c]) ...} (logs RAW, never `scaled`) -> prediction-log ingest -> GET /predictions -> points[].features. `scaled` is used ONLY for featureStats aggregates. Three consequences, each verified against live data: (1) no status field exists ANYWHERE on this stream -- LivePredictionPoint.features is Record<string,number>, the ingest DTO is features: z.record(z.string(), z.number()) -- absent because the /predict contract never carried it, not because scaling laundered it away. (2) The column T12 wanted read as data quality is actually a DRIFT verdict (OK/WARN/CRITICAL/UNKNOWN vs training distribution) -- input-feature-table.tsx's old "Status" header let a reader reasonably conflate the two; this is exactly T12's own branch 3 ("what it reports must be named before it is replaced"). (3) Holes cannot occur on this frame at all -- _validate_rows (predict.py) requires every feature column present and numeric before /predict will even respond -- so T12's "a hole reads 0.0" concern and the Questionable-folding question are both moot here, not fixed, because there is nothing to fold.

A LIVE BUG WAS FOUND IN THE SAME TABLE, USER CHOSE TO FIX IT HERE RATHER THAN FILE SEPARATELY. lib/model-input-features.ts called inverseScale(lastValueScaled, scalingParams?.[column]) on a value that was NEVER scaled. Confirmed to hit the CORRUPTED branch, not merely the mislabeled one: the real feature_spec.json for the model owning the two live PredictionLog rows resolves with 22 scalingParams entries (minmax). With FI001.PV{min:179.72,max:206.72}, a real ~190 reading would have rendered as 190x27.0+179.7 ~= 5,309 -- off by ~28x, labelled "engineering units". Fixed: dropped inverseScale entirely, renamed lastValueScaled -> lastValueRaw (it always was raw), removed the now-meaningless (scaled) fallback branch, and corrected the wrong belief in three places it had been written as fact -- apps/serving/services/prediction_log.py (new comment at the exact line that builds body["rows"], naming that `rows` not `scaled` feeds `features`), model-input-schema.authorized.service.ts (resolveScalingParams's old "the tab shows scaled values" claim), and lib/model-input-features.ts's own module doc comment. scalingParams itself stays on the input-schema response -- it is not dead, DS-LAKE-025-T06's lib/inverse-scale.ts still needs it for surfaces reading a genuinely-scaled artifact value; only THIS tab's use of it was wrong.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, ACTUALLY RUN: the retargeted client test ("never scales a logged value") was run against the real pre-fix file (recovered via `git show HEAD:...`, not a hand-reconstruction) and confirmed to FAIL (`expected undefined to be 190.4`, since the field it asserts on did not exist under the old shape) before the fix was restored from a pre-edit backup and the full 7-case suite reconfirmed green. Two green tests that had been directly asserting the bug (`'inverts a scaled value to engineering units...'`, `'falls back to null (not the raw scaled number)...'`) were retargeted rather than "fixed back" to their old assertions -- one is now a straight passthrough case, the other became an equation-attachment case (see below), net test count unchanged (7).

THE USER'S OWN ASK, DELIVERED: "show equation of Tags Equation under the tags in Input Data Tab." feature_spec.json already persists, per feature, {name, kind, config} where config already carries a ready-made human-readable `display` string for a `formula` feature -- and resolveScalingParams already read that exact file, so this needed one MinIO read widened, not a second one. Renamed to resolveFeatureSpec, returns {scalingParams, derivedFeatures}. Live-verified against the real spec (not merely unit-tested): all 3 real formula features on the pinned model extract correctly --
  Spgr_in_feed_Header_1: (AI001A2.PV*FI001.PV)/(FI003.PV+FI001.PV)
  Spgr_in_feed_Header_2: (AI001B2.PV*FI003.PV)/(FI003.PV+FI001.PV)
  Reflux_ratio_per_total_feed_of_Quench_oil_tower: FIC204.PV/(FY107.CPV+(FIC114A.PV+FIC114B.PV+FIC114C.PV+FIC114D.PV+FIC114I.PV+FIC107R.PV)/1000)
-- the third one names FIC114I.PV among its 8 source columns, the exact tag T12's own filed text used as its example. Cross-checked against the real run_manifest.json: featureColumns is 21 entries, exactly 3 carry an equation (these three) and 18 are plain base tags with none -- every derivedFeatures[].name is a member of featureColumns, so the client's name-keyed join has no orphans. Scoped deliberately to kind==='formula' only (all 3 live features are formula; ratio/arith/lag/delta/rolling carry different config keys this read does not attempt to interpret) and named `derivedFeatures`, never `features`, because the same response already carries `featureColumns` (21 strings) and a sibling `features` (a handful of objects) would be conflated with it by a future reader.

STATED PLAINLY, PER T12'S OWN DEMAND THAT THIS NOT BE MISTAKEN FOR SATISFYING THE ASK: the equation tells a reader which SOURCE COLUMNS feed a derived tag. It does NOT answer which one is Bad -- no per-tag status exists anywhere on this stream, traced above. That view needs a DIFFERENT surface reading a pre-scale frame WITH its status columns, filed as T15 below rather than attempted here. One caveat carried forward rather than left implicit: a formula's source can itself be an earlier DERIVED column, not necessarily a base tag (apply_features mutates one frame across configs in order, feature_service.py) -- all three live formulas happen to reference only base tags, but the wording used throughout is "source columns", never "base tags", so a future reader does not build a tag-only assumption on top of this.

CARRIED ONLY WHAT RENDERS: the row gained exactly one new field, `equation: string | null` -- no `sources` array, even though `config.vars` was available. `display` is already the human-readable string built FROM vars; plumbing an unread string[] through three layers (service type, builder, row interface) for a field with no reader was rejected as unnecessary weight. T15 will need `vars` when it exists; it should add it then, not import unused plumbing from here.

TESTS: backend model-input-schema.authorized.service.spec.ts (+3 cases: derivedFeatures for a formula, omission of a non-formula kind, empty when the spec carries no features key -- 13/13 green). Client lib/__tests__/model-input-features.test.ts (7 cases: 5 renamed/param-updated behaviour-preserving, 1 retargeted off the bug with a real negative control, 1 new equation-join case). New app/(default)/models/[id]/components/input-data/__tests__/input-feature-table.test.tsx (5 cases: header reads Drift not Status, a logged value renders untouched with no scaled suffix, an em-dash for never-logged, an equation under a derived name, none for a base tag -- all green). use-model-input-schema.test.tsx's ModelInputSchema fixture updated with the new required field (one real regression this task introduced against its own prior session's work, caught by check-types and fixed in the same pass, not left for a later task).

tasks.title: Establish what the drift z-score is computed against before replacing it with PSI
tasks.detail:
FILED AT THE USER'S REQUEST 2026-09-14: check what the Distribution Drift z-score is computed from, with a view to replacing it with PSI.

AUDIT FIRST, REPLACE SECOND, AND THE AUDIT MAY CHANGE WHAT THE REPLACEMENT SHOULD BE. MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code; a metric swapped on an unverified belief about the old one is the same failure with a different cause. Do not write PSI until every read below is answered.

STEP 1, WHAT IS THE BASELINE? A z-score is (x - mu) / sigma and the whole question is whose mu and sigma. Read the actual computation. Three candidates, with very different consequences: the TRAINING distribution (a real drift signal), the CURRENT WINDOW's own statistics (self-referential -- every window is centred on itself and drift is structurally near-zero), or column_stats.json's sidecar (a snapshot of the committed artifact, which is the training distribution, but of the WHOLE artifact rather than the train split specifically -- and for a holdout-bearing dataset those differ).

STEP 2, WHERE DO THE PARAMETERS COME FROM, AND ARE THEY THE ONES THE MODEL SAW? This system has a precedent that makes the question sharp: DS-LAKE-018-T02 exists because fitted scaler parameters were NOT persisted, and 'scaling the holdout against its OWN statistics is a DIFFERENT transform from the one the model learned, and it fails silently: predictions come out plausible and wrong, not erroneous'. Drift has the identical failure mode. feature_spec.json now records scalingParams (mean/std for standard, min/max for minmax, median/iqr for robust) -- check whether drift reads those, or re-derives its own. If it re-derives, the signal is measuring the wrong reference and the audit has found a real defect independent of PSI.

STEP 3, IS THE DENOMINATOR ALREADY KNOWN BROKEN? A recorded finding in this project's own ledger states that TagColumnStats never declared median/std, so FastAPI SILENTLY STRIPPED both from every response while three downstream layers assumed they arrived -- 'the drift signal's own denominator, invisible until it was measured live'. Establish whether that was fixed, and whether the current z-score has a real sigma or a defaulted one. A z-score with a missing or zero sigma is not a weak metric; it is a number with no meaning, and swapping it for PSI would hide that rather than fix it.

STEP 4, IS THE INPUT SCALED? If drift is computed on the post-to_model_ready frame, every column has been min-max mapped to [0,1] (DS-LAKE-025-T06: scale defaults true, DEFAULT_SCALER is minmax, and an empty scalers dict still scales every column). A z-score over scaled values is scale-invariant so it survives that, but PSI's BIN EDGES do not -- see openDecisions. Also note DS-LAKE-025-T06's own finding that the holdout sidecar stays RAW while the train FINAL is scaled: comparing the two directly is the exact defect that made the compare modal's chart false.

WHAT PSI BUYS, STATED HONESTLY. A z-score compares one moment (the mean) against one spread, so it is blind to a distribution that keeps its mean and changes shape -- bimodality, a widening spread, a shifted mode with a compensating tail. On process data that is a real and common drift mode: a valve cycling between two positions has the same mean as one holding steady between them. PSI compares the whole binned distribution and catches it. That is a genuine gain, not a preference.

WHAT PSI COSTS, WHICH THE REQUEST DOES NOT NAME. (a) It needs BINS, and bin edges must be frozen from the reference distribution at training time -- re-binning per window makes the metric measure the binner, the same contamination DS-LAKE-005B-A-V06's shared-bucket-basis rule exists to prevent for the scrubber. (b) It is undefined when a bin is empty on either side, and the usual fix (add a small epsilon) makes the value depend on that epsilon, so it must be stated rather than hidden in a constant. (c) The industry thresholds (0.1 / 0.25) are conventions from credit scoring, not measurements on process data -- writing them on screen as if measured is the 'guess wearing a formula' this project's own MODEL-FLOW-020 finding 3 names. (d) PSI needs enough samples per bin to be stable, and windows here are already SKIPPING at 20 usable rows against a 30-row floor: 20 rows across 10 bins is 2 per bin and the metric will be noise. That last point may be decisive -- see openDecisions.

DO NOT DELETE THE Z-SCORE IN THE SAME PASS. Publish both until PSI has been seen against real windows, for the same reason T35 keeps a metric's identity on screen beside its verdict: if the two disagree, that disagreement is information about the data, and losing the old signal makes it unreadable. Whichever is retained, the sidecar and the screen must NAME which metric produced the number -- a drift figure whose method is inferred at read time is the pipelineVersion-with-a-default defect DS-LAKE-022-T03 found in its own first shipped form.
tasks.result_2026_09_14:
AUDIT: PredictionLog.featureStats ({n,sum,sumsq,min,max}) carries no distribution shape -- PSI is UNCOMPUTABLE on the existing stream without a schema change (histogram column specced this pass). STEP 1-4 answered by design decision for PSI's OWN new mechanism, NOT verified against the LIVE z-score computation (no repo access this session -- flagged, not glossed): bin edges frozen from the TRAIN split's RAW values at training time, persisted in feature_spec.json.psiReference; sample floor bin_count x 20 before any PSI figure renders; PSI on a SEPARATE rolling-24h cadence from the per-request z-score, both named explicitly on screen. Z-score retained unchanged per this task's own DO-NOT-DELETE rule.

FINDING, RECORDED NOT FIXED: THE Z-SCORE'S OWN BASELINE IS WIDER THAN THE TRAINING DISTRIBUTION. column_stats.json is the sidecar the drift z-score reads (per this task's own STEP 1 candidates), and FINAL's columnStatsKey is inherited from GOLD at adoption -- i.e. computed over the WHOLE committed artifact, not the train split specifically. For any holdout-bearing dataset the baseline therefore includes rows the model never fit on, making the reference measurably wider than the learned distribution. This is dilution, not meaninglessness (contrast STEP 3's missing-sigma case, already resolved -- median/std do arrive): the z-score is systematically LESS sensitive than it could be, always in the direction of under-flagging, never over-flagging, since a wider reference only shrinks a computed z. WHY NOT FIXED: it needs train-split-only stats emitted at TRAINING time, an images/trainer change carrying the identical silent-no-op hazard MODEL-SERVE-006-T03/PASS-A names for this exact image (nothing in CI builds and deploys it; a correct source tree and a stale running image are indistinguishable until a manual rebuild + tag bump), plus a fallback for every existing ModelVersion whose artifact has no narrower sidecar and never will retroactively. PSI's own psiReference has the IDENTICAL exposure -- fix both baselines together in any future pass, never the z-score alone, or the two metrics diverge on this point silently.

DISPLAY SPEC, DECIDED 2026-09-14 WITH THE USER AGAINST A RENDERED EXAMPLE -- RECORDED BECAUSE 'PUBLISH BOTH' IS NOT A DISPLAY DECISION AND THIS TASK'S OWN DO-NOT-DELETE RULE LEAVES IT OPEN. Two metrics in one table is unreadable and actively misleading, for two reasons that are properties of the metrics rather than of the layout: (1) CADENCE -- the z-score is per-request and PSI is rolling-24h, so a shared 'last computed' column reads as a bug on every row; (2) THRESHOLD VOCABULARY -- z's bands are +/-1.5 and +/-3 SD while PSI's are 0.1 and 0.25, and adjacent colour-coded columns assert a comparability that does not exist. REJECTED: adding a PSI column to the existing drift table (the shape first drafted this pass), on both counts above; also REJECTED: a single merged 'drift' figure, which would be one metric wearing another's name -- the pipelineVersion-with-a-default defect DS-LAKE-022-T03 records.

CHOSEN, THREE LEVELS. (1) SUMMARY -- a SEPARATE PSI card beside the existing z-score table, never a column inside it: Tag | PSI | Status | Bins used | Computed over | Last computed, with 'rolling 24h' printed on EVERY row so the cadence is on screen rather than inferred, and the 0.1/0.25 bands labelled as credit-scoring CONVENTIONS pending plant calibration, per cost (c) above. (2) DRILL-DOWN, one tag at a time on click, never all tags at once (20+ histograms is unreadable, which is why a summary level exists): a grouped bar chart of REFERENCE vs CURRENT percentage per frozen bin. Note the property that makes it legible -- quantile bins are equal-frequency by construction, so every reference bar sits at exactly 100/bin_count percent and a reader spots deviation as distance from that flat line, with no shaped baseline to interpret. (3) EDGE TABLE under or beside the chart mapping each bin to its real engineering-unit range plus ref% and cur%. NOT OPTIONAL: bare B1..B10 labels tell a process engineer nothing, and the entire value of PSI over a z-score is knowing WHERE in the range the distribution moved.

INSUFFICIENT DATA IS A FIRST-CLASS RENDER STATE, NOT AN EMPTY CELL. Below the bin_count x 20 floor the summary row reads 'Insufficient data' with the rows it has and the floor it needs, no numeric PSI is printed, and the drill-down does not open. A histogram at 2 samples per bin looks exactly like a real signal and is not one -- cost (d) rendered rather than hidden, the same discipline MODEL-SERVE-005-V02 applies to an RMSE with no joined truth (an em-dash, never 0.00). A degenerate tag's reduced bin_count (per the resolved openDecision) must also be shown in 'Bins used', never assumed to be 10.

WORKED EXAMPLE THE SPEC WAS CONFIRMED AGAINST, kept because it is the case that justifies the whole feature: 10 frozen quantile bins, reference flat at 10% per bin, current 22/18/5/2/1/1/3/8/20/20 -- a bimodal pile-up at both ends with the middle emptied, i.e. mode cycling. PSI = 0.95, well past the 0.25 convention, while the z-score reads about 0.1 and PASSES, because the two tails compensate and the mean barely moves. A built PSI that does not separate these two figures on a fixture of this shape has not been demonstrated -- see V16.

tasks.title: INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS is one global constant; each schedule carries its own sampling interval
tasks.detail: FILED 2026-09-14, DURING T11, RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED THERE — implementing this under T11 would have been the unrelated refactor CLAUDE.md §3 forbids (T11's own measured cause was never this: TM2's schedule fetches at a 1-minute interval, verified live, so 30 is correct for it). env.config.ts derives INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS's default (30) from an assumed 1-minute sampling interval ("half an hourly window... at the observed dataset's 1-minute interval, 60 rows/hour") but the constant itself is GLOBAL — one value for every InferenceSchedule in the system. Each schedule's own fetchConfig.intervalTime can differ (InferenceSchedule.fetchConfig is per-schedule JSON, already read by the scheduler for other fields). A schedule fetching at a 5-minute interval has 12 rows in a complete, healthy hour — every one of its windows would read SKIPPED forever against a 30-row floor, for a plant that is working exactly as intended. This is the "guess wearing a formula" shape MODEL-FLOW-020's own finding 3 names, one level removed: the FORMULA is fine, but it is evaluated against the wrong (global, not per-schedule) interval. NOT YET INVESTIGATED: whether every existing InferenceSchedule row in production actually sets fetchConfig.intervalTime, whether the value is trustworthy enough to derive a per-schedule floor from without a separate validation step, and where such a derived value should live — on the InferenceSchedule row itself (a real per-schedule column, matching how lagMinutes already is) versus computed at read time from fetchConfig. Inspect existing storage architecture before deciding, per CLAUDE.md §12.
tasks.result_2026_09_15:
RESOLVED 2026-09-15. All three of this task's own NOT-YET-INVESTIGATED questions answered first, against the tree, per CLAUDE.md §12.

Q1, DOES EVERY SCHEDULE SET fetchConfig.intervalTime? NO — verified false. store/model-pipeline.ts's own DataSourceConfig union shows intervalTime exists ONLY on PIConfig; SQLConfig/InfluxConfig/RestApiConfig/CSVConfig carry no interval concept at all. The backend's own asFetchConfig (inference-window-scheduler.service.ts) already silently defaults any non-string intervalTime to '1m' — confirming a SQL-sourced schedule was already being defaulted to a false 1-minute assumption before this task, the identical failure shape one level removed from the global constant this task set out to fix.

Q2, IS THE VALUE TRUSTWORTHY WITHOUT VALIDATION? NO — intervalTime is free text typed into a plain <Input placeholder="1m"> in the Data Studio wizard (pi-config-form.tsx), no client-side format validation. Handled by never trusting it silently: deriveMinRows (lib/inference-windows.ts) parses with the same strict \d+[smhd] regex apps/client/lib/dataset-fetch.ts's own parseDurationMs uses (duplicated one unit up — minutes not ms — since backend and client are separate apps with no shared TS package sized for one format parser), and returns null — NEVER a wrong guess — for anything unparseable or absent. The caller falls back to the existing env.INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS in that case, the exact same safe default every schedule already used.

Q3, WHERE SHOULD THE DERIVED VALUE LIVE? A REAL COLUMN, matching lagMinutes exactly, per this task's own suggested precedent — NOT computed at read time from raw fetchConfig on every scheduler tick. Read-time derivation would re-parse a potentially malformed value every tick and inherit asFetchConfig's own silent-default behaviour with no single point to audit; a stored column matches this codebase's own repeated discipline (psiRefEdges/scalingParams: fit once, freeze, never re-derive at read time) and is unconditionally recomputed by putScheduleService on every enable/update — not merged against the existing row like autoRetrain/warnSd — since it tracks fetchConfig/cadenceMinutes, which are THEMSELVES always freshly resolved from the dataset's current pipelineConfig on every call, never frozen at first-enable time.

WHAT SHIPPED. InferenceSchedule.minRows (packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma), Int NOT NULL DEFAULT 30 — applied directly against the live dev Postgres and marked resolved in Prisma's migration history (migration 20260915100000) rather than via `prisma migrate dev`, which refused with a PRE-EXISTING, UNRELATED drift (DatasetArtifact.droppedBadRows, not part of this task) demanding a destructive schema reset — flagged, not fixed; out of this task's scope, and a reset would have destroyed dev data no CLAUDE.md rule authorizes discarding on a task this narrow. deriveMinRows + parseIntervalMinutes (lib/inference-windows.ts), pure, unit-tested (inference-windows.spec.ts, 8 new cases: the 1m/30-row reproduction of env's own default, a 5-minute-interval derivation, a non-hourly cadence, seconds/hours units, the clamped-to-1 degenerate case, whitespace tolerance, absent-interval null, and 8 unparseable-string cases via it.each). putScheduleService (inference-window.authorized.service.ts) computes and writes minRows unconditionally in both the upsert's create and update branches, and returns it in the response. inference-window-scheduler.service.ts's SKIPPED decision now reads schedule.minRows instead of the global env.INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS; the failureReason message updated to match.

SCOPE DECIDED, NOT ASKED FOR IN THE FILED TASK: no new user-facing manual-override control was added (no DTO field for a human to set minRows directly). The task's own text frames the choice as stored-column vs. read-time-derivation, not stored-column-plus-override — adding one would be an unrequested feature, and every schedule's floor is already correctly self-deriving from real data with a safe fallback. Flagged as a natural follow-up if a real need for a manual override surfaces.

VERIFIED BY TEST SUITE — not against live infra (no schedule was actually run through a real PI/SQL fetch this pass; the migration SQL itself WAS applied and verified live against the real dev Postgres, confirmed via \d "InferenceSchedule" showing the real column). Full backend jest run: 752 passed / 761 total, the SAME 9 pre-existing baseline failures as before this task (auth/plan/workspace/nodes/workspace-plant/model-run controller DI-resolution errors, confirmed byte-identical to committed HEAD 16e6919 via direct diff — unrelated to inference-window entirely, not touched). check-types clean on every touched file (two real bugs found and fixed during this pass: a fetchConfig object-spread losing its index signature under strict TS, fixed by reading intervalTime off the pre-spread record directly; three `result.data` possibly-undefined test assertions, fixed by reading the same value off the upsert mock call args instead, matching this file's own established assertion idiom). Lint: verified by direct eslint --stdin comparison against the git-HEAD-committed content of both touched spec files that this task added ZERO net new lint errors — both files' pre-existing @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-* count (28 and 32 respectively, from the established `.mock.calls[0][0]` without-narrowing idiom already used throughout) is unchanged; this is pre-existing baseline debt, not something this task introduced or is in scope to refactor.

A dedicated regression-proof test (inference-window-scheduler.service.spec.ts) demonstrates the actual defect fixed, not just that a field reads correctly in isolation: a schedule at a 5-minute interval receiving 10 scored rows — which the OLD global-constant behaviour would have marked SKIPPED (10 < 30) — now spawns its container, because 10 is at or near a complete window for that schedule's own real interval (deriveMinRows(60, '5m') = 6, and 10 >= 6).

tasks.title: Per-tag Good/Bad status for a derived (equation) feature, on a surface that actually carries it
tasks.detail:
FILED 2026-09-14, DURING T12, RECORDED NOT BUILT THERE -- T12's own STEP 1 investigation established that the Input Data tab's traffic stream (PredictionLog / points[].features, the /predict request's own RAW values) carries NO status field at all -- not laundered away by scaling, simply never part of that contract (features: z.record(z.string(), z.number()), no sibling status map). T12 delivered the adjacent, cheaper half of the user's ask (an equation feature's SOURCE COLUMNS, from feature_spec.json, already read for scalingParams) but explicitly does NOT answer "which source is Bad", because the stream it reads cannot say. The rule this would display already exists and is already correct -- feature_service.py's _compute_feature_column reads every source through _good_value (None for a non-Good cell) and writes (0.0, STATUS_BAD) the moment ANY required source is None; formula/ratio/arith/log/lag/delta all gate the same way. T15 is a DISPLAY task for that already-correct upstream verdict, never a re-derivation of it client-side (T12's own finding on this exact point, and the drift class DS-LAKE-003/DS-LAKE-021-T02 already closed once each). NOT YET INVESTIGATED: which surface actually reads a PRE-SCALE frame with its status columns intact -- a scheduled window's input.parquet is the nearest candidate but T10 Part A explicitly refuses pointing the Input Data tab at it (one tab, two provenances); a NEW surface, or an existing one not yet audited for this, needs establishing before implementation. A formula's config.vars (available, not yet plumbed anywhere -- T12 deliberately left it unread since nothing consumed it) is what T15 will need to resolve a source COLUMN to its own status sibling; note it may itself be a derived column, not only a base tag (feature_service.py: apply_features mutates one frame across configs in order).

RESOLVED 2026-09-15. THE SURFACE QUESTION THIS TASK LEFT OPEN IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER REFRAMES WHAT "PER-TAG STATUS" MEANS EVERYWHERE IN THIS SYSTEM.

THE FINDING, TRACED FIRST-HAND, THAT DECIDED EVERYTHING ELSE: `{tag}__status` IS NOT PI'S QUALITY FLAG. The historical/summary fetch every dataset and every inference window runs through -- `aveva_connect.convertAverageDicttoDataFrame` (aveva_connect.py:73-92) -- builds its rows from `.value.timestamp` and `.value.value` ONLY. PI's `good`/`questionable`/`substituted` are never selected on that path, and `TagDataPoint` (schemas/data.py:88-91) has no field to carry them if they were. `frame_service.from_pi_response` then derives `{tag}__status` from `_coerce_value` (frame_service.py:45-67 -- "is this a parseable finite number") plus a per-tag `status == "failed"` check. That is PARSE/ARRIVAL health, not PI quality. `STATUS_QUESTIONABLE` is defined but never produced by any live path (`mark_questionable` has zero production callers). Consequence: BRONZE, SILVER, GOLD and a scheduled window's `input.parquet` all carry a status that is real and useful but is NOT what an operator means by "is this tag Good in PI". Anyone reading `__status` as PI quality is reading it wrong.

WHICH SURFACE, THEN: none of the persisted ones. PI's own flag reaches this system on exactly ONE path -- the snapshot read (`tag_service.current_values`, selecting `items.value.good;items.value.questionable;items.value.substituted`). That path was already built end to end and had never been called from any UI: python `POST /v1/data-sources/pi/current`, NestJS `POST authorized/data-source/:id/tags/current` (`tagsCurrentById`, which already resolves the source, refuses a non-PI one, and decrypts credentials), and even a client function (`services/data-sources.ts:151`) that was dead code. This task wired that existing path to the Input Data tab rather than building anything new to fetch with.

SCHEDULED-WINDOW `input.parquet` WAS EVALUATED AND REJECTED ON EVIDENCE, not only on T10 Part A's plane-separation rule: `drop_bad_feature_rows` runs at inference_window_service.py:263, BEFORE `put_frame` at :278, so every Bad-feature row is deleted before the object is written. That surface has ZERO Bad cells surviving by construction -- it could not have shown a Bad tag even if the tab were pointed at it.

WHAT SHIPPED. A new `GET authorized/model/:modelId/input-status` (`ModelInputStatusAuthorizedService`), deliberately SEPARATE from `/input-schema`: that endpoint's own discipline is "never a broken tab", and folding a live PI call into it would blank the whole feature list whenever the historian is down. Every failure path here returns `unavailableReason` with a 200 instead of throwing -- PI unreachable, a non-PI source, a source the caller cannot read (`resolveById` scopes by `createdById`), no resolvable source, no recorded feature columns. Source resolution reuses the established rule: `InferenceSchedule.sourceId` when a schedule exists (already a deliberate, validated choice resolved against the pinned version's own `sourceDatasetId`), else the dataset's single source, else an honest refusal rather than a guess between several.

THE DERIVED-FEATURE HALF, WHICH THIS TASK'S OWN TEXT SAID WOULD BE NEEDED: `feature_spec.json`'s `config.vars` is now read (it was persisted but unplumbed, exactly as filed). A new shared `lib/feature-sources.ts` resolves each derived column to the BASE tags it depends on TRANSITIVELY -- necessary because `apply_features` mutates one frame across configs in order, so a formula's own `vars` can name an earlier derived column (a formula over a lag) that PI has never heard of. Per-kind config shapes come from `feature-engineering.ts`'s own union: formula -> `config.vars` values, lag/rolling/delta/log -> `config.tag`, ratio/arith -> `config.tags`, datetime -> no tag at all (reads the timestamp, so no tag's quality can spoil it), anything else -> UNRESOLVED and reported UNKNOWN rather than guessed. The Bad-if-any-source-is-not-Good rule mirrors `_compute_feature_column`'s own gate (`_good_value` returns None for any status other than STATUS_GOOD) and is implemented ONCE, server-side -- never client-side, per this task's own instruction and the DS-LAKE-003 / DS-LAKE-021-T02 drift class. The failing sources are NAMED on the row.

ALSO DONE IN THE SAME PASS, AT THE USER'S REQUEST: PSI was removed from the Input Data tab (it remains on the Monitoring tab's Distribution Drift panel, beside the z-score, unchanged). That tab now answers one question per column -- Status: is this tag's data healthy in PI right now; Drift: how far live inputs have moved from the training distribution -- and its standing note, which used to say a per-tag Good/Bad view could not be shown here at all, now says what each column is instead.

TESTED, FRESH COUNTS FROM THIS SESSION: apps/backend 51 passed (`feature-sources.spec.ts` 12 -- transitive resolution, the unrecognised-kind and cyclic-spec refusals, datetime's empty-not-null source list; `model-input-status.authorized.service.spec.ts` 10 -- isGood/questionable/absent mapping, a Bad source naming itself on the derived row, PI queried for the BASE tag behind a derived column rather than the derived name, a PI failure degrading to `unavailableReason` instead of throwing, the multi-source refusal; plus the existing prediction-drift/prediction-psi suites still green at 15 and 14). apps/client 34 passed across the five touched files. packages/py-scaling 32 passed, untouched by this task and re-run as a control.

NOT VERIFIED, STATED PLAINLY: the real-PI leg. `nslookup scgc-piwebapi.scg.com` -> NXDOMAIN from this machine, checked this session, the same blocker V12 still carries. Every test above mocks the python client. What is proven is the mapping, the transitive resolution, the refusals and the degradation; what is NOT proven is that a live PI snapshot for this plant's real tags comes back shaped as expected. That leg must be confirmed the next time PI is reachable.

tasks.title: Rebuild the PSI display into the three levels T13 itself chose, and widen the API to carry bins
tasks.detail:
FILED 2026-09-15, DURING A DIRECT REQUEST TO 'fix display layout in MODEL-SERVE-001-T13'. AUDIT FIRST: T13's own result_2026_09_14 records a DISPLAY SPEC decided WITH THE USER against a rendered example, and that spec explicitly REJECTED one shape: 'adding a PSI column to the existing drift table (the shape first drafted this pass), on both counts above'. That rejected shape is exactly what shipped in the working tree — DriftPanel rendered PSI as two extra columns (PSI, PSI status) in the SAME six-column table as the z-score, sharing one status palette, with all three of DriftPanel's empty/loading/unavailable rungs gated on the Z-SCORE's own state only (so a good PSI report was invisible whenever drift had none, and vice versa). This task is the correction, not a new feature: T13's own CHOSEN three-level spec (a separate summary card; a per-tag click-to-open grouped bar chart of reference vs. current per frozen bin; an engineering-unit bin-edge table, marked NOT OPTIONAL) had never been wired to the API at all — ColumnPsi carried only {column, liveTotal, psi, outOfRangePct, status, reason}, with no edges/refCounts/live counts/binCount/binMode, so even level 1's own 'Bins used' column was unbuildable (the resolved binCount existed only interpolated into an INSUFFICIENT_DATA reason string).

THREE DELIBERATE DEPARTURES FROM T13's LITERAL TEXT, each because following it verbatim would have asserted something false about a system that had moved on since T13 was written:

(1) T13 says print 'rolling 24h' on every summary row. PSI is computed SYNCHRONOUSLY PER REQUEST — no scheduler, no cache — and the client fetches it over the SAME [from, to] as the z-score (use-prediction-monitoring.ts), which equals a rolling 24h only when the range toggle happens to sit on 24h. Printed literally, that label would be false on every other range. Replaced with the REAL window from basis.from/basis.to, satisfying T13's actual intent (cadence on screen, not inferred) without asserting a cadence the system does not have.

(2) T13 says show 'Last computed'. No computedAt/generatedAt exists anywhere in the PSI path — the figure is computed fresh on every read. Replaced with 'Computed over', carrying the real window plus a contributing-request count (histogramRequests of sampleRequests), rather than printing a timestamp that would only ever mean 'when you loaded the page'.

(3) T13's drill-down rationale claims 'quantile bins are equal-frequency by construction, so every reference bar sits at exactly 100/bin_count percent'. True for continuous bins, but psi.py's OWN module docstring contradicts it for categorical mode: 'a valve closed 90% of the time has a real 90/10 reference split, not 50/50' — which is why quantile_edges MEASURES refCounts for both modes rather than assuming uniform. The chart and table both render the measured refCounts unconditionally; the flat-reference hint text is shown only when binMode === 'continuous', where it is actually true.

WHAT SHIPPED, BACKEND: ColumnPsi gained a nested, nullable `bins` block (apps/backend/src/lib/prediction-psi.ts) — null EXACTLY when status is UNKNOWN (no reference at all), populated on every other status INCLUDING INSUFFICIENT_DATA (a below-floor tag still has a real reference and a real, if too-small, live pool; the row needs liveInRangeTotal/below/above/minSamples to print rows-vs-floor). `edges`/`refCounts` are echoed BY REFERENCE (same array identity as the caller's PsiReference — the existing V16 frozen-edges test was extended to assert this on `bins` too, not only on the raw reference object). PSI_EPSILON is now exported per T13's own 'must be stated, never hidden in a constant' instruction. The service's /psi response basis gained thresholds{warn,critical,minSamplesPerBin} (env-derived, so the on-screen disclaimer can never silently drift from what computePsi was actually called with), epsilon, and histogramRequests (the count AFTER the null-featureHistograms filter — sampleRequests, captured BEFORE that filter, overstates what actually fed the pool whenever a request predates T13; both are now sent, sampleRequests kept only for parity with DriftReport).

WHAT SHIPPED, CLIENT: PsiColumn/PsiReport mirrored the widened contract verbatim (services/model-monitoring.ts). Three new components under monitoring/psi/: PsiPanel (level 1 — its OWN loading/unavailable/empty ladder, fully independent of DriftPanel's — the structural fix; summary table Tag|PSI|Status|Bins used|Computed over; INSUFFICIENT_DATA is first-class — rows-vs-floor text, em-dash never a numeric PSI, row not clickable; single useState<string|null> selection, one tag open at a time, expand/collapse via a second <tr colSpan> row per the alert-row.tsx precedent), PsiBinChart (level 2 — the repo's FIRST grouped multi-series bar chart, built on ChartContainer/ChartConfig per ingestion-trend-chart.tsx rather than residual-histogram-chart.tsx, which hardcodes a hex fill DESIGN_SYSTEM.md forbids; below/above render as flanking bars after a gap, reference pinned to 0% there by construction, omitted entirely for a categorical tag; no status colours in the bars — status stays in the summary badge), and PsiBinTable (level 3, NOT OPTIONAL per T13 — real engineering-unit ranges per bin, overflow rows visually set apart with their OWN stated denominator, since liveTotal vs. liveInRangeTotal must never be silently conflated into one implied percentage base). A new shared lib/psi-bins.ts resolves binMode-dependent edge semantics ONCE (continuous: binCount+1 boundaries, bin i = [edges[i], edges[i+1]); categorical: edges.length === binCount, each entry IS the bin) for both the chart and the table to consume — duplicating that branch into two files is exactly how an off-by-one renders a plausible WRONG range, the silent failure this whole rebuild exists to prevent. drift-panel.tsx had its PSI columns, psiByColumn map, and PSI props deleted outright — it is the original four-column z-score table again, unit-tested with a dedicated negative-space case (queryByRole for a PSI columnheader returns null on any render). model-monitoring-tab.tsx gained a seventh card, same shell as its four siblings, stacked full-width BELOW Distribution Drift rather than beside it at any breakpoint — both cards are dense 5-6 column tables with a wide 'Computed over' cell; a 2-column grid would cramp both. 'Beside' in T13's own text read as 'a separate card on the same tab', not a column-width constraint.

VERIFIED BY TEST SUITE — NOT AGAINST LIVE INFRA, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN BORROWING THIS LEDGER'S 'VERIFIED LIVE' LANGUAGE FOR SOMETHING IT IS NOT: no real Postgres, MinIO, or running dev server was exercised this pass — every assertion below ran against jest/vitest with mocked Prisma and fixture data, the same distinction MODEL-SERVE-004's V01/V02 (docker ps against real containers) draws against a plain unit run. Both FULL suites were run, not only the touched files, specifically to catch a change with an effect outside them: backend jest (9 failed / 733 passed / 742 total) and client vitest (27 failed / 1273 passed / 1300 total). Every failing suite in both was confirmed BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed HEAD (16e6919) via `git diff --stat` on the failing spec files themselves and their underlying components — a pre-existing baseline this task did not touch and does not fix, not a regression this change introduced. None of the 36 pre-existing failures are in prediction-psi, prediction-log, or any monitoring/psi/ file. Targeted, all green: 14 backend prediction-psi.spec.ts cases (extended, not just re-run) now also assert bins is null on both UNKNOWN branches, populated with correct minSamples/liveInRangeTotal/binCount on INSUFFICIENT_DATA, bins.edges/refCounts/liveCounts are the SAME array references as the caller's inputs, and outOfRangePct reconciles exactly against (bins.below + bins.above) / liveTotal * 100 on a real non-zero-overflow fixture — ONE fact, one representation, never two independently-computed percentages that could silently diverge. 7 prediction-log.authorized.service.spec.ts cases extended to assert the new basis fields and histogramRequests <= sampleRequests when a row's featureHistograms is null. Client: 23 vitest cases across the extended empty-states.test.tsx and the new psi-panel.test.tsx, including V16's own worked example — 10 frozen quantile bins, reference flat at 10% each, current 22/18/5/2/1/1/3/8/20/20 (the exact fixture T13's own text names as 'the case that justifies the whole feature') — rendering CRITICAL with psi=0.947 on the card, plus the categorical branch (a real measured 90/10 reference, never an assumed flat 50/50; no <lo/>hi overflow bars; edges.length === binCount asserted on the LAST bin specifically, the exact spot an off-by-one would surface).

tasks.title: PSI needs a per-window histogram row; PredictionLog is the wrong plane for it
tasks.detail:
FILED 2026-09-15, SPLIT OUT OF T13 AFTER THAT TASK'S OWN AUDIT FOUND THE PLANE WRONG. T13 resolved PSI's design against PredictionLog.featureStats. THAT PREMISE IS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE REASON THIS TASK EXISTS: PredictionLog is written by apps/serving's synchronous /predict path ONLY (MODEL-SERVE-005-T01's own result, and T10 Part A traced it end to end), and scheduled inference does not write there at all -- decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference keeps the two planes separate deliberately. T10's own live database check measured PredictionLog rows = 0 for TM2, a scheduled-only model. So a PSI built on PredictionLog would have zero rows on the deployment that asked for it.

THE SAME CORRECTION APPLIES TO THE EXISTING Z-SCORE AND MAY BE THE LARGER FINDING. MODEL-SERVE-005-T02's poolFeatureStats reads the SAME PredictionLog stream, so the Distribution Drift z-score is ALSO structurally empty for any scheduled-only model -- consistent with T10 having to rewrite DriftPanel's third rung to name the stream it reads rather than say 'no data'. Establish whether the z-score should move to this plane in the same pass. DO NOT move only one: a screen showing a PSI figure beside a permanently-blank z-score is less readable than today's two blanks, and T13's DO-NOT-DELETE rule assumes both metrics are legible side by side.

THE RIGHT SOURCE IS THE WINDOW'S OWN INPUT FRAME. materialize_window's sequence is fetch -> apply_features -> trim -> select_columns -> missing_pct -> drop_bad_feature_rows -> put_frame, and MODEL-SERVE-005-T03's own retention note enumerates four objects per window (input.parquet, predictions.parquet, metrics.json, truth.parquet). input.parquet is therefore post-clean and PRE-SCALE, which is exactly what PSI's frozen bin edges require -- see T13's STEP 4, where a post-to_model_ready frame would have been min-max mapped to [0,1] and the edges would not apply.

CADENCE AND STORAGE, DECIDED WITH THE USER 2026-09-15: ONE histogram row per WINDOW (binCounts per tag against the frozen edges), rolling a trailing 24 windows to produce the published PSI. Per-window rows are additive, so a rolling figure is EXACT rather than an average of averages -- the same sufficient-statistics trick poolFeatureStats already uses for drift and InferenceWindowTruth already uses for live error, now used a third time rather than a new mechanism invented.

THE FLOOR IS ON SUMMED SAMPLES, NOT ON WINDOW COUNT, AND THIS IS THE EASY MISTAKE TO MAKE. 24 windows is 1,440 samples at a 1-minute interval and 24 samples at a 1-hour interval, and the second cannot support 10 bins at any window count. Gate on the SUM of binCounts across the rolling set against bin_count x 20; below it publish 'insufficient data' with the samples held and the floor needed, never a numeric PSI (T13's cost (d), rendered rather than hidden). This is the same defect shape T14 records for INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS -- a correct formula evaluated against an assumed rather than per-schedule interval -- so T14 is a DEPENDENCY of this task, not a sibling: both derive a row floor from fetchConfig.intervalTime, and neither of T14's first two open questions (whether every schedule sets it, and whether the value is trustworthy enough to derive a floor from) has been answered.

WHERE THE BINNING RUNS IS THE DECISION THAT DOMINATES THE COST -- see openDecisions. Prefer the option that does NOT touch images/trainer: MODEL-SERVE-006-T03 and PASS-A both record that nothing in CI builds and deploys that image (ghcr.io/soft-sensor-project 404s as both org and user, checked 2026-09-10, while the deployed tag lives under scgc/), so a correct source tree and a stale running image are indistinguishable until someone rebuilds and bumps the tag by hand. A PSI whose writer silently does not exist in the running image is worse than no PSI.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not change materialize_window, drop_bad_feature_rows, or to_model_ready; it does not make a schedule write PredictionLog (two planes by decision, not oversight); it does not delete the z-score (T13's rule); and it does not set alert thresholds -- 0.1/0.25 remain credit-scoring conventions until calibrated against this plant's own noise floor, per T13's cost (c).
tasks.result_2026_09_15:
RESOLVED 2026-09-15. Three openDecisions answered against the tree, all live-verified:

(3) inputKey pinning — ALREADY satisfied. InferenceWindow.inputKey/inputChecksum exist (schema.prisma), written by dispatchOne (inference-window-scheduler.service.ts) before any status decision. No change needed.

(2) Does a SKIPPED window carry a real frame — YES, verified against the live DB: `materialize_window` (apps/python/services/inference_window_service.py) calls `store.put_frame` unconditionally, before the backend's minRows floor check ever runs. Measured live: 25 of TM2's 71 windows carry inputKey, 20 of those FAILED IN THE CONTAINER with 60 clean rows each (more usable input than the 3 SUCCEEDED windows combined). The resolved rule needs no status whitelist: a window feeds the pool exactly when it carries a stored histogram/stats row (which happens exactly when a real cleaned frame was written); `basis.statusBreakdown` discloses the mix rather than filtering on it.

(1) Where the binning runs — a FOURTH option, not the ledger's own A/B/C: binning happens INSIDE `materialize_window` itself (apps/python/services/inference_window_service.py's new `_psi_histograms`/`_scaled_feature_stats`), returned in `InferenceWindowMaterializeResponse` the backend already stores from. Beats option A (backend-on-complete) on three counts: no second python round-trip (the function already holds the frame and already `get_json`s feature_spec.json); it runs before the status branch exists, so SKIPPED/FAILED windows get histograms too (option A would have covered only 3 of TM2's 25 real-input windows); no images/trainer change, so PASS-A's silent-no-op hazard for that image does not apply.

DECIDED WITH THE USER, NOT IN THE TASK'S OWN TEXT: (a) the z-score moves in the SAME pass as PSI — InferenceWindow gained featureStats (scaled units, via a THROWAWAY softsensor_scaling.to_model_ready copy using the frozen scalingParams — never re-fit on the window's own rows) alongside featureHistograms; the module docstring's "never calls to_model_ready" claim is amended, narrated, not silently contradicted: the frame WRITTEN stays raw/pre-scale, only a discarded copy is scaled for aggregates. (b) No backfill code for the retrain lever — PSI stays UNKNOWN on TM2 until the dataset artifact is rebuilt (compute_psi_ref_edges runs at GOLD-write time, verified live and reached, not gated); this is a user action, not a gap in this task. (c) Plane selection (window vs. PredictionLog) is decided by InferenceSchedule ROW PRESENCE, never by which table has rows — InferenceWindowMonitoringService.hasSchedule, a new service in inference-window/authorized/, exported from InferenceWindowModule; PredictionLogModule imports it (one-directional, verified acyclic); PredictionLogAuthorizedService.getDriftService/getPsiService dispatch on it, with the ORIGINAL /predict-plane bodies otherwise untouched.

REUSE, NOT DUPLICATION: resolveBaseline/resolvePsiReference (column_stats.json / feature_spec.json reads) were extracted verbatim from PredictionLogAuthorizedService into lib/artifact-baseline.ts so the window plane reads the identical sidecar the same way, rather than a second copy that could drift. lib/prediction-drift.ts / lib/prediction-psi.ts (computeDrift/computePsi/poolFeatureStats/poolHistograms) are UNCHANGED — pure and plane-agnostic; only the query that feeds them differs.

LIVE-VERIFIED, STATED PLAINLY ABOUT WHAT THAT MEANS: the new python helpers (_psi_histograms, _scaled_feature_stats) were run against TM2's REAL production feature_spec.json and a REAL already-fetched window frame (dt=2026-09-15/hour=02, 18 rows, SKIPPED) pulled live from MinIO. Result matched prediction exactly: feature_histograms=None (TM2's spec is featureVersion 2, no psiRefEdges — confirmed live, not assumed), feature_stats populated for all 21 feature columns using the FROZEN scalingParams — independently confirmed correct (not re-fit) by hand-checking one tag: AI001A2.PV's window-raw range (0.6063-0.6065) sits below its trained min (0.631, read live from the same spec), so scaling against the frozen [0.631, 0.652] range correctly produces a NEGATIVE scaled value (~-1.17); a re-fit would have trivially forced [0,1] and hidden this. The exact computed feature_stats JSON (21 tags, 2111 bytes) was then round-tripped through a real Postgres jsonb column (COPY in, read back out) — byte-identical, no serialization edge cases. Migration 20260915110000 was applied directly against the live dev DB (prisma migrate dev hit the SAME pre-existing droppedBadRows drift T14 already recorded; applied SQL directly + prisma migrate resolve --applied, same handling, never a reset) and confirmed via `\d "InferenceWindow"` showing both real jsonb columns; `prisma migrate status` reports the full history in sync. packages/prisma's dist/ build (a stale compiled output the live @softsensor/prisma import resolves to, not just the src/generated/client checked by `prisma generate` alone) had to be rebuilt (`pnpm --filter @softsensor/prisma build`) before apps/backend's own tsc even saw the new columns — a real, easy-to-miss gap between `generate` and what backend/apps actually import, worth remembering next schema change.

NOT LIVE-VERIFIED, AND SAID SO RATHER THAN GLOSSED: the actual NestJS scheduler tick -> real PI/SQL fetch -> dispatchOne -> Prisma write end-to-end path was not exercised against a live-spawned container this pass (would need real historian network reachability this dev environment's connectivity to the plant PI server was not verified for, and a full backend+python dev-server boot). That link rests on: (a) the SAME update() call already writing inputKey/inputRows live for 25 real windows, now carrying two more fields via the IDENTICAL DbNull-ternary pattern prediction-log's already-tested ingest path uses; (b) the full backend jest suite (754/763 pass, the SAME 9 pre-existing DI-resolution baseline failures T14 documented, confirmed via file-name diff, zero regressions); (c) the targeted prediction-log + inference-window jest suites (102/102, including two new dispatch tests proving getDriftService short-circuits to the window plane and never touches PredictionLog when a schedule exists). PSI on TM2 stays UNKNOWN until the user rebuilds the dataset artifact — the z-score renders (thin at first: zero windows carry featureStats until one new one materializes, since nothing was backfilled by decision) as soon as the next window runs.

WHAT SHIPPED: apps/python/services/inference_window_service.py (_psi_histograms, _scaled_feature_stats, _column_aggregate; module docstring amended) + apps/python/schemas/preprocess.py (InferenceWindowMaterializeResponse widened) + apps/python/tests/test_inference_window_psi_stats.py (11 new cases, including the re-fit-vs-fitted-params sabotage check). packages/prisma: InferenceWindow.featureHistograms/featureStats (migration 20260915110000). apps/backend: lib/python-preprocess-client.ts (schema widened), inference-window-scheduler.service.ts (writes both columns in the SAME update as inputKey, before the SKIPPED branch), lib/artifact-baseline.ts (new, extracted), inference-window/authorized/inference-window-monitoring.authorized.service.ts (new: hasSchedule, getDriftReport, getPsiReport, rolling <=24-window basisOf with statusBreakdown/windowsUsed/real windowStart span), inference-window.module.ts (exports the new service), prediction-log.module.ts (imports InferenceWindowModule), prediction-log.authorized.service.ts (dispatch + basis.plane on both branches), prediction-log.authorized.service.spec.ts (+2 dispatch tests, 8 call sites updated for the new constructor param). apps/client: services/model-monitoring.ts (MonitoringBasis widened onto both DriftReport/PsiReport basis), drift-panel.tsx (new Samples column rendering the already-wired col.n; plane-aware empty-state and basis-line copy), psi/psi-panel.tsx (plane-aware empty-state, basis line, and per-row "Computed over" unit noun; windowLabel prefers the REAL pooled windowStartEarliest/Latest over the requested range when on the window plane, so it never overstates what was actually pooled) + 4 test-fixture files updated for the new required basis.plane field.
