tasks.title: Monitoring's Actual-vs-Predict shows no y_actual; establish which of six causes it is before changing anything
tasks.detail:
FILED AT THE USER'S REQUEST 2026-09-15: Actual-vs-Predict on the Monitoring tab renders no y_actual, and the user asks whether the target tag is being fetched at all.

PLACEMENT, SAME POINTER AS T09/T10/T11: the subject is MODEL-SERVE-005-T03's (the ground-truth join, InferenceWindowTruth, the truth sweeper) and MODEL-SERVE-006's (InferenceWindow). Filed here because both read completed/100. A reader looking for the truth-join read side should expect it there and will not find it.

THE FRAMING TO REFUSE: 'the Y tag is not being fetched'. That is ONE of at least six causes, and four of the others produce the identical blank screen with a completely different fix. Worse, TWO of them mean the system is behaving CORRECTLY and there is nothing to fix -- so changing code before discriminating them risks 'fixing' a correct empty state, which on this surface means fabricating an actual value, the plausible-wrong-answer failure global_definition_of_done forbids.

STEP 0, READ THE SCREEN BEFORE READING ANY CODE. MODEL-SERVE-005-T03 built EmptyTruth (model-monitoring-tab.tsx) to discriminate FIVE causes by name -- transport error, no windows in range, join failed for N windows, scored-but-no-lab-measurement, measurement-outside-tolerance -- and T11 added a sixth (N windows were SKIPPED). If the tab is showing a bare 'no data' instead of one of those sentences, THAT is the first defect and it is a different task from the join itself. If it IS showing one of them, that sentence names the cause and most of this task is already done.

STEP 1, READ THE ROWS THAT ALREADY HOLD THE ANSWER. InferenceWindowTruth stores n, truth_rows, targetColumn, pairsKey, failureReason, attempt counter and nextJoinAfter, and the 2026-09-14 follow-up pass added failureReason precisely so 'the lab has not reported yet' and 'we could not ask' stop looking alike. Query them for the model in question BEFORE touching anything: a row with failureReason set is cause (B)/(C)/(D) below and carries the connector's own words; a row with n=0 and no failureReason is cause (E), a correct empty; NO row at all is cause (A) or (G).

SIX CANDIDATE CAUSES, DERIVED FROM THIS LEDGER'S OWN RECORDED FACTS AND NOT FROM A LIVE READ -- VERIFY EACH, DO NOT ASSUME THE ORDER IS THE LIKELIHOOD.

(A) THERE IS ALMOST NOTHING TO JOIN, AND NOTHING IS DUE. A truth join needs predictions.parquet, which only a SUCCEEDED window has. T10's live check found TM2 holding 50 FAILED + 1 SKIPPED and ZERO SUCCEEDED; T10's later live container run produced its FIRST SUCCEEDED window, 60cb652a at windowStart 2026-09-14T07:00Z. InferenceSchedule.truthLagMinutes defaults to 1440, so that single window was not even ELIGIBLE for a truth join until 2026-09-15T07:00Z. If the tab was read before then, zero pairs is the correct answer and there is no defect. CHECK THE CLOCK AGAINST truthLagMinutes FIRST -- it is the cheapest of the six and it would explain the symptom completely.

(B) THE SOURCE IS UNREACHABLE. The truth fetch goes to the window's OWN source (InferenceSchedule.sourceId + fetchConfig), i.e. the same historian the feature fetch uses. T11 and V12 both recorded nslookup scgc-piwebapi.scg.com -> NXDOMAIN on 2026-09-14, twice, and V12 is BLOCKED on exactly that. If PI is still unreachable the truth fetch throws before any upsert and backOff writes a failure row -- so this is visible in failureReason, not invisible.

(C) THE PI TRUTH PATH HAS NEVER RUN LIVE. MODEL-SERVE-005-T03's own result states it plainly: 'NOT LIVE-VERIFIED ... the PI branch. PI is unreachable from this dev machine ... so the Count-probe/EventWeighted path ships reviewed, with unit tests that inject a fake PI response.' The Count probe, the cal_basis override to EventWeighted, and the two-sequential-calls arrangement are all unexercised against a real PI. A genuine defect there would look exactly like this symptom, and no unit test can have caught it -- every mock accepts whatever it is handed, which is the same class of failure that hid the requestedAt +00:00 bug until V01 ran live.

(D) THE SQL CONNECTOR CANNOT FILTER A TIMESTAMP COLUMN. Recorded in MODEL-SERVE-005's implementation note as pre-existing and flagged-not-fixed: intergrations/sql_connect.py binds the range as VARCHAR, so Postgres refuses the comparison against a TIMESTAMP-typed time column ('operator does not exist: timestamp without time zone >= character varying'), and T03's own live verification deliberately used a text-typed column to sidestep it. If this model's lab source is SQL with a real TIMESTAMP column, the truth fetch fails every time for a reason that has nothing to do with the target tag.

(E) THERE GENUINELY WAS NO LAB EVENT, AND THE REFUSAL IS THE CORRECT BEHAVIOUR. The target is a .lab tag (FeaturePreset.targetY's own schema comment: 'Always a .lab tag'), and a real run's feature_spec.json records target_y = S204FBP.lab. Lab samples arrive hours or days apart while windows are hourly, so MOST windows hold zero -- T03's own granularity note says so. The join deliberately REFUSES a held value: PI holds a sparse .lab tag's last reading between samples, so the PI branch probes for event presence first and keeps only intervals an event actually occurred in. A blank chart here is the system declining to publish a confident number against a value nobody measured. DO NOT 'FIX' THIS ONE.

(F) THE TARGET DOES NOT RESOLVE FOR THIS VERSION. Truth resolves the target through ModelVersion -> sourceRun -> ModelTrainingRun.targetY, and T03's backOff path exists partly because resolving the target is itself one of the things that can fail (the 2026-09-14 migration dropped NOT NULL from truth.targetColumn for this reason). Confirm targetY is non-null on the PINNED version's source run specifically, not on some other run of the same model. This is the closest cause to the user's own hypothesis and it is checkable in one query.

(G) THE SWEEP IS NOT RUNNING IN THE PROCESS THAT SERVES. InferenceTruthSweeperService has its own setInterval(...).unref() at 900000ms and V06 observed the boot line 'Ground-truth join sweep scheduled every 900000ms.' But T11 recorded this dev machine running TWO nest --watch and TWO dist/main processes at once, with which one serves traffic never established. Confirm the sweeper in the process actually answering requests, not in whichever process logged last.

ALSO CHECK, BECAUSE IT WOULD MASK EVERYTHING ABOVE: V05's batch-head starvation is FIXED (backOff now writes a row so a permanently-failing window stops sitting at the head of every sweep), but the fix is only as good as findDueWindows' ordering over the CURRENT row set. With 50 FAILED windows on this model and a batch of 25, confirm the one joinable window is actually reached.

WHAT THIS TASK DELIVERS: the identified cause with its evidence, and either the fix if the cause is a defect, or the recorded finding if it is (A) or (E). It does NOT change the join's semantics, does not relax the event-presence requirement, does not touch EvalPoint's non-optional actual/residual (T03 kept it non-optional on purpose and fed it only joined rows), and does not add an upload path -- decisions.ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_target_tag rejected that for this pass and named the condition for reconsidering it.
tasks.result_2026_09_15:
RESOLVED 2026-09-15. The framing in the task's own filed text ("the Y tag is not being fetched") is REFUTED. The actual cause, established by reading the rows that already held the answer (STEP 1) before touching any code, per this task's own required order:

CAUSE (A), CONFIRMED: NOTHING IS DUE YET. TM2 has 3 SUCCEEDED windows (2026-09-14 07:00/08:00/09:00 UTC), all carrying predictionsKey. InferenceWindowTruth held 0 rows at investigation time. The sweeper's own findDueWindows predicate is `windowEnd <= now - schedule.truthLagMinutes` (truthLagMinutes = 1440 = 24h for TM2); earliest eligible window is therefore 2026-09-15 08:00 UTC, and the investigation ran at 2026-09-15 04:03 UTC — about 4 hours early. Zero truth rows is CORRECT, not a defect.

CAUSE (F), THE USER'S OWN HYPOTHESIS, RULED OUT: queried live. The pinned PRODUCTION version (2eb8e6c8) -> sourceRun (d2abe89d) -> targetY = 'S204FBP.lab'. Non-null, a real .lab tag, resolves correctly. The target IS being fetched (or would be, once due) -- the premise behind the user's own question does not hold.

CAUSE (D) SQL-TIMESTAMP-BINDING RULED OUT: TM2's source (92da5f93) is type 'aveva' (PI), not SQL -- the recorded SQL connector bug (VARCHAR-bound timestamp comparison) cannot apply here.

STEP 0 CONFIRMED: EmptyTruth (model-monitoring-tab.tsx) already discriminated the four causes it names correctly for TM2's actual state (windowsInRange=3, truthRows=0, windowsFailed=0 at investigation time) -- it rendered the accurate branch 5 sentence. The screen was not the defect.

tasks.title: Stop does not take effect on already-queued windows; the Model List toggle carries two different states in one control; and monitoring health has no home in the status model at all
tasks.detail:
FILED AT THE USER'S REQUEST 2026-09-15, FROM A REAL OPERATIONAL SYMPTOM: after a model's container FAILED, the next hourly window still ran, and pressing Stop did not appear to take effect. The user additionally asks that this state be linked to the toggle on the Model List, and points out -- correctly, and this is the sharpest part of the report -- that a container FAILURE is a DEPLOY/RUN-STEP state while a monitoring Warning arises only AFTER a model has been running, so the two are not points on one scale.

PLACEMENT, SAME POINTER AS T09/T10/T11/T17: the subject is MODEL-SERVE-006's (the scheduler is T02's, the schedule row is T09's, deployStatus and classifyDeployStatus are T12's). Filed here because 006 reads completed/100 and this would reopen it.

CAUSES BELOW ARE DERIVED FROM THIS LEDGER'S OWN RECORDED FACTS, NOT FROM A LIVE READ. Verify each from source before implementing anything -- this ledger's unbroken record is that each pass finds its predecessor's premise overstated or mis-framed, and the whole point of T13's audit-first rule applies here identically.

=== PART A -- WHY STOP DOES NOT TAKE EFFECT ===

THE FRAMING TO REFUSE: 'Stop is broken'. Stop has at least four distinct meanings and the report is consistent with several of them being individually correct while the combination is surprising: (i) stop inserting NEW windows, (ii) stop dispatching windows ALREADY INSERTED, (iii) kill a container that is IN FLIGHT right now, (iv) stop the model from being considered deployed at all. Establish which of the four the code implements today before deciding which it SHOULD, because more than one may need to change and they need changing differently.

(A1) STRONGEST CANDIDATE -- dispatchDue MAY NOT CHECK enabled, AND 48 HOURS OF ROWS MAY ALREADY BE QUEUED. T02 describes the tick as insert-plus-reconcile, and its own dispatch_order_2026_09_14 note describes the claim as 'PENDING windows ... with no model scoping and take = INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY' -- a description of the claim query that mentions ordering and concurrency and says nothing about the schedule's enabled flag. If insertDueWindows filters on enabled but dispatchDue does not, then disabling a schedule stops FUTURE rows and does nothing to the rows already sitting there. INFERENCE_BACKFILL_HORIZON_HOURS defaults to 48 and that same note records a freshly enabled schedule inserting the full horizon at once, so a disabled model could have up to 48 PENDING rows that keep being claimed one tick at a time -- which is exactly the reported symptom, one window per hour continuing after Stop. THIS IS A QUERY TO READ, not a theory to argue about: read dispatchDue's where clause and settle it in one look.

(A2) EVEN IF DISPATCH DOES CHECK enabled, THE QUEUED ROWS ARE A SECOND SURPRISE. Nothing in this ledger says disabling a schedule CANCELS its PENDING rows. If they merely sit dormant, then re-enabling the schedule weeks later replays a backlog of windows whose ranges are long past -- and under T02's `desc` ordering the newest of those old rows wins the slot ahead of a genuinely current window. Decide explicitly what Stop does to PENDING rows: cancel them to a terminal status, leave them dormant, or leave them and bound them by age. Whichever is chosen, the row must record WHY it reached that status, the way SKIPPED already carries its reason.

(A3) AN IN-FLIGHT CONTAINER IS ITS OWN QUESTION AND IS ARGUABLY CORRECT AS-IS. Stop disabling a schedule says nothing about a container already running. Letting it finish is defensible -- it will write a real window for a real range -- but it means 'Stop' is followed by a prediction landing, and a user reading the screen will take that as Stop having failed. If it is left to finish, the SCREEN must say so ('stopping -- one window still in flight'), because the alternative is a correct behaviour that reads as a broken one.

(A4) TWO BACKEND PROCESSES WERE MEASURED ON THIS DEV MACHINE, AND THIS WOULD LOOK IDENTICAL. T11 recorded, as a live fact rather than a hypothesis, TWO `nest start --watch` and TWO `dist/main` instances alive at once with which one serves traffic never established. Two processes each running the tick means INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY -- a per-process bound -- permits two concurrent containers, and a Stop issued to the process serving HTTP does not stop the tick in the other. Confirm the process count before attributing anything to application logic; if this is the cause, the fix is operational and the code is innocent.

(A5) A FAILED WINDOW DOES NOT AND CURRENTLY SHOULD NOT DISABLE THE SCHEDULE -- SAY SO ON SCREEN. The status is DERIVED at read time (T12), so it heals to 'running' on the next success with no sticky error, and T12's warmup_2026_09_14 amendment makes a never-succeeded schedule read 'error' on its FIRST failed window rather than waiting for three. That is deliberate: the user's own environment demonstrates why auto-disabling on failure would be dangerous -- PI resolved NXDOMAIN for a period (T11, V12), which would have permanently stopped every model over a transient network condition. But a model that reads 'error' while continuing to spawn a container every hour is behaviour nobody has been told about, and that gap is what produced this report. See openDecisions for whether a circuit breaker belongs here at all.

=== PART B -- THE TOGGLE IS BOUND TO THE WRONG KIND OF VALUE ===

ONE CONTROL CANNOT CARRY BOTH A SETTING AND A DERIVED FACT. `enabled` is a setting the operator owns and writes. deployStatus is DERIVED from windows and is not writable by anyone -- T12 removed it from UpdateModelSchema for exactly that reason. A toggle whose visual state comes from the derived value has no honest position to sit in when the two disagree: a model with enabled=true and status 'error' is ON as a setting and failing as a fact, and whichever one the toggle shows, it is silently hiding the other. That is the same two-sources-of-truth defect T09 had to close when it deleted the optimistic `setModel(...deployStatus: next)` write for asserting 'running' where the classifier would have said 'initializing'.

WHAT TO BUILD: the toggle reflects and writes `schedule.enabled` ONLY -- pressing it changes a thing the user owns, and its position is never computed from windows. The derived status renders BESIDE it as a badge, from the same classifyDeployStatus every other surface uses (never a second classifier, per T12's one-decider rule), with the reason T09 already plumbed through getStatusService (lastFailure / lastSkipped, URL-redacted). The Model List's per-model figure is BATCHED through deriveDeployStatuses, so it must read the same classifier as the detail page or the two screens will disagree about one model -- the divergence T09 had to close one screen over.

CHECK T09's OWN GATING WHILE HERE, BECAUSE IT IS A CANDIDATE FOR 'THE BUTTON DID NOTHING'. T09 gated Start/Stop on the status hook having resolved once, so the disabled state would not flip under the cursor. If that hook errors or never resolves, the button stays disabled and a user experiences it as unresponsive with no message -- indistinguishable from a Stop that was issued and ignored. Confirm the hook's error path renders something.

=== PART C -- HEALTH IS A SECOND AXIS AND HAS NO HOME TODAY ===

THE USER'S OBSERVATION IS THE DESIGN FINDING: a container failure and a monitoring warning are not two severities of one thing. A failure is a RUN-LIFECYCLE fact (did the window execute) and is knowable from the first window; a drift or SD warning is a HEALTH fact (is the model still right) and is only knowable AFTER windows succeed and, for live error, after the lab reports. Confirmed by what each one reads: classifyDeployStatus reads InferenceWindow statuses, while warnSd / criticalSd / driftMonitor / driftThresholdPct live on InferenceSchedule (persisted by T09, under the wizard's own atom names) and drift/PSI read the aggregates T16 is moving to the window plane.

TWO GAPS, BOTH REAL, NEITHER PREVIOUSLY FILED. (1) THE THRESHOLDS HAVE NO EVALUATOR: T09 gave those four fields a persisted home and phase-6-deploy.tsx renders the controls, but nothing in this ledger records anything CONSUMING them to raise a warning -- MODEL-SERVE-005-T02's drift report classifies OK/WARN/CRITICAL against system-wide env defaults, and its own implementation note says so explicitly ('system-wide env defaults in this pass, not persisted per model -- MODEL-SERVE-006-T09 is explicitly where those atoms get a real per-model home'). So a per-model threshold the operator set is quite possibly not the threshold anything evaluates. VERIFY THAT SPECIFICALLY: it is a setting that appears to work and may do nothing, which is worse than an absent control. (2) THE ALERTS SURFACE READS A FIELD NOTHING WRITES: T10's own correction (A) records that lib/alerts.ts filters `model.data.logs` for level==='error' and attaches the last three to every failed-deploy alert row, while the field's only writer (appendLogService) has NO client caller -- so those alert rows have always shown an empty error list. Any health work here should feed alerts from the real sources (InferenceWindow.failureReason, the drift/PSI report) rather than build on that field.

DO NOT WIDEN classifyDeployStatus's ENUM TO CARRY HEALTH. Adding 'warning' beside stopped/running/initializing/error makes one value answer two independent questions, and the first model that is healthy-but-drifting or failing-but-within-thresholds has no representable state. Add a SEPARATE health classifier with its own pure function and its own spec file, mirroring lib/deploy-status.ts's shape, and render the two together. A model shows an operational state AND, once it has succeeded at least once, a health state -- never one collapsed value.

WHAT THIS TASK DOES NOT DO: it does not change the cadence, INFERENCE_BACKFILL_HORIZON_HOURS, or T02's `desc` dispatch ordering (all deliberate, with recorded reasons); it does not touch SKIPPED's semantics or its relationship to the staleness alarm (settled by T01/T10 and re-affirmed by T11); it does not alter the connector's error text; and it does not set drift thresholds from measurement -- calibrating 0.1/0.25 and the SD bands against this plant's own noise floor remains T13's open cost (c).
openDecisions: DOES REPEATED FAILURE AUTO-PAUSE THE SCHEDULE? A circuit breaker on classifyDeployStatus's existing `failing` condition (three consecutive failed terminal windows) is the obvious shape and it is NOT obviously right. Against it: the failure mode this deployment actually experienced was a transient network condition -- PI resolving NXDOMAIN for a period, recorded twice on 2026-09-14 -- and auto-pausing would have permanently stopped every model over an outage that healed itself, with a re-enable nobody knew was needed. For it: an hourly container that cannot possibly succeed is wasted spawn, wasted log volume, and a screen that reads 'error' forever while doing work. A middle option worth costing: keep dispatching but BACK OFF geometrically after consecutive failures, which is the exact mechanism MODEL-SERVE-005-T03's truth sweeper already uses for the same problem one entity over, and which heals on its own without an operator action. Decide with the plant's own tolerance in view, and whichever is chosen, the screen must state it -- 'paused after N failures' and 'retrying, backed off to every N minutes' are different facts and a reader must not have to infer which applies.

WHAT DOES Stop DO TO PENDING ROWS -- cancel, leave dormant, or leave and age-bound? Cancelling needs a terminal status with a recorded reason (and a decision on whether CANCELED joins the five-value vocabulary four enums in this schema already share, or whether SKIPPED with a distinct reason is enough -- note T01 is explicit that SKIPPED is a real terminal status and not a synonym for FAILED, so overloading it needs care). Leaving them dormant preserves backfill intent but makes re-enabling replay history under `desc` ordering. Age-bounding is the middle option and needs a number someone chose, not a default.

DOES THE HEALTH AXIS GATE ANYTHING, OR IS IT PURELY INFORMATIONAL? A warning that only colours a badge is safe and may be sufficient. A warning that blocks a promote, pauses a schedule, or triggers autoRetrain (a field T09 persisted and, per the same gap as the SD thresholds, quite possibly nothing consumes) is a control-flow change and needs its own refusal semantics with an override on the record -- the shape MODEL-SERVE-001-T06's r2 floor already established for promotion. Do not let it become a gate by accident: decide, and record the rejected alternative.
tasks.result_2026_09_15:
VERIFIED FROM SOURCE, NOT FROM THIS LEDGER'S OWN CAUSES -- as instructed, every cause above was re-derived from code and live data before anything was built.

A1 CONFIRMED: dispatchDue's `where` read only `{ status: 'PENDING' }`, no `enabled` check, no schedule join (insertDueWindows already filtered `enabled: true`; dispatchDue did not). A2 CONFIRMED: Stop is exactly `updateMany({ enabled: false })`, nothing touches PENDING rows. A4 CONFIRMED LIVE, WITH ARITHMETIC PROOF NOT JUST A PROCESS COUNT: `finishedAt` during the 2026-09-15 01:12-01:46 UTC backfill split into two series exactly 5:00 apart, offset ~3:10 -- two independent tick loops (INFERENCE_TICK_INTERVAL_MS=300000, INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1 makes one process incapable of that spacing alone). `ps`/`lsof` confirmed: PID 96593, a 26-HOUR-OLD `dist/main` (started 2026-09-14 11:08), still ticking against the same DB; only the other PID (12660) serves HTTP. THE ORPHAN IS NOT PART OF THIS FIX AND WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT RUNNING (no process killed, per the plan) -- ITS CONSEQUENCE MUST BE STATED PLAINLY: the A1 code fix is NOT in effect for this deployment until BOTH (a) 12660 is rebuilt and restarted, AND (b) 96593 is killed. Leaving 96593 alive after (a) alone silently defeats the fix -- it holds pre-fix `dispatchDue` in memory regardless of source changes.

THE LEDGER'S OWN FRAMING WAS WRONG ON WHAT ACTUALLY PRODUCED THE REPORT. A1+A4 need a PENDING backlog to manifest, and steady-state at this schedule's cadence/lag is ~0-1 PENDING rows (drains in one tick) -- not the reported symptom. THE REAL ROOT CAUSE, found only by reading both surfaces' branch conditions: `classifyDeployStatus` returns 'error' for an ENABLED-but-failing schedule, and both the Model List switch (`isOn = deployKey==='running'||'initializing'`) and the detail page's button branch (`deployKey==='running'||'initializing' ? Stop : Start`) keyed off that DERIVED value -- so an enabled-but-failing model showed OFF/Start on every surface, and the only action offered wrote `enabled: true`. Confirmed against the live DB: `InferenceSchedule.updatedAt` moved to `enabled=true` at a timestamp seconds after a SKIPPED window finished, then fresh windows kept appearing hourly -- consistent with the user pressing what looked like Start (because the switch read OFF) on a model that was already enabled and failing. DECIDED BY THE USER (2026-09-15, via AskUserQuestion) -- REJECTED ALTERNATIVE RECORDED FOR EACH, PER THIS TASK'S OWN RULE: (1) SCOPE this pass = the Stop-control defect + A1 only; rejected bundling the key-mismatch bugs, the Part C evaluator, or all of T19 (CLAUDE.md section 15). (2) PENDING rows on Stop = leave dormant, decide later; rejected a CANCELED enum value (a migration before semantics are settled) and age-bounding (no chosen number yet) -- filed as T20. (3) Repeated failure = status only, no backoff, no circuit breaker; rejected both, because this deployment's actual failures are connector reachability, the exact transient class a circuit breaker would have mishandled (recorded in openDecisions above from the PI/NXDOMAIN incident). (4) prodStatus stays operator-writable; a derived health value renders beside it when Part C is built; rejected making it derived now (T12's move for deployStatus) -- filed as T21.

BUILT AND VERIFIED THIS PASS: (i) `lib/deploy-status.ts` -- new `DeployState { status, enabled }`; `deriveDeployStatuses` and `overlayDeployStatus` widened to carry both (the `enabled` value was already being selected and discarded); all four call sites (getModelsService, updateModelService, appendLogService, getWorkspaceModels) updated, none needed body changes beyond the type flowing through. tasks.detail:
SAME POINTER AS T19: the subject is MODEL-SERVE-006's (InferenceWindow/InferenceSchedule, T02's scheduler). Filed under 001 because 006 reads completed/100.

Deferred from T19 by the user's own 2026-09-15 decision: leave PENDING rows dormant for now, revisit the policy separately. With T19's A1 fix shipped, a disabled schedule's PENDING rows simply stop being claimed (dispatchDue now scopes its claim to enabled schedules), so this is no longer urgent -- but the rows still sit there, and re-enabling the schedule replays them newest-first under T02's own `desc` ordering, including any that are now hours or days stale.

OPEN DECISION, CARRIED FORWARD FROM T19 VERBATIM: cancel to a terminal status (needs a decision on whether CANCELED joins InferenceWindowStatus's five values -- a migration -- or SKIPPED with a distinct reason suffices, noting T01 is explicit that SKIPPED is not a synonym for FAILED and overloading it needs care); leave dormant indefinitely (current behaviour, preserves backfill intent, accepts stale replay on re-enable); or age-bound (dormant rows older than a chosen threshold are never dispatched even after re-enable -- needs a number someone picks, not a default). Whichever is chosen, the row must record WHY it reached that status, the way SKIPPED already does.

tasks.title: Build the health axis: an evaluator for the five per-model threshold fields, and feed prodStatus from a real measurement
tasks.detail:

VERIFIED THIS PASS (T19), NOT PREVIOUSLY CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE: `warnSd`, `criticalSd`, `driftMonitor`, `driftThresholdPct` (schema.prisma) are written by putScheduleService and read back ONLY by getScheduleService to echo into the settings UI -- no backend file compares them against a measurement anywhere, `apps/python` has zero hits for the snake_case equivalents, and `if (schedule.driftMonitor)` exists nowhere. These are five settings that appear to work and may do nothing.

THE LEDGER'S OWN DO-NOT-DO: do not widen classifyDeployStatus's enum to add a 'warning' value -- a model that is healthy-but-drifting or failing-but-within-thresholds has no representable state if operational and health are collapsed into one. Render the two states together, never one collapsed value.

DECIDED BY THE USER (2026-09-15, ON T19): prodStatus stays operator-writable (UpdateModelSchema's dto.prodStatus path, model.authorized.service.ts) -- this task's evaluator output renders BESIDE it, not in place of it. Rejected: making prodStatus derived and removing the manual write path (T12's move for deployStatus) -- revisit only if this task's output is trusted enough to replace the manual control, and that is a SEPARATE decision from building the evaluator itself.

CARRIED OPEN DECISION FROM T19: does the health axis gate anything (block a promote, pause a schedule, trigger autoRetrain), or is it purely informational (colours a badge only)? Decide and record the rejected alternative before implementing -- do not let it become a gate by accident.
tasks.detail_addendum:

tasks.title: alerts.ts's error-log decoration is dead by construction -- feed it a real source or remove it
tasks.detail_addendum:

tasks.detail:
SAME POINTER AS T19/T10: the subject is MODEL-SERVE-006's (Model.data.logs, InferenceWindow.failureReason).

THE LEDGER'S OWN DIAGNOSIS FOR THIS WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE, VERIFIED FROM SOURCE THIS PASS: T10's claim ('appendLogService has NO client caller') is FALSE -- `apps/client/services/model.ts`'s `appendModelLog` is a real client wrapper, called from `apps/client/hooks/model/use-model-retrain.ts` (four call sites, wired to a live 'Retrain' button on the model detail page), and `git blame` shows those calls existed four days before a comment in model-log-sheet.tsx asserted the opposite. The ACTUAL defect is different: every one of those four call sites hardcodes `level: 'info'` -- `level: 'error'` is produced by ZERO code paths anywhere in the client (confirmed by a full-client grep; the only hit is a test fixture). So `apps/client/lib/alerts.ts`'s `.filter(l => l.level === 'error')` is guaranteed to evaluate empty today, and its `.at(-1)?.timestamp` fallback always resolves to `model.updatedAt` -- the OUTCOME T10 described (empty error list, always) is correct; the REASON is not dead code, it is a live code path that never emits the level this filter looks for.

TWO WAYS TO CLOSE THIS, NEITHER IMPLEMENTED YET -- DECIDE WHICH: (a) make some real event emit `level: 'error'` through appendLogService (e.g. a failed retrain), so the existing filter has something to find; or (b) drop `model.data.logs` as this feature's data source entirely and read the REAL sources instead -- `InferenceWindow.failureReason` (already surfaced via getStatusService's lastFailure/lastSkipped, redacted) and the drift/PSI report -- which is what T19's Part C audit recommended for any health-adjacent work touching alerts. (b) is likely the smaller, more correct change: `model.data.logs` was never the deploy-failure source of truth (classifyDeployStatus already reads InferenceWindow directly), so alerts.ts is decorating a real failed-deploy row with a field that was always going to be empty by construction, not by bug.

tasks.title: The two-axis contract: deploy reads preflight evidence, not a guess
tasks.detail:
PLACEMENT, SAME POINTER AS T09-T23: the subject is MODEL-SERVE-006's (classifyDeployStatus is T12's, lib/deploy-status.ts). Filed here because 006 reads completed/100.

THIS TASK IS THE CONTRACT, NOT A UI. deploy = is the schedule alive and dispatching; monitoring = is the data and the model still right. One classifier per axis, per T12's one-decider rule and per the shape T21 already established when it added lib/model-health.ts beside lib/deploy-status.ts rather than widening it.

DO NOT WIDEN classifyDeployStatus's ENUM with 'warning' or 'frozen'. T21 already recorded the reason: a model that is healthy-but-drifting or failing-but-within-thresholds has no representable state once operational and health collapse into one value.

DO NOT RENAME THE WIRE KEYS to 'failed'/'offline'. T22 has just finished fixing three client maps that keyed on the word 'failed' and silently fell through a ?? to Stopped/green (model-detail-dialog.tsx's DEPLOY_MAP, node-detail-panel.tsx's DEPLOY_DOT/DEPLOY_LABEL, and PROD_MAP's missing 'frozen'). Renaming the enum manufactures a second round of the identical defect. Change LABELS only: 'error' -> 'Failed' (already what DEPLOY_CONFIG displays), 'stopped' -> 'Offline'.

THE CURRENT 'initializing' CONDITION CANNOT SURVIVE THIS FEATURE. classifyDeployStatus reads !hasEverSucceeded && !hasFailedWindows (T12's warmup_2026_09_14 amendment), which is an inference from window history. Once Running must persist through failures (T26), that inference is unusable. This task changes the classifier's INPUT, not its output: store the preflight EVIDENCE (T25) and keep deriving. Storing preflightOk is storing a fact about an event, the same class of thing as promotedAt -- it is not writing a status, so T12's derived-at-read-time rule still holds for Running/Offline.

NOT IN SCOPE: a second classifier for the deploy axis, the cadence, INFERENCE_BACKFILL_HORIZON_HOURS, or T02's `desc` dispatch ordering -- all deliberate, all with recorded reasons.
tasks.result_2026_09_16: COMPLETED. Contract recorded and LABELS ONLY changed, per this task's own 'THIS TASK IS THE CONTRACT, NOT A UI'. The two-axis contract now lives in lib/deploy-status.ts's own doc comment: DEPLOY = is the schedule alive and dispatching; MONITORING (lib/model-health.ts) = is the data and the model still right. DeployStatus's four wire values are UNCHANGED ('stopped'|'running'|'error'|'initializing') and the enum was NOT widened with 'warning'/'frozen' nor renamed to 'failed'/'offline' -- T22 had just repaired three client maps that keyed on 'failed' and fell through a ?? to green/Stopped, and renaming would manufacture a second round of that identical defect. 'error' already displayed 'Failed'; 'stopped' -> 'Offline' applied to all SEVEN copies of the label found in the client (deployed-table.tsx, deploy-summary-pills.tsx, models/[id]/page.tsx's DEPLOY_CONFIG, model-detail-dialog.tsx, model-preview-sheet.tsx, model-table.tsx, models/views/page.tsx) -- the ledger named six, the seventh was an inline literal in models/views/page.tsx. classifyDeployStatus stays derived-at-read-time: only its INPUTS changed.

tasks.title: Preflight at enable: Initialize resolves to Running or Failed, and a failure inserts nothing
tasks.detail:
TODAY, ENABLING A SCHEDULE WITH AN UNREACHABLE SOURCE INSERTS UP TO 48 HOURS OF WINDOWS AND FAILS HOURLY FOREVER. Measured, not theorised: T19 read TM2's live rows and found 70 FAILED windows, every one reading 'Materialize failed: Could not read the source...', and NONE of them ever spawned a container (the raise happens before runner.spawn). That is the symptom this task closes.

VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST: putScheduleService ALREADY has four enable-time refusals (no PRODUCTION version, non-empty derived_from_target, target_scaled, no recorded feature columns -- T09/D5). This task adds a LIVE PROBE as a fifth refusal. It does not build a new mechanism.

REUSE T15's PROBE, DO NOT WRITE A SECOND ONE. GET .../input-status already: queries PI's snapshot path (tag_service.current_values, the ONE path in this system that carries PI's own good/questionable/substituted flag -- see T15's finding on why no persisted surface does), resolves a derived feature's base tags TRANSITIVELY via lib/feature-sources.ts (a formula's vars can name an earlier derived column), and returns unavailableReason with a 200 instead of throwing.

TWO LIMITS THAT CHANGE THIS TASK'S SCOPE -- ESTABLISH BOTH BEFORE ESTIMATING. (1) input-status accepts PI sources ONLY; a SQL source returns unavailableReason immediately, so SQL needs a single-window materialize dry-run instead. (2) intergrations/sql_connect.py binds the time range as VARCHAR, so Postgres refuses the comparison against a genuinely TIMESTAMP-typed time column -- recorded twice already (MODEL-SERVE-005's implementation note, and decisions.ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_target_tag). A SQL preflight will therefore fail for a reason that is not the operator's config. FLAG IT, DO NOT FIX IT: it belongs to the connector.

STORE THE EVIDENCE ON InferenceSchedule: preflightAt, preflightOk, preflightReason. preflightReason MUST be the connector's own text VERBATIM, via diagnose_empty_pi_fetch (T04/V09) -- V09 exists precisely because a guessed category sent a reader to audit a config that was already correct. Redact at the READ boundary with lib/redact-urls.ts: connector text can carry a presigned URL's X-Amz-Signature, the class MODEL-FLOW-000-T06 forbids and which this ledger has now had to close twice (T09 for failureReason, T10 for InferenceWindowLog).
openDecisions: WHAT DOES 'STOP' MEAN WHEN PREFLIGHT FAILS? RECOMMENDED: refuse at enable -- no windows inserted, no dormant PENDING rows for T20 to sweep, and the client already surfaces a server refusal's own message verbatim (the three bare `catch {}` blocks fixed in this feature's implementation note). It does NOT reverse T19's user decision of 'status only, no backoff, no circuit breaker': that decision refused auto-pausing a schedule that is already RUNNING, which is a different boundary from refusing the press that starts one -- and the failure class behind it (PI resolving NXDOMAIN for a period) is exactly why a refusal the operator can retry is safe where an auto-disable was not. REJECTED: enable-then-auto-halt (needs halt semantics, a re-enable path nobody asked for, and cuts against T19's own reasoning). REJECTED: insert-but-do-not-dispatch (leaves 48h of PENDING rows whose policy T20 has not settled).
tasks.result_2026_09_16: COMPLETED. THIS TASK'S HEADLINE PREMISE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE, verified against the code rather than against the prose: 'ENABLING A SCHEDULE WITH AN UNREACHABLE SOURCE INSERTS UP TO 48 HOURS OF WINDOWS' -- IT INSERTS NONE. putScheduleService ends in a single inferenceSchedule.upsert and inserts no InferenceWindow rows on any path; the 48h backfill is minted later by the scheduler tick's insertDueWindows (inference-window-scheduler.service.ts, INFERENCE_BACKFILL_HORIZON_HOURS at its own line). The measured OUTCOME T19 recorded (70 FAILED windows, none ever spawning a container) is real -- the refusal prevents the tick from ever reaching that schedule. This changed V18's assertion; see V18. SECOND PREMISE CORRECTION: the task says putScheduleService has FOUR enable-time refusals. It has EIGHT (no PRODUCTION version, derivedFromTarget, targetScaled, no featureColumns, dataset not found, ambiguous sourceId, no fetch config, warnSd>=criticalSd) -- the feature's own 2026-09-14 implementation note already enumerated eight. The probe is the NINTH. IMPLEMENTATION: schema.prisma gains preflightAt/preflightOk/preflightReason on InferenceSchedule (migration 20260916100000_model_serve_001_t25_inference_schedule_preflight), all three NULLABLE with NO BACKFILL -- preflightOk=NULL means NOT PROBED, which carries every pre-existing live schedule across the migration without asserting an observation nobody made. T15's probe is REUSED, not duplicated: new ModelInputStatusAuthorizedService.preflightSourceService wraps getInputStatusService, which gained an optional sourceIdOverride so the probe hits the source the CALLER chose rather than the one already on the row (resolveSourceId reads the existing schedule, which on a first enable does not exist and on a source change is stale). ModelVersionModule now exports the service and InferenceWindowModule imports it; direction stays acyclic (InferenceWindow -> ModelVersion -> DataSource). ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: evidence is written first and the throw second, so a failed probe never reaches the upsert -- no window in which a schedule is enabled while its own preflight says it should not be, and no transaction spanning a throw. On a FIRST enable that fails, no schedule row is created at all (update, not upsert), so T20's sweep inherits no disabled ghost. SQL SOURCES ARE NOT PROBED (user decision, 2026-09-16): input-status accepts PI only (data-source.connect.service.ts rejects src.type !== 'aveva') and sql_connect.py binds the time range as VARCHAR, so a SQL probe would fail for a CONNECTOR defect rather than the operator's config. FLAGGED, NOT FIXED, as this task instructs. Such a schedule enables with preflightOk=null. preflightReason stores the connector's text VERBATIM via the unavailableReason path (diagnose_empty_pi_fetch); redaction stays at the READ boundary with lib/redact-urls.ts, as T09 did for failureReason, so server logs keep full evidence. FOUND AND FIXED AFTER REVIEW, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL IMPLEMENTATION: the probe was initially run on EVERY enabled:true call, but that path also serves a PARTIAL SETTINGS UPDATE on a live schedule (what T09's merge logic above it exists for). A thirty-second PI blip while an operator nudged a threshold would then refuse the update AND write preflightOk:false to a row that stays enabled:true and whose windows keep succeeding -- pinning a demonstrably working model to Failed until someone happened to re-enable it successfully. That is the 'deployStatus asserts something untrue' defect T12's module exists to remove, re-introduced through a new field, and it crosses the line T25's own openDecision drew (refusing the press that STARTS a schedule is in scope; condemning one already RUNNING is the auto-pause T19 decided against). The probe and all three evidence writes are now scoped to the OFF -> ON transition via the `wasEnabled` flag stampDeployed already uses; a settings update omits the three fields entirely rather than overwriting a real observation with a probe that never ran. Pinned by its own regression test.

tasks.title: Running is sticky: move fetch faults AND staleness off the deploy axis in one pass
tasks.detail:
After preflight passes, the deploy axis leaves 'initializing' permanently and only Offline can take it out of Running -- operator Stop, no PRODUCTION version, or no schedule row. 'error' becomes reachable only during preflight (T25). Everything about the DATA moves to the monitoring axis (T27).

THE SINGLE LARGEST RISK IN THIS WHOLE FEATURE, STATED PLAINLY: staleness -> 'error' is TODAY THE ONLY SIGNAL that the monitoring record has stopped being written. MODEL-SERVE-006-T10 is labelled 'DO NOT CUT THIS TASK' for exactly this, in its own words: 'A drift dashboard with no incoming data looks calm, and calm is exactly the wrong signal.' If Running persists and staleness is not re-homed in the SAME pass, both axes read healthy while the scheduler is dead -- strictly worse than today. Do not split this task from its staleness half.

CALL isStale(lastWindowStart, cadenceMinutes, lagMinutes), which already exists in lib/deploy-status.ts. T11 extracted it precisely because the same computation was duplicated inline in deriveDeployStatuses and getStatusService and would have read a merely-slow model as 'error' after the dispatch-timing fix. Do not write a third staleness formula.

NOT IN SCOPE: SKIPPED's own semantics or its relationship to the alarm (settled by T01/T10, re-affirmed by T11), the connector's error text, INFERENCE_BACKFILL_HORIZON_HOURS.
openDecisions: WHERE DOES STALENESS LIVE? RECOMMENDED: Monitoring = Alert with reason STALE. Monitoring Offline should mean DELIBERATELY NOT WATCHING (schedule disabled, or driftMonitor false); collapsing 'the operator turned it off' and 'the record died' into one value is the same one-control-two-facts defect T19 Part B had to close when the Start/Stop toggle was bound to a derived value. REJECTED: Monitoring = Offline (dresses a fault as an intention, which is the failure this whole task exists to prevent). REJECTED: keep it on Deploy = Failed (contradicts the Running-always requirement).
tasks.result_2026_09_16: COMPLETED, INCLUDING ITS STALENESS HALF -- not split, per this task's own instruction. DEPLOY AXIS: classifyDeployStatus's body is now !enabled -> 'stopped'; preflightOk===false -> 'error' (the ONLY remaining path to error); preflightOk===null && !hasEverSucceeded -> 'initializing'; otherwise 'running'. staleness/failing/hasFailedWindows are gone from its input. Running is sticky: a probed schedule reads running from the press. hasFailedWindows was REMOVED from getStatusService and failingByModel/hasFailedByModel from deriveDeployStatuses rather than left computed-but-unread, so no reader has to guess which axis they still belong to. deriveDeployStatuses widens its EXISTING schedule SELECT with preflightOk -- same query, same round trip. MONITORING AXIS (a minimal T27 slice, pulled forward by user decision 2026-09-16 because V19 asserts a reason this axis could not express): HealthStatus gains 'ALERT'; new HealthReason = 'SOURCE_UNREACHABLE' | 'STALE'; classifyModelHealth now takes one object and returns {status, reason}. Three consecutive FAILED windows -> ALERT/SOURCE_UNREACHABLE; isStale() -> ALERT/STALE. isStale is CALLED, not copied -- T11 extracted it precisely so a third formula would not appear; it changed axes, it did not fork. ONE JUDGEMENT CALL, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS NOT IN EITHER TASK'S TEXT: fetch faults and staleness are NOT gated behind driftMonitor, though drift is. driftMonitor DEFAULTS TO FALSE, so gating liveness behind it would leave every schedule that never opted into drift watching reading OFF while its source was down -- reinstating the exact calm-dashboard blindness MODEL-SERVE-006-T10 forbids, for the majority of models. driftMonitor governs whether this system WATCHES FOR DRIFT; it was never a claim about whether windows are arriving. OFF therefore keeps its single meaning (deliberately not watching: schedule disabled, or drift off with no fault), and staleness is never routed to OFF. New private resolveLivenessFaults on InferenceWindowMonitoringService counts a genuine TRAILING run of FAILED windows (stops at the first non-FAILED), and does NOT count SKIPPED -- T01/T10/T11 all hold that SKIPPED is legitimate for a quiet plant; a consecutive SKIPPED run is T27's NO_PREDICTIONS, with its own code. CLIENT: HEALTH_CONFIG (models/[id]/page.tsx) gains ALERT -- MANDATORY, since its read site has no ?? fallback and an unlisted status would render undefined and throw. Reason rendered beside it via HEALTH_REASON_LABEL, on screen rather than inferred. Drift palette, not the deploy red/amber vocabulary. InferenceStatus.health on the client gains 'ALERT' and reason. TWO THINGS FOUND AFTER REVIEW, BOTH REGRESSIONS THIS PASS WOULD OTHERWISE HAVE SHIPPED. (1) FALSE ALARM ON EVERY FRESH ENABLE, caught by a failing fixture rather than reasoned about in advance: isStale(null, ...) returns STALE by its own documented refusal-direction rule, so a schedule enabled ten seconds ago -- which has produced nothing YET by construction -- read ALERT/STALE immediately. classifyModelHealth now takes hasEverSucceeded and only alarms STALE when the record actually STOPPED, which presupposes it ever started; the deploy axis already says 'initializing' for the warm-up. DECLARED RESIDUAL GAP: a schedule that passes preflight and then never produces a single window reads UNKNOWN forever rather than ALERT. Closing that needs a clock this function does not have (time since enable, against cadences) -- that is T28's stale-cadence threshold, and it was NOT guessed at here. (2) THE LIST PATH WENT SILENT. deriveDeployStatuses lost failing/hasFailedWindows, so a model with three failed windows returned status:'running' and nothing else -- and the Alerts page plus the workspace failure counts key on deployStatus==='error' through isDeployFailed (client lib/model-status.ts). Moving fetch faults off the deploy axis therefore displaced the very blindness this task exists to prevent from the detail page onto the list. DeployState now carries `monitoring: ModelHealth`, computed from rows deriveDeployStatuses ALREADY fetches (the take-3 terminal sample and lastSucceededAt) -- no new query, no N+1 -- and overlayDeployStatus carries it onto the list payload. Drift is deliberately NOT evaluated on that path (it needs a per-model baseline read, the exact per-model request the batched derivation exists to avoid), so the list's monitoring value carries LIVENESS ONLY and its OFF means 'no fault, no claim'. THE CLIENT HALF OF THIS IS NOT DONE -- see T30.

tasks.title: Monitoring classifier: five states, each carrying a reason code
tasks.detail:
Widen classifyModelHealth (T21 -- already returns OFF/UNKNOWN/OK/WARN/CRITICAL) to Normal / Warning / Alert / Sensor Frozen / Offline.

EVERY STATE CARRIES A REASON CODE, BECAUSE Alert COLLAPSES TWO FAULTS WITH OPPOSITE ACTIONS: SOURCE_UNREACHABLE / TAG_MISSING / NO_PREDICTIONS / STALE send a reader to the connector; DRIFT_CRITICAL sends them to the process or to a retrain. Collapsing them into one word is what T16 refused when it declined to put PSI in the z-score's table -- and the reason must be on screen, not inferred at read time (the pipelineVersion-with-a-default defect DS-LAKE-022-T03 records).

INPUTS, ALL ALREADY ON THE ROW: fetch faults from InferenceWindow.status + failureReason; structural tag-missing should have been caught by T25, so what remains here is Bad cells, which surface as missingPct on the window row (T05) -- never open parquet for this; drift from computeDrift + computePsi with thresholds from thresholdsFromSchedule (T21), never from env.

THREE RULES THIS LEDGER HAS ALREADY SETTLED AND THIS TASK MAY NOT BREAK.
(1) SKIPPED IS NOT AN ALERT. T01/T10/T11 each state that it is a legitimate terminal status for a quiet plant and must neither raise nor suppress the alarm. Count only a CONSECUTIVE RUN (>=3) as Alert with reason NO_PREDICTIONS; T11 already added windowsSkipped to the coverage payload.
(2) PSI's UNKNOWN AND INSUFFICIENT_DATA MUST NEVER FOLD INTO Normal. psiRefEdges are computed at GOLD-write time only, and T17 confirmed LIVE that TM2's spec is featureVersion 2 with no edges at all -- so an Alert path built on PSI today SHIPS DARK AND REPORTS HEALTHY. Check this before anything else in this task.
(3) ONE UNKNOWN COLUMN MUST NOT MASK ANOTHER COLUMN'S CRITICAL. prediction-drift.spec.ts already pins this for the drift rollup; the five-state rollup must preserve it.

CADENCES DIFFER -- z is per-window, PSI is rolling 24 windows (T16/T17) -- so the card must name WHICH metric fired and over WHAT window. DO NOT MINT A SINGLE MERGED DRIFT FIGURE: that is one metric wearing another's name.

PROPOSED PRECEDENCE: Offline > Alert > Sensor Frozen > Warning > Normal, with the card free to show several reasons at once. A frozen tag makes its own drift figure a measurement of nothing, so Alert leads while the per-tag badge stays.

RECORDED, NOT FIXED HERE: the z-score baseline is column_stats over the WHOLE artifact rather than the train split, so it under-flags systematically (T13), and psiReference carries the identical exposure. Fix both baselines together in any future pass or the two metrics diverge on this point silently.
tasks.note_2026_09_16: SCOPE REDUCED BY T26, 2026-09-16. Already shipped by that task and NOT to be re-implemented: HealthStatus's 'ALERT' value, the HealthReason type, classifyModelHealth's object signature returning {status, reason}, and the two codes SOURCE_UNREACHABLE (>=3 consecutive trailing FAILED windows) and STALE (isStale). Also already settled there: SKIPPED is NOT counted as a failure, and fetch faults/staleness are NOT gated behind driftMonitor while drift IS -- see T26's result for why (driftMonitor defaults false). STILL OPEN HERE: Sensor Frozen (needs T29), TAG_MISSING, NO_PREDICTIONS from a consecutive SKIPPED run, DRIFT_CRITICAL, and rule (2)'s PSI dark-ship guard -- check psiRefEdges BEFORE anything else, T17 confirmed live that TM2's spec is featureVersion 2 with no edges.
tasks.result_2026_09_16: COMPLETED. classifyModelHealth now grades Offline > Alert > Sensor Frozen > Warning > Normal, every graded state carrying a reason code. WIRE VALUES ARE ADDED, NEVER RENAMED. T27 describes five states; those are DISPLAY LABELS. The enum gained 'FROZEN' only -- OK/WARN/CRITICAL/ALERT/OFF/UNKNOWN keep their spellings, because T22 spent a whole task repairing three client maps that keyed on a renamed value and fell through a ?? to green, and T24 froze the deploy enum for the same reason. Labels: OK->Normal, WARN->Warning, ALERT->Alert, FROZEN->'Sensor Frozen', OFF->Offline. 'CRITICAL' REMAINS IN THE UNION BUT IS NO LONGER PRODUCED -- a drift CRITICAL now surfaces as ALERT + reason DRIFT_CRITICAL, which is what T27 asks for (the card must name WHICH metric fired: z is per-window, PSI is rolling-24, so one merged figure would be one metric wearing another's name). DELIBERATE ASSERTION CHANGE, recorded the way V19's 'error'->'running' was: model-health.spec.ts's 'passes the drift report status straight through' asserted CRITICAL->CRITICAL and now asserts ALERT/DRIFT_CRITICAL. The client's HEALTH_CONFIG.CRITICAL entry is KEPT: that map has no ?? fallback and deleting an entry a stored payload might still carry is how it throws. 'Sensor Frozen', not 'Frozen', resolving T29's recorded open decision: prodStatus.frozen is operator-set and already renders as 'Data Frozen' with the Snowflake treatment, and two badges on one header both reading 'Frozen' is the two-contradictory-verdicts defect T22 fixed in model-detail-dialog.tsx. Renaming the persisted value was rejected -- a migration plus every map, for the lower-value half. RULE (1), SKIPPED: only a CONSECUTIVE RUN >= skipStreakAlert is NO_PREDICTIONS. `windowsSkipped` (the existing coverage payload) is a COUNT, not a streak, so it was the wrong input. The terminal sample was ALSO widened from a hard-coded take:3 to Math.max(3, skipStreakAlert): against a fixed 3 an operator setting 5 would have had a threshold that could NEVER fire, silently -- the very 'settings that appear to work and may do nothing' defect T21's audit found and T28 exists to prevent. frozenWindows is clamped against the take:24 for the same reason. RULE (2), THE DARK-SHIP GATE, is a REQUIRED `driftEvidence` input rather than an assumption: drift speaks only when the baseline is non-empty AND >=1 window carried featureStats. This matters live, not hypothetically -- `resolveColumnBaseline` returns {} from its SUCCESS path as well as its catch path (indistinguishable downstream), and T17 confirmed today's specs carry no psiRefEdges at all. Without it a model whose column_stats read failed reports healthy. computeDrift's own UNKNOWN also passes through as UNKNOWN, never folded into OK. Liveness faults are still reported when the gate is closed -- it silences the drift CLAIM, not the axis. RULE (3) is preserved: the per-column no-masking rollup is still computeDrift's own, untouched. TAG_MISSING DELIBERATELY NOT IMPLEMENTED, with evidence rather than as an omission: T27 itself says structural absence is T25's preflight's job, and the only signal available here -- a column absent from featureStats -- is AMBIGUOUS, since `_scaled_feature_stats` excludes any tag whose scaler is not 'none' and which has no scalingParams entry, a legitimate state. Emitting it on that signal would report a missing tag for a correctly-configured column. It needs a real per-tag liveness read (T15's probe). BAD_DATA reads the NEWEST terminal window's missingPct, not a rollup -- the band asks 'is the data bad right now', and a rollup disagrees on a plant that just recovered. `missingPct` had to be ADDED to resolveProductionWindows's select; the band would otherwise have had no input at all. `getHealthStatus` was restructured to resolve windows and baseline ONCE for both drift and frozen, and the baseline (an HTTP round trip to apps/python) is fetched only when a window actually carries stats -- which today is never, so this costs nothing extra. frozenColumns rides EVERY status, not just FROZEN: a higher-precedence fault outranks the band without making the instruments un-stuck, per T27's own 'Alert leads while the per-tag badge stays'.
tasks.review_followup_2026_09_16: REVIEW FOLLOW-UP 2026-09-16 (3 fixes after the slice was written). (1) SHAPE BUG, would have been a runtime mismatch: the no-schedule branch of `getStatusService` hand-builds `health: {status:'OFF', reason:null, thresholds:null}` and omitted `frozenColumns`, while the client's `InferenceStatus.health` type now requires it. Backend tsc accepted it because that return type is INFERRED, not annotated — so the client asserted a field the server did not deliver, on the most common shape there is (a model with no schedule row). Now present-and-empty. (2) The `Math.min(schedule.frozenWindows, PRODUCTION_WINDOW_TAKE)` clamp was removed: the `<=24` bound is already owned by the DTO's `.max(24)`, so the clamp was dead code whose comment read like a live guard — and had it ever fired it would have badged frozen off FEWER windows than the operator asked for. `detectFrozenColumns` already returns [] on a short sample, which is the honest answer. (3) TEST THAT PROVED THE WRONG THING: 'is OFF when driftMonitor is false — never fetches a baseline' still passed after the restructuring, but only because its fixture's `findMany` returns [] (statsRows.length === 0 skips the baseline). It proved 'no stats, no baseline', NOT 'monitoring off, no baseline'. Added a case with `driftMonitor:false` AND three real flat `featureStats` windows: asserts the baseline IS fetched, status is FROZEN/SENSOR_FROZEN, and `thresholds` stays null. Negative control: gating the frozen branch behind `driftMonitor` → 1 failed/5 passed; restored → 6 passed. Without this case, re-adding an early return would silently turn Sensor Frozen off for every model that has not opted into drift watching (the majority — `driftMonitor` defaults false) with the whole suite still green. Also widened the client `InferenceSchedule` interface with T28's five threshold fields, which `getScheduleService` already returned. Backend after: 830 passed / 10 pre-existing failures (same set).

tasks.title: The new bands' thresholds belong on InferenceSchedule, not in env
tasks.detail:
T27 needs thresholds that have no home yet: missingPctWarn / missingPctAlert, skipStreakAlert, frozenWindows (default 3), frozenTolerancePct, and the stale-cadence count. Put them on InferenceSchedule beside warnSd / criticalSd / driftThresholdPct, whose home T09 already built.

THE REASON IS MEASURED, NOT AESTHETIC. T14 proved it for INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS: one global constant whose derivation assumed a 1-minute sampling interval, while each schedule carries its own fetchConfig.intervalTime -- a schedule fetching every 5 minutes has 12 rows in a complete, healthy hour and would read SKIPPED forever against a 30-row floor. That is the 'guess wearing a formula' MODEL-FLOW-020's finding 3 names, evaluated against the wrong axis. deriveMinRows + parseIntervalMinutes (lib/inference-windows.ts) are the precedent: parse strictly, return NULL rather than a wrong guess, and fall back to the env default.

MERGE PARTIAL UPDATES SAFELY, as putScheduleService already does for T09's five fields -- updating one must not reset the others. RE-CHECK RELATIONAL CONSTRAINTS (warn < alert) SERVER-SIDE AGAINST THE MERGED STATE: a DTO refine only catches the case where both arrive in one request, which is the exact gap T09 found for warnSd/criticalSd.
tasks.note_2026_09_16: UNCHANGED BY T26, stated so it is not assumed done. T26 introduced NO new configurable threshold: its 3-consecutive-failure bar is the bar the deploy axis already used (deriveDeployStatuses's own `failing` rule), and staleness reuses isStale/INFERENCE_STALE_AFTER_CADENCES. Every field this task names (missingPctWarn/missingPctAlert, skipStreakAlert, frozenWindows, frozenTolerancePct, the stale-cadence count) is still unbuilt. Note that InferenceSchedule gained preflightAt/preflightOk/preflightReason in T25's migration -- those are EVIDENCE fields, not thresholds, and this task's own migration should not disturb them.
tasks.result_2026_09_16: COMPLETED, FIVE OF SIX FIELDS. Migration 20260916120000_model_serve_001_t28_inference_schedule_health_thresholds adds missingPctWarn(5)/missingPctAlert(20)/skipStreakAlert(3)/frozenWindows(3)/frozenTolerancePct(0) to InferenceSchedule, all NOT NULL WITH DEFAULTS -- the opposite of T25's preflight* columns, and deliberately: these are SETTINGS, so every existing schedule has a correct value the moment it applies, whereas a default for an OBSERVATION would assert a probe nobody ran. frozenTolerancePct is `.nonnegative()` in the DTO, NOT `.positive()` like its sibling driftThresholdPct -- 0 is this field's own default AND its most meaningful value (exact flatness, the only scale-invariant threshold available without reference to a column's training spread), so copying the sibling's validator would have made the default unsettable. Plumbed on T09's exact path: `.optional()` on the `.strict()` schema (omitting that step would make any request carrying them fail outright), a `dto.X ?? existing?.X ?? default` merge so a partial update does not reset the other four, a second `.refine` for warn<alert, and -- the part the refine cannot do -- a SERVER-SIDE re-check of missingPctWarn < missingPctAlert against the MERGED state, closing the same gap T09 found for warnSd/criticalSd. Both checks are pinned by their own tests. Echoed by getScheduleService in BOTH branches with the same defaults the schema and the merge use, never a second set. NOT BUILT, THE SIXTH FIELD: the stale-cadence count. Staleness already works through env.INFERENCE_STALE_AFTER_CADENCES inside `isStale`, and per-scheduling it means changing that function's signature and every caller for no behaviour this slice needs. It is the one field of T28's six still open, and it is also what would close classifyModelHealth's declared never-produced-forever gap. NO CLIENT EDITOR THIS PASS, stated rather than left to be discovered: these are API-settable and read back by getScheduleService, but the only surface that edits the T09 five is the create wizard's Step 6, and operational thresholds do not belong on a creation screen. Adding them there would also have made a SIXTH place the default set is written (service merge, getScheduleService's no-row branch, the atoms, use-model-wizard-mode's hydration).

tasks.title: Sensor Frozen from featureStats over three windows, badged per tag
tasks.detail:
THE FIT THAT MAKES THIS TASK CHEAP: deriveDeployStatuses already reads the last THREE terminal windows per model (T23 widened that same select to carry failureReason -- same query, same rows, same round trip), and featureStats (n/sum/sumsq/min/max per column, SCALED units) is already a column on InferenceWindow (T17). Three windows at a 60m cadence IS the three-hour span requested. No new query.

DEFINITION: per column, pooled range = max(max) - min(min) across the last three windows carrying featureStats; frozen when range <= eps.

FOUR GUARDS, NONE OPTIONAL.
(1) A TAG THAT WAS ALREADY FLAT IN TRAINING -- a setpoint, a valve held closed -- would badge frozen forever. Skip any column whose column_stats.std is at or near zero before computing anything.
(2) DEFINE IT IN WINDOWS, NOT ROWS. T14 proved a global row count is the wrong axis because each schedule has its own fetchConfig.intervalTime (a 5m interval makes three hours 36 rows, not 180). '3 rows / 3 hr' therefore reads as three consecutive windows.
(3) eps IS A FRACTION OF THE TRAINING RANGE, NOT A CONSTANT. featureStats are scaled by the FROZEN scalingParams, so range == 0 is exact and scale-invariant while any other value must be expressed against the training range. T17 confirmed live that a scaled value can go NEGATIVE when a window falls outside the trained range (AI001A2.PV at ~-1.17) -- do not assume [0,1].
(4) REQUIRE A MINIMUM n PER WINDOW, or a one-row window reads flat by construction.

PAYLOAD: have python compute a compact constantColumns: string[] inside materialize_window -- _scaled_feature_stats already holds the frame and already computes min/max -- and pool three windows backend-side. Cheaper than dragging ~2KB of featureStats jsonb x 3 x every model on the list. USEFUL SIDE EFFECT: a SKIPPED window carries featureStats too (put_frame runs before the minRows check, confirmed live in T17), so a thin-but-stuck plant is still caught.
openDecisions: THE WORD COLLIDES WITH prodStatus.frozen. RECOMMENDED: name the monitoring value 'Sensor Frozen' (or 'Stale Tags'). prodStatus.frozen is OPERATOR-SET (T21 confirmed prodStatus stays writable), already renders with the Snowflake treatment in PROD_CONFIG, and T22 has just added it to PROD_MAP -- renaming a persisted value buys nothing. REJECTED: keep both words and disambiguate by axis label -- two badges on one header reading 'Frozen' and 'Data Frozen' is the same two-contradictory-verdicts-in-one-view defect T22 had to fix in model-detail-dialog.tsx. REJECTED: rename prodStatus.frozen (a migration plus every map, for the lower-value half).
tasks.result_2026_09_16: COMPLETED as a pure backend module, `apps/backend/src/lib/sensor-frozen.ts` + co-located spec (the pure-function-plus-spec shape its 13 siblings in lib/ follow). USER DECISION 2026-09-16: computed BACKEND-SIDE from the featureStats already on the row -- no Python change, no migration, no new column. T29's proposed `constantColumns` payload was a LIST-PATH cost optimisation and the list path is T30's scope; featureStats already carries per-column min/max (`_column_aggregate`), so the pooled range needs nothing new. FINDING THAT CHANGED THE IMPLEMENTATION: `poolFeatureStats` (lib/prediction-drift.ts) CANNOT be reused here. It takes GLOBAL extremes across every window handed to it, and its caller pools the standard take:24 -- pooling 24 windows destroys the very signal this needs (a tag still for three hours is invisible inside a day of movement) and discards each window's own `n`, which guard (4) depends on. This module pools its own small slice and keeps per-window identity. FIVE GUARDS, each pinned by a V21 case and each proven by negative control: (1) skip any column whose baseline.std is ~0 -- flat in TRAINING; (2) windows, not rows (T14's axis argument); (3) eps = frozenTolerancePct * (p99-p1) from the baseline, in scaled units, so the same setting means the same thing on a tag spanning 0.01 and one spanning 400 -- and NOT assuming [0,1], since T17 measured a real scaled -1.17; (4) a minimum n per window; (5) an ABSENT column is skipped, never read as flat. GUARD (4)'s FLOOR IS 2, NOT `minRows`, AND THIS IS LOAD-BEARING. `minRows` IS the SKIPPED threshold, so a minRows floor would discard every SKIPPED window and destroy T29's own stated side effect ('a SKIPPED window carries featureStats too ... so a thin-but-stuck plant is still caught'). Two points is the minimum that can have a range at all, which is the whole of guard (4)'s stated concern. The reasoning is in the module's doc comment so it is not 'tidied' back. ONE MORE REFUSAL ADDED: a non-zero tolerance against a baseline with no percentile range returns null and SKIPS the column rather than falling back to 0 -- falling back would silently apply a STRICTER rule than the operator configured. VERIFIED BY UNIT TEST ONLY, AND THIS IS A REAL LIMIT, NOT A FORMALITY: all 76 live InferenceWindow rows carry featureStats = NULL. Not a broken writer -- the last SUCCEEDED window is 2026-09-14 09:00 and T17's migration is 20260915110000, so no window has succeeded since the column existed. The frozen path cannot be demonstrated end-to-end until a schedule runs successfully, and the writer itself stays unproven live.

tasks.title: Feed frozen tags, drift and fetch faults into alerts.ts
tasks.detail:
buildAlerts IS A PURE FUNCTION OVER THE MODELS LIST, so any new signal must ride the list payload or one page becomes N requests. T23 already solved this shape by carrying lastFailure on DeployState, sourced from the existing take-3 terminal-window query. Do the same: constantColumns (T29) and the monitoring status plus reason (T27) come up through deriveDeployStatuses.

acceptance_criteria: Save Model produces exactly one ModelVersion at STAGING and no PRODUCTION version.
Two concurrent promotes against one model cannot both leave a PRODUCTION row — enforced by the database, proven by a concurrent test rather than by reading the service.

Promoting a version whose object is missing or whose checksum does not match fails and leaves the current PRODUCTION untouched.
A ModelVersion row's artifact pointer, checksum and metrics are never updated after creation.

verification.description: Fire two promotes concurrently against different versions of one model and confirm exactly one PRODUCTION row survives. Sequential promotes would pass a weaker test while leaving the race entirely uncovered — the constraint this feature adds exists for the concurrent case.
verification.result_2026_09_01: LIVE-PROVEN against the real dev DB, at the SQL level rather than through the NestJS/auth stack (no backend server was running to exercise HTTP end to end; the actual mechanism under test — the partial unique index — is a DB-level guarantee, so a real concurrent DB test proves the acceptance criterion directly). Seeded one Model with two STAGING ModelVersions under two real ModelTrainingRun rows. Two concurrent `psql` sessions each opened a transaction and updated a DIFFERENT version to `stage='PRODUCTION'`, staggered so both UPDATEs landed before either committed. Observed: transaction A's UPDATE succeeded and committed; transaction B's UPDATE BLOCKED (Postgres's standard behavior for a value that might conflict with an uncommitted row), then on A's commit failed immediately with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "ModelVersion_one_production_per_model"` and rolled back. Final state queried: exactly one PRODUCTION row (version-1), version-2 untouched at STAGING. This is precisely the P2002-on-that-constraint-name path `ModelVersionAuthorizedService`'s `promote()` catches and maps to a 409. Test rows cleaned up via `DELETE FROM "Model"` (cascades) — which also re-confirmed T01's FK fix live a second time.

PROVE THE DRIFT REFERENCE IS THE TRAINING DISTRIBUTION, NOT THE WINDOW'S OWN. Feed a window whose values are shifted well away from the recorded training statistics and assert the drift figure MOVES; then feed a window drawn from the training distribution and assert it does not. A self-referential metric -- computed against the current window's own mean and spread -- returns near-zero for BOTH and looks like a working stable signal, which is the exact failure this item exists to catch. Assert separately that sigma is a real recorded value and not a default: DS-LAKE's own record has median/std silently stripped at a response boundary once already, and a z-score with a defaulted denominator is a number with no meaning rather than a weak one.

RESOLVED 2026-09-14. Two new regression tests added to the EXISTING prediction-drift.spec.ts (apps/backend/src/lib/), which already covered most of this item's ground from MODEL-SERVE-005-T02 -- this closed the remaining gap rather than duplicating it. First test: an 8-training-SD shift against a literal, live-independent baseline fixture moves z past CRITICAL; the SAME fixed baseline against matching values keeps z within 1e-5 of zero -- the two cases together are the proof requested, and the baseline object's construction (no reference into the live population at all) is itself the evidence against self-reference. Second test: a null-std and a zero-std baseline both produce `z: null` (asserted directly, not inferred from the status string) with a named reason -- sigma degrades to "no meaningful number", never a fabricated denominator. 15/15 passing, run fresh this session.

PROVE PSI CATCHES WHAT THE Z-SCORE CANNOT, AND THAT THE BINS ARE FROZEN. Construct a window with the SAME MEAN as the reference but a different shape (bimodal, or a materially wider spread) and assert the z-score stays low while PSI rises -- if both move, or neither does, the fixture does not demonstrate the reason for the swap and proves nothing about it. Then assert the bin edges used for that window are byte-identical to the ones recorded at training time: re-binning per window makes the metric measure the binner, the same contamination the shared-bucket-basis rule (DS-LAKE-005B-A-V06) exists to prevent for the before/after scrubber. Record the measured PSI at the real per-window row count, and if that count makes the figure unstable, say so rather than reporting the number.

tasks.title: Multi-model loader with a bounded cache
tasks.detail_addendum: REVISED 2026-08-24: verify model_sha256 (the field name is now known, not hypothesised) and verify image_digest against the serving runtime — noting that a digest match is not achievable if serving runs a DIFFERENT image from the trainer, which decisions.training_and_serving_are_separate_planes deliberately requires. So the digest is a provenance record to CHECK FOR PRESENCE and log, not a value to match. What must actually be validated at load is that the serving runtime's own library versions are compatible with the pickle; the digest tells you what to go and look up when they are not.
tasks.detail: Resolve model_id -> PRODUCTION version -> object; verify checksum; verify the recorded framework version against the runtime and REFUSE on a mismatch rather than warn (see findings — a silently-loaded mismatch produces plausible wrong numbers). Cache bounded by memory, not by entry count: models differ in size by orders of magnitude and a count-based cap sizes for the smallest one.
tasks.audit_2026_09_01: MODEL-SERVE-000 found the loader must also resolve scaler state alongside the model object — read feature_spec.json's scalingParams via ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey (one hop, verified non-null on 73/73 runs) at the same load step, and resolve each tag's method the way to_model_ready does (scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER)), never by checking whether the spec's `scaling` array is non-empty — see the empty-`scaling`-array trap finding, which is real and specific to this task.
tasks.result_2026_09_02: apps/backend GET /authorized/serving/models/:modelId/descriptor (new model-serving module, ServingTokenGuard shared-secret auth) resolves PRODUCTION version -> presigned model URL + checksum + featureColumns (from run_manifest.json) + scalers/scalingParams (from feature_spec.json, resolved via scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER) per the empty-scaling-array finding, never by branching on scaling's emptiness) + frameworkVersions + imageDigest. apps/serving/services/loader.py (ModelLoader) downloads -> sha256-verifies (refuses on mismatch, honest-legacy-null on absent) -> checks frameworkVersions against the runtime (refuses on mismatch, warns on absent) -> joblib.load, in a bytes-bounded LRU keyed by (modelId, versionId). Live-verified: V01 (correct load + correct predict) and V04 (tampered checksum genuinely refused with both hashes named in the error) both ran against real Postgres + MinIO + a real fitted model, not synthetic fixtures. A real gap was found and fixed along the way: a network failure during download reached the caller as an unhandled 500 (violating LoadError's own stated invariant) — _download now wraps requests.RequestException as LoadError, unit-tested via a real unreachable-port connection failure.
