What was built: (1) `max_replay_lookback` (with `feature_column_name`/`_reads_tags`/`_own_lookback`) moved out of apps/python into softsensor_scaling.features — the same extract-and-switch-the-caller-in-one-change pattern T05 used; apps/python imports them back under their original names, so artifact_service.py:95/533 and tests/test_feature_spec_quirks.py are untouched, and apps/python's full suite stayed green with only its 3 known pre-existing failures. (2) The backend descriptor now passes the recipe through as `features`, FLATTENED from feature_spec.json's `{name, kind, config}` nesting into the top-level shape max_replay_lookback reads (the shape apps/python already feeds it) — flattened in the backend rather than re-modelled, and NOT reimplemented in TypeScript, so one implementation of 'how deep does this recipe reach back' exists, not two. (3) apps/serving's `required_history_rows` computes that depth from the descriptor with that same shared function, and the target-derived refusal now names both WHICH history columns are missing and HOW MANY consecutive prior observations the recipe reaches back over — the half a bare presence check leaves a caller unable to act on. An absent or unreadable recipe reports depth 0 and omits the sentence rather than fabricating a number; depth is advisory context on a refusal, never itself a gate, so an unparseable recipe cannot turn a satisfiable request into a 500. Tests: 8 new package tests (compounding, independent-chain, datetime-reads-nothing, naming, unknown-kind) + 6 new serving tests including V03's fabricated fixture + 2 new backend descriptor tests for the flattening. Suites after: package 14/14, apps/serving 25/25, apps/backend 496 passed with the same 9 pre-existing failing suites, apps/python 809 passed with the same 3 pre-existing failures.

tasks.title: Invalidate the cache on promote
tasks.result_2026_09_02: Contract chosen, implemented, and LIVE-PROVEN under continuous load (V02: 90/90 requests succeeded, switchover at t=30.44s against a promote at t=5.25s, both consistent with the 30s TTL). services/descriptor.py caches descriptors with a 30s TTL (decisions.serving_cache_staleness_bound) and offers invalidate(); services/loader.py's ModelLoader.invalidate() exists but nothing calls it on a promote webhook yet — the bound today is TTL-driven only, never sooner than the TTL. Remaining work, if the bound is ever tightened below 30s: wire a promote-triggered invalidate() call (webhook or poll) instead of relying on TTL expiry alone.
tasks.detail: After a promote, replicas holding the old version keep serving it until something tells them. Whatever the mechanism (a short TTL on the version lookup is the cheapest and is probably enough), the CONTRACT is what matters: state the maximum time a promoted version can take to become live, and make it a number someone chose rather than an emergent property. Silent divergence between two replicas answering the same request differently is very hard to diagnose from the outside.

acceptance_criteria: A promoted model answers /predict with no image rebuild and no redeploy.
A request missing a required column is refused with that column named — not a 500 from the estimator.
A model whose feature spec is target-derived cannot be served without target history, and the refusal states why.
The transform applied at inference is the SAME CODE as the one applied at training, not an equivalent one.
A checksum or framework-version mismatch prevents a load; it never degrades to a warning.
/healthz does not depend on MinIO or Postgres; /readyz does.
After a promote, every replica serves the new version within the stated bound.

verification.description: PROVE NO SKEW, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT: take a row from the model's own test split, send it through /predict, and assert the prediction matches the value in that run's predictions artifact to numerical tolerance. Any test using synthetic input proves the endpoint returns a float, which is not the claim. This is the V02-of-MODEL-FLOW-000 of this ledger — the one verification whose absence would make everything else look fine.
verification.result_2026_09_02: RAN LIVE against real Postgres + MinIO + a real fitted OLS model (run cd2db914-3bb4-4abb-a305-9f3ae19eb50d). Seeded a test Model+PRODUCTION ModelVersion, read real feature rows from the run's own SILVER artifact (corrected mid-implementation: SILVER is pre-scale, GOLD is already scaled — see the 2026-09-02 GOLD-is-scaled finding) for timestamps present in the run's own predictions.parquet, POSTed them through the live /predict, and compared to the recorded y_pred. n=20: max diff 0.0. n=1000: max diff 2.66e-15 (float noise, effectively bit-exact). Script: scripts/verify/model_serve_002_v01.py. Test rows cleaned up after.

verification.description: Promote a new version while /predict is under continuous load and confirm every response is answerable by SOME valid version, with the switchover inside the stated bound and no request failing at the boundary.
verification.result_2026_09_02: RAN LIVE against real Postgres + apps/serving (no --reload, exact PIDs tracked, to eliminate any file-watcher restart hazard during the timed window). Seeded a Model with two real ModelVersions (v1 PRODUCTION on run cd2db914, v2 STAGING on run 5b9ec2f7 — a genuinely different fitted model, same feature_spec_key so one request row validates against both), polled /predict every 0.5s for 45s (90 requests total), and 5s in ran the same stage transition promote() performs (old PRODUCTION -> ARCHIVED, new -> PRODUCTION) directly against the DB. Result: 90/90 requests returned HTTP 200 — zero failures anywhere, including across the switchover boundary. Last v1 response at t=29.92s, first v2 response at t=30.44s, promote landed at t=5.25s — consistent with the 30s descriptor-cache TTL (decisions.serving_cache_staleness_bound), which is the mechanism actually providing the bound today (see T07 — no explicit invalidate() is wired to promote yet). Script: scripts/verify/model_serve_002_v02.py. Test rows cleaned up after.

verification.description: Load a model whose feature spec declares a non-empty derived_from_target and confirm a history-less request is refused. Then submit history at the WRONG sampling interval and confirm it is also refused — a serving process that accepts the second has not implemented this task, only half of it.
verification.note_2026_09_02: SUPERSEDED, PRESERVED: 'HALF DONE, HALF BLOCKED (not merely unrun) ... Wrong-sampling-interval: CANNOT run — the check itself cannot be built without first deciding the request contract for target-derived models. Decision needed: should /predict accept a timestamped history sequence for target-derived models (a request-shape change), or is presence-only sufficient given zero real models in this class today?'
verification.result_2026_09_02: COMPLETED against a fabricated target-derived fixture, as this verification's own text anticipates it must be (0 of 21 live specs have derived_from_target). The fixture is the COMPOUNDING case on purpose — 'lag 3 of the target, then a rolling(12) mean of that lag' — whose true depth is 15, a number a non-compounding implementation would silently under-report as 12; that is asserted directly. Proven: (a) a history-less request is refused, with the message naming both the missing column and the 15-observation depth; (b) a request carrying the full history columns is accepted; (c) a BATCH where only one row omits the column is still refused (one good row does not excuse another that would predict from an absent lag); (d) a descriptor with no recipe reports depth 0 and omits the depth sentence rather than fabricating one; (e) an unreadable recipe does not turn a satisfiable request into a 500. The second half of this verification's original text — 'submit history at the WRONG sampling interval and confirm it is also refused' — is RETIRED, not skipped, and not silently dropped: see the premise-correction finding dated 2026-09-02. In short, the interval is not the axis this system validates on; the recipe's compound ROW depth is, and that is what both this guard and prepare_holdout_for_run now refuse on, via one shared function.

verification.description: Point the loader at an object whose bytes have been altered and confirm the load fails on checksum rather than succeeding.
verification.result_2026_09_02: RAN LIVE against the real backend descriptor endpoint and real MinIO-hosted model bytes: seeded a PRODUCTION ModelVersion with a deliberately corrupted modelChecksum (real one confirmed first, then a byte-flipped copy written to the DB), hit the live /predict, got HTTP 422 with both the expected and actual sha256 named in the error — the model was never loaded. A genuine bug was found and fixed in the process: a transport failure during download (e.g. presigned host unreachable) was reaching the caller as an unhandled 500 instead of a mapped error; apps/serving/services/loader.py's _download now wraps requests.RequestException as LoadError, covered by a new unit test (test_download_network_failure_becomes_load_error) using a real unreachable port. Full apps/serving suite: 19/19 passed after the fix. Test row cleaned up after.

features.title: Batch Prediction and Job Results
features.description: Score a parquet input in object storage as an asynchronous job, and return the result by reference. This is the '/predict + /result' pair from the original question, split because they are two different operations.

tasks.title: PredictionJob entity and its state machine
tasks.detail: QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELED, mirroring ModelTrainingRun's vocabulary rather than inventing a parallel one. State in Postgres, never in process memory — MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's stranded run is the demonstration of what in-memory job tracking does across a restart, and a result endpoint answering 404 for a job that finished is the same bug with a friendlier face. RESULT 2026-09-02: PredictionJob + PredictionJobStatus (fifth copy of the 5-value vocabulary) added to schema.prisma, hand-written migration for the partial unique index (modelId, idempotencyKey) WHERE idempotencyKey IS NOT NULL. Applied via db:migrate:deploy, table confirmed live via psql.

tasks.title: POST /predict:batch with an idempotency key
tasks.detail: Returns a job id immediately. The idempotency key is not optional: MODEL-FLOW-003-T09 had to add poll-failure tolerance specifically because a transient error pushed users toward a retry that would spawn a SECOND container against the same draft. A batch endpoint without a key has the identical hole and the same trigger. RESULT 2026-09-02: idempotencyKey in the DTO body (not a header — zero precedent for @Headers in this codebase). Submit: create -> P2002 caught by constraint name -> fall back to reading the winner's row. LIVE-VERIFIED under genuine concurrent submission (V02) after fixing a real bug found in that same test — see the P2002-shape finding below.

tasks.title: Batch worker, chunked
tasks.detail: Stream the input rather than loading it whole. MODEL-FLOW-010-V03 exists because a single unbounded read at 8,000 tags produced 76MB where 489KB was needed; a batch scorer is the most likely place for that to reappear, and it will reappear on someone else's data, not in a test. RESULT 2026-09-02: images/trainer/app/pipelines/batch.py streams the input via pq.ParquetFile(...).iter_batches(batch_size=50_000, columns=feature_columns) + incremental pq.ParquetWriter, mirroring export_service.py's BATCH_ROWS precedent. LIVE-VERIFIED twice: (1) in-container smoke test, 130K vs 1.5M rows, peak RSS 220.6MB -> 244.2MB despite 11.5x more data; (2) real end-to-end run through the actual backend+container+MinIO with an 8M-row / 1.19GB input (V01's job) completed successfully, confirming the bound holds against real infra, not just the in-container harness.

tasks.title: GET /jobs/:id — status, and the output by presigned reference
tasks.detail: Never stream result bytes through the API. Reuse the existing presign path (artifact_service.presign_artifact) rather than writing a second one, and honour MODEL-FLOW-000-T06's rule: neither the presign request nor the URL reaches a log, because the URL IS the capability. RESULT 2026-09-02: Input reuses presign_artifact unchanged (is_committed_artifact_key). Output is a SIBLING function, presign_prediction_job_object (+ presign_prediction_job_upload for the container's own writes) — never a widened is_committed_artifact_key guard, matching presign_run_object's own precedent and stated reason. GET /prediction-jobs/:jobId mints the output URL fresh on read. LIVE-VERIFIED end-to-end: real presigned GET URL returned by a real backend, real object downloaded from real MinIO, byte-exact against a reference computed with the same softsensor_scaling.to_model_ready call /predict uses (max abs diff 0.0 across 12 rows). ALSO FOUND AND FIXED: the route was originally POST /predict:batch, not /predict-batch — find-my-way (Fastify's router) parses a bare ':' as a param opener, so that path silently matched ANY /predict<suffix>, not just the literal string. Confirmed live against find-my-way@9.6.0 before switching to /predict-batch — see prediction-job.authorized.controller.ts's own comment.

tasks.title: Record which version scored the batch
tasks.detail: Pin the version at job START and store it on the job. A long batch spanning a promote must not silently score its first half on one model and its second on another — and a result whose model is 'whatever was production at some point' cannot be reproduced or defended later. RESULT 2026-09-02: modelVersionId pinned at submitPredictionJobService, never re-resolved. ModelServingAuthorizedService gained getDescriptorByVersionIdService (resolves ANY ModelVersion by id, no stage filter) alongside the existing getDescriptorService (current-PRODUCTION only) so claimJobService always reads the version pinned at submit, even after it is demoted. LIVE-VERIFIED as V03 below — an ARCHIVED version resolved correctly mid-job.

acceptance_criteria: The batch endpoint returns a job id without waiting for the work.
Job state survives a restart of the process that created it.
Results are delivered by presigned reference; no result bytes traverse the API.
The same idempotency key cannot produce two jobs.
Every job records the exact model version that scored it, pinned at start.
A batch over a wide input keeps memory bounded — no unbounded read of the input frame.

verification.description: Submit a batch, restart the serving process mid-flight, and confirm GET /jobs/:id still reports truthfully — either a completed job or a job that reached a terminal FAILED with a stated reason. Permanently RUNNING is the failure this checks for, and it is the exact state MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 observed on the training side. RESULT 2026-09-02, LIVE: submitted an 8M-row/1.19GB batch against a real backend, paused its container via `docker pause` right after spawn (containerId set, status RUNNING) to force a genuine in-flight window, then force-killed and restarted the backend process. Boot log: 'Reconciled 1 orphaned run/container(s) at boot' — the job stayed RUNNING (re-attached via container.inspect() + watch(), not marked FAILED for a container that still existed). Unpaused; the NEW process's re-attached watch() tracked it to real completion (SUCCEEDED, 8,000,000 rows) roughly 55s later. Never permanently RUNNING, never falsely FAILED for a live container.

Submit the same idempotency key twice concurrently and confirm one job. Sequential submission is a weaker test that a naive check would also pass. RESULT 2026-09-02, LIVE: fired two concurrent POST /predict-batch requests with the same idempotencyKey (bash background jobs, same instant). FIRST ATTEMPT FOUND A REAL BUG: both this file's isUniqueViolation and its two precedents (model-version.authorized.service.ts, dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts) check err.meta.target, which does not exist on this Prisma version's driver-adapter P2002 shape — reproduced live, the actual meta was {modelName, driverAdapterError:{cause:{originalCode:'23505', originalMessage:'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "PredictionJob_idempotency_key"', constraint:{fields:[...]}}}}, no `target` anywhere. The constraint-name check therefore never matched, and BOTH concurrent requests got either a raw 500 or (worse) both would have raced past the intended graceful fallback. Fixed in this file's isUniqueViolation to also check meta.driverAdapterError.cause.originalMessage, keeping the old target check for forward-compat. Re-ran the same concurrent race after the fix: exactly one PredictionJob row, both requests returned the SAME jobId (one 201, one 200 'A job already exists for this idempotency key'). NOT FIXED (out of scope for this feature, flagged for follow-up): the identical bug in model-version.authorized.service.ts (breaks the intended clean 409 on a concurrent promote race, currently surfaces a raw 500 instead) and dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts's resolveOrCreateEditDraftService. Both should get the same fix.

Promote a new version DURING a running batch and confirm the output was scored end to end by the pinned version, asserted from the job row and the output's own recorded version — not inferred from timing. RESULT 2026-09-02, LIVE: submitted a batch pinned to ModelVersion v1 (PRODUCTION at submit time), paused its container before it could claim, promoted a real second ModelVersion v2 to PRODUCTION while v1's job sat paused (v1 -> ARCHIVED, confirmed via psql), then unpaused. The job claimed, scored, and completed successfully. Asserted from TWO independent sources, neither inferred from timing: (1) PredictionJob.modelVersionId in Postgres = v1's id, unchanged; (2) the container's OWN self-written batch_manifest.json in MinIO recorded modelVersionId = v1's id too. Never retargeted to v2 despite v2 being the live PRODUCTION version for the entire duration the container actually ran. getDescriptorByVersionIdService's no-stage-filter design (T05) confirmed correct against a real ARCHIVED-version resolution, not just unit-mocked.

features.title: POST /retrain — Trigger Only
features.blocked_on: RESOLVED 2026-09-01 BY TRANSCRIPTION (MODEL-SERVE-000-T05 / upstream re-read) — status flipped blocked -> pending. ORIGINAL, PRESERVED: 'The same decision MODEL-FLOW-005 is blocked on — see MODEL-FLOW decisions.fine_tuning_undefined and this ledger's decisions.retrain_and_fine_tuning_are_one_question. Until retrain is defined (a fresh fit on a widened window? a hyperparameter search reusing the split? a warm start on a framework that supports one?), the tasks below describe a job whose work is unspecified.' Upstream decisions.fine_tuning_undefined resolved 2026-08-25 (user decision): fine-tuning = a hyperparameter search — one algorithm, one artifact, one split, N hyperparameter sets in sequence, best kept by RMSE. Transcribed into this ledger's decisions.retrain_is_blocked_on_the_same_definition_as_fine_tuning. MODEL-FLOW-005 was built on this definition and all 8 of its tasks are completed — it is a proven implementation pattern, not a speculative one. No engineering against MODEL-SERVE-004 has been done in this pass; only the block is lifted.
features.description: An endpoint that records the intent to retrain and returns. The work is done by the existing trainer image, spawned the way MODEL-FLOW-003-T04 already spawns it. A successful retrain produces a new ModelVersion at STAGING and promotes nothing.

tasks.title: Define what retrain means, and write it in the shared decision
tasks.detail: This is the whole blocker and it is a product decision, not an engineering one. Everything below is unscopeable until it lands. Write the answer into MODEL-FLOW decisions.fine_tuning_undefined so both ledgers read one definition.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: Done by transcription, not new deliberation — see this feature's blocked_on and decisions.retrain_is_blocked_on_the_same_definition_as_fine_tuning: retrain = a hyperparameter search, one algorithm/artifact/split, N sets tried in sequence, best kept by RMSE.

tasks.title: Trigger endpoint with idempotency and a per-model lock
tasks.detail: Three clicks must not become three containers competing for the same 8 GiB. MODEL-FLOW-000-T03 established that /scratch's tmpfs shares the container's memory cgroup, so concurrent fits are not merely slow, they are a plausible OOM.
tasks.result_2026_09_03: POST /authorized/model/:modelId/retrain (ModelRetrainAuthorizedController, the same authorized/model/:modelId prefix model-version and prediction-job already use; a plain path, not '/retrain:trigger' — see MODEL-SERVE-003's find-my-way finding). TWO guards, not one: (1) the per-model LOCK is the partial unique index ModelCandidateJob_one_live_per_model, so the row is created FIRST and only the request that owns it reaches the spawn — a loser is refused before any container exists, which is what V02 actually measures; (2) idempotencyKey is opt-in and scoped (modelId, idempotencyKey), so a retry after a dropped response returns the ORIGINAL job even after it finished. The P2002-by-constraint-name check is copied from prediction-job.authorized.service.ts (the FIXED shape reading meta.driverAdapterError.cause.originalMessage), NOT from model-version.authorized.service.ts, whose meta.target-only copy MODEL-SERVE-003 proved never matches on this Prisma version — that copy is still broken and is flagged below, not fixed here.

tasks.title: Spawn the existing trainer; never fit in the serving process
tasks.detail: Per decisions.training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.
tasks.result_2026_09_03: Nothing fits in-process. launchModelRun -> trackSpawn -> TrainningContainerAuthorizedService.spawn(runId, token) with the default MODE=train — the identical path a wizard run takes, including the 8 GiB memory cap and the /scratch tmpfs this task's own note worried about. The trigger returns 201 with a job id while the first container is still starting. Because a retrain candidate is an ordinary ModelTrainingRun, the boot-time reconcileOrphanedRuns sweep re-attaches a retrain run after a backend restart with NO new code — the gap MODEL-FLOW-011-T04 closed applies here for free.

tasks.title: On success, create a STAGING version — promote nothing
tasks.detail: Auto-promotion would put an unreviewed model in front of live traffic on a schedule, which is a decision no one made. MODEL-SERVE-001-T03 takes the same position for Save Model, for the same reason.
tasks.result_2026_09_03:
advanceJobForRun's completion branch now forks on owner: a draft-owned job points ModelDraft.currentRunId at the winner (unchanged); a model-owned job calls completeModelOwnedJob, which mints a ModelVersion at the schema default STAGING from the winning run and writes resultVersionId. It reads nothing about PRODUCTION and writes nothing to it.

The compare-and-swap updateMany and the modelVersion.create are ONE interactive transaction, unlike the draft branch's two statements. The draft branch tolerates a crash between them (the next read re-derives); a retrain cannot — getJobService only reconciles QUEUED/RUNNING, so a job left SUCCEEDED with resultVersionId null would have lost its only deliverable with nothing able to repair it. getRunManifest (an HTTP call to apps/python for model_sha256/framework_versions) is read BEFORE the transaction opens, Save Model's own ordering. Re-entrancy uses ModelVersion.sourceRunId @unique: the transaction looks for an existing version for that run and ADOPTS it rather than racing the constraint. A winner with no modelKey fails the job with a named reason instead of minting a version that could never be loaded.

tasks.title: Compare the candidate against the incumbent, and publish the comparison
tasks.detail: The comparison is only meaningful on a common evaluation basis; a retrain on a widened window has a different test split, so a raw R² delta is not a like-for-like number. State the basis alongside the numbers rather than presenting a delta that reads as one and is not — the same discipline MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 applies to publishing the holdout's missing rate beside every metric.
tasks.result_2026_09_03: PREMISE CORRECTED AGAINST T01, the fourth time this ledger's own re-audit has had to do that. T05 was written while 'retrain' might still have meant a refit on a widened window, and it worried that a delta across two different test splits reads like a like-for-like number and is not. T01's resolution deleted that case: a retrain reuses the incumbent's artifact, target and split, so the delta IS like-for-like. What T05 asks for survives as a CHECK rather than a caveat — GET /authorized/model/:modelId/retrain/:jobId publishes a `comparison` block whose `basis` names goldArtifactId, artifactChecksum, targetY and the split, and `rmseDelta` is emitted ONLY when all four match between the candidate's run and the incumbent's. Otherwise comparable:false carries the reason, rmseDelta is null, and BOTH raw numbers are still published. RMSE leads and r2 is reported beside it, never used to rank (the observed r2 = -1,110,858 run is why). Both directions were exercised live — see V04.

acceptance_criteria: The endpoint returns immediately with a job id and never fits in-process.
Concurrent triggers for one model produce one job.
A successful retrain creates a STAGING version and changes no PRODUCTION pointer.
The candidate-versus-incumbent comparison states its evaluation basis, and refuses to present a delta across incomparable bases as if it were one.

verification.description: Trigger a retrain and confirm PRODUCTION is unchanged after it succeeds. The point of the feature is what it does NOT do.
verification.note:
LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-03 against the real dev stack (Postgres, MinIO, apps/python :8000, a backend process running THIS code, real trainer containers — not mocked). Fixture: a COPY of a real SUCCEEDED run (ridge alpha=100, FINAL artifact, chronological 0.7, rmse 0.34326) adopted by a throwaway Model, its version 1 promoted to PRODUCTION through the REAL promote endpoint (with an override reason — no run in this dev database has a positive r2, which is itself the T06 floor doing its job). A copy, never the original row, because Model -> ModelTrainingRun is ON DELETE CASCADE and cleaning up the fixture must not delete a real draft's run.

PRODUCTION row before: a1b9822e… PRODUCTION promotedAt 01:42:58.238 updatedAt 01:42:58.244. After a retrain ran to completion: byte-identical on all four fields, still exactly ONE PRODUCTION row. The new version came out as version 2, stage STAGING, sourceRunId = the job's bestRunId, and the job's resultVersionId points at it. The winner was the LOWEST-RMSE candidate (0.255914, alpha=0.01) and not the last to finish (alpha=10, 0.327699) — the same '<' not '<=' selection MODEL-FLOW-005-V01 proved for the draft path, now proved for the model path.

verification.description: Fire three concurrent triggers and confirm one container. Count containers, not jobs — a service that dedupes the row but spawns three is the failure this guards.
verification.note: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-03 with real concurrent HTTP requests and a real container count, not a job count. Three simultaneous POST /retrain for one model returned exactly one 201 and two 409s naming the in-flight job, and the database held exactly ONE ModelCandidateJob row. Repeated a second and third time with the same result. Containers were counted by polling `docker ps --filter label=dslake.role=training` every 200ms across the whole search: MAX RUNNING = 1. (An earlier pass counted `docker ps -a` and saw 2 — an exited, not-yet-reaped container overlapping the next candidate's start; that is the chain working, not the burst, and the corrected measurement is the one recorded here.) Idempotency was exercised separately: three concurrent triggers sharing one key produced one job, and replaying that key AFTER the job completed returned 200 with the SAME jobId instead of starting a second search.

features.implementation:
Built 2026-09-03, backend only — no client wiring (not asked for; apps/client/lib/retrain.ts's 700ms setTimeout simulation and use-model-retrain.ts stay exactly as they are, and that file's own comment 'Retraining is a simulation today (no training infra yet)' is now the only stale thing left, flagged not fixed). NO new orchestrator and NO trainer-image change: a retrain is a ModelCandidateJob owned by a Model instead of a ModelDraft, so it runs on the SAME advanceJobForRun compare-and-swap chain MODEL-FLOW-005/013 already live-verified, and each candidate is an ordinary ModelTrainingRun spawned by the SAME MODE=train path (soft-sensor-trainer 1.0.6 untouched, no tag bump — the search is orchestrated ABOVE the container, as schema.prisma's own ModelCandidateJob comment states).

Extraction, not duplication, three times over (the discipline MODEL-FLOW-005 established when it split createDraftRunService): (a) ModelRunLaunchAuthorizedService.createRunService -> assertModelAccess + new public launchModelRun(modelId, dto, candidateJobId?), the no-user/no-role write a webhook-driven chained candidate needs; (b) the ModelVersion field mapping out of Save Model's inline tx.modelVersion.create into @/lib/model-version-from-run (buildModelVersionData + nextModelVersionNumber), so Save Model's version 1 and a retrain's max+1 differ in exactly one field and cannot drift; (c) getJobService's reconcile-on-read + per-candidate table into reconcileAndShape, called by both the wizard's GET and the retrain GET.

Schema: modelDraftId nullable + modelId/sourceVersionId/resultVersionId/idempotencyKey added, with a hand-written XOR CHECK (ModelCandidateJob_owner_exactly_one) and two hand-written partial unique indexes (ModelCandidateJob_one_live_per_model, ModelCandidateJob_idempotency_key) — the same hand-written-partial-index precedent this table already carries for the draft owner. sourceVersionId/resultVersionId are bare Strings with NO foreign key, deliberately: an FK there would add a third edge to the Model -> ModelVersion/ModelTrainingRun cascade diamond that broke deleteModelService once (MODEL-SERVE-001's ModelVersion_sourceRunId_fkey). V03 was added to this feature to prove that delete still works rather than assume it.

REAL BUG CAUGHT WHILE WIRING, not by review: getJobService rebuilt a candidate's loss-history key as draftRunKey(job.modelDraftId, run.id, 'loss_history.json'). For a model-owned job that is 'drafts/null/runs/…', which soft-fails to null and would have silently shown NO loss history on every retrain candidate. Fixed by reading the STORED run.lossHistoryKey (written by complete()'s buildRunKey(owner,…), correct for either owner) — the same 'read the pinned key, never re-derive it' rule MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 established for featureSpecKey. The draft path is unaffected either way.

One narrowing recorded rather than discovered later: an incumbent fitted with expanding-window CV is REFUSED (422, reason named). A job row carries one trainTestSplit ratio, and a CV incumbent has no single ratio to reuse — reconstructing one would retrain on a different basis than the version it claims to improve on, exactly what T05 exists to prevent.

features.title: Prediction Logging and Drift Signal
features.description: Record inputs and predictions so that a model going wrong is observable, and so that a future automatic retrain has a trigger that is a measurement rather than a calendar.

tasks.title: Log request features, prediction and version to the time-series store
tasks.detail: Sampled, not every request — full-fidelity logging of a high-rate soft sensor is a second data pipeline nobody planned for. State the sampling rate; a rate chosen by accident makes every downstream statistic uninterpretable.
tasks.result_2026_09_03: PredictionLog Prisma model (packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma) + hand-written migration 20260903120000_model_serve_005_prediction_log; apps/serving samples per-REQUEST (SERVING_LOG_SAMPLE_RATE, default 1.0) and caps per-request detail rows (SERVING_LOG_MAX_ROWS, default 200) while computing aggregates over the FULL request regardless of the cap; every logged row records the sampling rate that was actually in force, on the row, never re-derived from current config later. New backend module prediction-log/ (PredictionLogIngestAuthorizedController under authorized/serving, ServingTokenGuard) and apps/python's prediction_log_service.append write the object to serving-logs/{modelId}/{modelVersionId}/dt=.../hour=.../{uuid}.parquet. Bounded so logging can never fail or delay /predict — verified in the unit suite, not just asserted.
tasks.result_2026_09_03_live: LIVE-VERIFIED against the real stack (Postgres, MinIO, a real backend on :4000, a real apps/python on :8000, a real apps/serving on :8100, real /predict calls against a real fitted model.joblib). Sampling: fired 40 requests at SERVING_LOG_SAMPLE_RATE=0.5, got EXACTLY 20 PredictionLog rows, every one carrying samplingRate=0.5 on the row. Objects: read a real serving-logs/{modelId}/{modelVersionId}/dt=.../hour=.../{uuid}.parquet object directly from MinIO — 5 rows, timestamp + all 21 raw feature columns + prediction, matching rowCount/loggedRows exactly. Series read: GET .../predictions returned 15 points across 3 real requests, strictly time-ordered, with real raw feature values and the correct pinned modelVersionId on each point. Cleanup: deleting the fixture Model cascaded onto PredictionLog correctly (23 rows -> 0, no orphan, no FK error) — the NO ACTION-on-modelVersionId choice (PredictionJob's own precedent) proven live, not just read. Resilience ('logging cannot break serving') is proven by the unit suite (test_predict_succeeds_even_when_logging_would_fail, a real requests.ConnectionError injected into the log POST) rather than the live stack: BACKEND_API_BASE is shared between descriptor resolution and log ingest, so pointing it at an unreachable host in a live attempt breaks descriptor resolution too (a different, correctly-fatal failure mode) and cannot isolate logging specifically — the unit test's monkeypatch CAN and does.

tasks.title: Compare live input distributions against the training distribution
tasks.detail: The training distribution is already characterised — column_stats is the sidecar the dataset wizard writes and MODEL-FLOW-010-T04 reads. Compare against it rather than recomputing a baseline, so both surfaces agree on what 'normal' was.
tasks.result_2026_09_03: apps/backend/src/lib/prediction-drift.ts: poolFeatureStats + computeDrift, comparing pooled live sufficient statistics against column_stats.json's mean/std (exact z-score) with an explicitly-labelled ESTIMATED out-of-range rate (Normal-CDF against the baseline's empirical p1/p99). Reused the EXACT column_stats.json sidecar MODEL-FLOW-010-T04 already reads (this feature's own acceptance criterion) via the existing getArtifactColumnStatsService's own postToPython('/v1/preprocess/column-stats', ...) call shape, called directly (no user session on this path) the same way freezeSplitStats calls python directly one layer over. Found and fixed the TagColumnStats median/std wire-model bug this task's own baseline depended on (see this feature's own implementation note) before building on it. GET /authorized/model/:modelId/drift; 13 new unit tests (prediction-drift.spec.ts) cover pooling, the CDF estimate's bounds, the OK/CRITICAL/UNKNOWN classification, a column absent from live data or from the baseline, and that one UNKNOWN column never masks a CRITICAL one in the rolled-up report status. NOT live-verified against the real stack this pass — the OrbStack Docker VM became unresponsive before V01 could run; see the feature's own implementation note.
tasks.result_2026_09_03_live: LIVE-VERIFIED, both directions, against a real column_stats.json (22 tags) and a real fitted model. In-distribution: built RAW feature values by inverting each column's real minmax scalingParams (feature_spec.json) so the SCALED value lands exactly on that column's training mean; drift report came back status OK with |z| < 0.003 on every column. Shifted: pushed AI001A2.PV and TI202.PV to training_mean + 10*training_std in SCALED space (via the same inverse-scaling construction) and left every other column at its in-distribution value; the report returned z=10.001... on BOTH shifted columns (matching the intended 10-SD shift to 3 decimal places), status CRITICAL, outOfRangePct=100 on exactly those two, and every untouched column stayed OK — proving the comparison is genuinely per-column, not a blanket 'something changed' signal. This IS MODEL-SERVE-005-V01, run for real.

tasks.title: Join late-arriving ground truth and track live error
tasks.detail: For a lab-sampled target the truth arrives hours or days later, so this is a delayed join, not a live metric. Publish the missing/Bad rate of the joined window beside the error, for the reason MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 gives: with no imputation, a hole depresses the score with no trace of why.
tasks.blocked_on: CONFIRMED STILL BLOCKED 2026-09-03, scope decision taken WITH THE USER before this pass began (T01+T02 now, T03 explicitly deferred). No persisted ground truth exists anywhere in this system — measured, not assumed: the evaluation UI's lab points live in `useState<LabPoint[]>` in apps/client/hooks/use-model-evaluation.ts:75-76 and are never sent to a server; no Prisma model or column anywhere holds an actual/observed/measurement value (grep across schema.prisma confirms zero hits outside prose). This task needs, at minimum: (a) a decision on how truth ARRIVES — a re-fetched `.lab` PI tag on a stated lag, or the evaluation UI's own CSV-upload path made to persist server-side instead of staying client-only; (b) a join granularity, which this pass's PredictionLog schema does not provide (one row per LOGGED REQUEST, not one row per time window) — MODEL-SERVE-006-T01's InferenceWindow (modelVersionId, windowStart) is the natural join key this task would actually want, per this feature's own original scope_correction; (c) MODEL-SERVE-006-T04's ingestion-lag decision, since a live error can only be computed once the window it scores is known to be closed. None of the three exist yet.
tasks.unblocked_2026_09_14: UNBLOCKED 2026-09-14. Two of the three gaps this task's own blocked_on named closed on their own: (b) join granularity is now InferenceWindow (MODEL-SERVE-006-T01, @@unique [modelVersionId, windowStart]) — exactly the key this task's blocked_on said it would want; (c) the ingestion-lag decision is InferenceSchedule.lagMinutes (MODEL-SERVE-006-T04). (a) how truth ARRIVES was decided at plan approval on 2026-09-14 — see decisions.ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_target_tag.
tasks.result_2026_09_14:
BUILT 2026-09-14. Truth arrives by RE-FETCHING THE TARGET TAG on its own, much longer lag (decisions.ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_target_tag), joined to the window's own stored predictions.parquet on a stated tolerance.

SCHEMA. New InferenceWindowTruth (migration 20260914120000_model_serve_005_t03_window_truth), ONE row per window via `windowId @unique` — it inherits InferenceWindow's own @@unique([modelVersionId, windowStart]) rather than minting a second idempotency key. It stores SUFFICIENT STATISTICS (n, sumSe, sumAe, sumSigned, sumActual, sumActualSq), not finished metrics, so a rolling metric over N windows is EXACT rather than an average of averages — the same trick poolFeatureStats already uses for drift one task over. Its only FK is windowId->InferenceWindow ON DELETE CASCADE; modelId/modelVersionId are deliberately denormalised plain columns with NO constraint, so the delete-ordering footgun that forced NO ACTION on InferenceWindow_modelVersionId_fkey cannot recur here. InferenceSchedule gained truthLagMinutes (default 1440), truthToleranceMinutes (30) and truthHorizonHours (168), all positive-never-zero, merged partial-update-safe exactly as T09's five deploy fields are.

PYTHON. New services/ground_truth_service.py: the same pi|sql fork materialize_window uses (this side holds the only source credentials), but fetching ONE column with no recipe replay — the target is a base tag, so apply_features/max_replay_lookback do not apply. Bad cells are DROPPED, never imputed, the same rule and the same reason drop_bad_feature_rows states. The join is pandas.merge_asof(direction='nearest', tolerance=...) followed by one-pair-per-prediction-closest-wins — the EXACT semantics apps/client/lib/lab-ingestion.ts's alignLabToPredictions already defines, so the server and the Evaluation tab cannot disagree about what 'aligned' means. merge_asof appeared nowhere in this repo before. Writes truth.parquet as a FOURTH filename under the window's own existing hour prefix (inference/{modelId}/{modelVersionId}/dt=/hour=/), key built python-side only per INFERENCE_ROOT's one-writer-one-key-builder rule. Returns SUMS only; python never computes an aggregate, the same split T01 draws. A read-side `series` takes EXPLICIT keys rather than listing a prefix — unlike prediction_log_service.series, every truth object is already indexed by InferenceWindowTruth.pairsKey, so the database is the index.

BACKEND. lib/live-error.ts (pure, no I/O — the prediction-drift.ts shape): poolTruthStats + computeLiveError, using the IDENTICAL formulas and sign convention (residual = predicted - actual) apps/client/lib/model-evaluation.ts's computeMetrics uses, with two deliberate differences stated in its own header: it returns NULL rather than computeMetrics's {rmse:0,mae:0,r2:0} on an empty set (harmless in a mock-fed chart, dangerous as a published monitoring figure — a window no lab has reported on would read as a perfect score), and it does not round (rounding belongs to the renderer). New InferenceTruthSweeperService with its OWN setInterval(...).unref() — deliberately NOT inside the scheduler tick, because MODEL-SERVE-006-T02's rule is that the tick inserts and reconciles and nothing else, and a truth join is a real historian fetch that would otherwise delay the inserts whose absence is a permanent gap. Re-join is an UPSERT on windowId (never a second row) with a geometric `nextJoinAfter` backoff: without it every window inside its horizon would be re-fetched every sweep, ~168 round trips per window at the defaults, nearly all returning rows already held. Routes GET /inference/truth and POST /inference/truth/rejoin on the existing InferenceWindowAuthorizedController; the re-join drives the SAME sweeper method a scheduled join does, per MODEL-SERVE-006-T11's no-second-code-path rule.

THE ONE CORRECTNESS RULE, and the trap it closes: a truth value must be EVIDENCED BY AN ACTUAL LAB EVENT in the interval, never by a held or interpolated summary. The live PI path is a TimeWeighted/Average summary (PIWebAPI.getAverageValue -> get_summaries_ad_hoc) and PI holds a sparse .lab tag's last value between samples, so inheriting the schedule's own fetchConfig would return a plausible number for EVERY interval — including every interval in which no measurement was ever taken — and publish a confident R2 against a held value. The PI branch therefore overrides cal_basis to EventWeighted and runs a Count PROBE first, keeping only intervals the probe saw an event in. Two sequential calls, not one: from_pi_response builds one value per (tag, timestamp), so a single call asking for both Count and Average would collide two summaries into one column.

CLIENT. The Monitoring tab's Actual-vs-Predict and Residual charts, simulated for as long as this task was blocked, now read REAL joined pairs (hooks/model/use-live-error.ts, one cache key for its one endpoint). EvalPoint stayed NON-OPTIONAL and the charts were not modified: only joined rows are fed in, so the series renders SPARSELY — one point per lab measurement, not one per scored interval — which is what a lab-sampled target honestly looks like. The 'simulated pending the ground-truth join' label is gone; lib/mock-lab-data.ts stays because the Evaluation tab still uses its sibling generator. Coverage is published BESIDE the number (windows joined / in range, paired vs. lab-sample counts, windows awaiting truth) with the WORST window's missingPct rather than a mean — a mean hides the one window whose sensor stopped, which is the case MODEL-SERVE-006-T05 exists to make visible. The RMSE KPI renders an em-dash, never 0.00, when nothing has joined. Metrics are GROUPED BY VERSION and the top-level figure is null when a range mixes versions: MODEL-SERVE-006-T07 allows two versions to score one windowStart and each resolves its target through its OWN source run, so two versions in a range can predict different things and one pooled RMSE over them would be a number about nothing. `targetColumn` is stored on the row so that is checkable at read time.

COMMENT ROT FIXED AT THE SOURCE rather than left: lib/metric-registry.ts's doc comment claimed monitoring metrics were not backfillable 'because ground truth is not joined (MODEL-SERVE-005-T03 stays blocked)', and use-prediction-monitoring.ts's LivePredictionPoint said the same. Both are now corrected — monitoring metrics ARE backfillable, from truth.parquet (metrics.json still has no `actual` and never will: it is written at scoring time, hours or days before the lab reports).
tasks.result_2026_09_14_live:
LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-14 against real infrastructure (real MinIO, real dev Postgres, a real apps/python on :8000, a real SQL lab source), not by inspection. Every figure below was hand-computed from the fixture BEFORE the run and matched exactly.

Fixture: 6 predictions (15:00->41.0, 15:10->41.5, 15:20->42.0, 15:30->42.5, 15:40->43.0, 15:50->43.5) written as a real predictions.parquet in MinIO; a lab table carrying 15:02->40.0, 15:32->40.5, 15:45->NULL and 16:05->99.0, tolerance 600s.

V04 (ARITHMETIC, NOT PLUMBING): the join returned truth_rows 3, paired_rows 2, n 2, sum_se 5, sum_ae 3, sum_signed 3, sum_actual 80.5, sum_actual_sq 3240.25 — every one the hand-computed value. Reading the written truth.parquet back out of real MinIO showed exactly two rows: (15:00, 41.0, 40.0, +1.0) and (15:30, 42.5, 40.5, +2.0), confirming each lab sample paired with its NEAREST prediction and residual = predicted - actual.
NEVER IMPUTED: the 15:45 NULL is absent from truth_rows — proven by the count, not by a null-check.
TOLERANCE BOUNDARY: the 16:05 sample sits inside the fetch range but 15 minutes from the nearest prediction, and was DROPPED rather than snapped to a distant one.

V03 (THE INCREMENTAL RE-JOIN — the property an insert-once design would silently break): two more lab rows were added (15:12->41.0, 15:52->42.0) and the SAME window re-joined. Result: truth_rows 3->5, n 2->4, sum_se 5->7.5, sum_actual 80.5->163.5, sum_actual_sq 3240.25->6685.25 — again every figure hand-computed first. The SAME object key was rewritten (checksum changed, one object not two).

V02 (THE NO-TRUTH CASE — what separates a working join from one that has merely not been fed): a window whose range holds no lab sample returned n 0, truth_rows 0, object_key NULL and checksum NULL, with prediction_rows still 6 so 'no truth' and 'no predictions' stay distinguishable. No object was written at all.

READ SIDE: the truth-series endpoint returned all 4 real pairs in timestamp order, and a deliberately nonexistent key in the same request was SKIPPED rather than failing the range read — a reclaimed window is a gap in the chart, not a broken endpoint.

DATABASE (8/8 against the real dev Postgres, fixture ids all `ms005t03-`, removed afterwards): the migration's table accepted the row the sweeper builds; the sums round-tripped through DOUBLE PRECISION exactly (3240.25 and 5 came back unchanged); a re-join left EXACTLY ONE row with the SAME id and carried n 2->4 forward; the range read's Prisma select joined the window row for missingPct; the sweeper's own `truth: { is: null }` relation filter compiled and selected the right window; and deleting the fixture Model cascaded onto InferenceWindowTruth cleanly (truth 0, windows 0), proving the deliberate absence of a ModelVersion FK live. This also proved the sweeper's exact `create: { windowId, ...scalars }` shape works at RUNTIME — tsc accepting it is not the same evidence, since Prisma 7 rejects mixed checked/unchecked create inputs at runtime and several fixture creates in this very session failed exactly that way.

The live numbers are PINNED as a regression in lib/live-error.spec.ts ('matches the live-verified sums from the real stack'), as literals rather than recomputed from the pairs, so a future change to the join's arithmetic cannot move both sides together. Pooled r2 over those four real pairs is 1 - 7.5/2.1875 = -2.43, published as the negative number it is rather than clamped.

NOT LIVE-VERIFIED, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: (1) the PI branch. PI is unreachable from this dev machine — the same fact that made MODEL-SERVE-006-T04 set lagMinutes as a chosen rather than measured value — so the Count-probe/EventWeighted path ships reviewed, with unit tests that inject a fake PI response proving the probe runs FIRST, that a held-value interval with count 0 is refused, and that cal_basis is overridden to EventWeighted on both calls. The SQL branch, which IS the branch MODEL-SERVE-006-V03 verified, was exercised live end to end. (2) The backend HTTP routes and the Monitoring tab in a browser: the join, the sweeper's candidate query, the upsert and the metric math were each exercised against real infrastructure, but not through a logged-in end-to-end request.

features.scope_correction: REVISED 2026-08-25. This feature was written assuming prediction logging is a sampled by-product of synchronous requests. With MODEL-SERVE-006, the primary prediction stream is the hourly window record, which is complete rather than sampled and already carries version and missing rate. So T01's sampling concern applies to MODEL-SERVE-002's sync path only, and T02 (drift vs column_stats) and T03 (late ground-truth join) now read from InferenceWindow. They stay here rather than moving into 006 because they are analysis over the record, not production of it.
features.acceptance_criteria_correction: The first two criteria listed here ('r2 at or below zero cannot be promoted' and 'the image digest is retained') were misfiled — they belong to MODEL-SERVE-001-T06 and -T07 respectively and are removed from this feature. Recorded rather than silently deleted, per MODEL-SERVE-000-V01's rule.
acceptance_criteria: Predictions are logged with their model version and the logging is sampled at a stated, deliberate rate.
Drift is measured against the artifact's own column_stats, not a separately-computed baseline.
Live error is reported only for windows where ground truth has actually arrived, with the joined window's missing rate published beside it.

verification.description: Feed input shifted well outside the training distribution and confirm the drift signal fires. Feeding in-distribution data proves only that nothing crashed.
verification.note: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-03 against the real dev stack (Postgres, MinIO, real backend/python/serving processes, a real fitted model — not mocked), after an earlier attempt this same day was blocked for 20+ minutes by an unresponsive OrbStack Docker VM (host CPU idle throughout; a VM-internal resource issue, not a code defect) and recovered on its own. In-distribution rows (constructed by inverting the model's real minmax scaler so the scaled value lands on the training mean) reported drift status OK, |z|<0.003 on every column — proving no false positive on the happy path. Rows with two columns pushed to +10 training-SD reported status CRITICAL with z=10.001 on exactly those two columns (matching the intended shift almost exactly) while every untouched column stayed OK — proving the signal is real, per-column, and correctly scaled math, not a coincidence or a blanket flag. A real bug (requestedAt's `+00:00` vs `Z` — see this feature's own implementation note) was found and fixed by this verification pass before it could pass.

verification.description: A SUCCEEDED window whose range holds NO lab sample must report no error — not an error of zero. A test that only feeds a window with truth cannot tell a working join from one that has merely not yet been fed, and a zero renders as a perfect model.
verification.result_2026_09_14: LIVE. n 0, truth_rows 0, object_key NULL, checksum NULL, prediction_rows still 6 — no object written. lib/live-error.ts returns null for n<=0 (unit-covered), and the Monitoring tab renders an em-dash plus a named reason rather than 0.00.

verification.description: Truth is late AND incremental: re-joining a window after more lab results arrive must UPDATE the same row and the same object, never insert a second. An insert-once design silently freezes every window on its first, thinnest number.
verification.result_2026_09_14: LIVE, from TWO independent sources. Python: adding two lab rows and re-joining moved truth_rows 3->5 and n 2->4 with the same object key rewritten (new checksum). Postgres: the upsert left exactly ONE row, with the SAME id, carrying n=4.

verification.description: Hand-compute one residual and the pooled figures from the real fetched numbers and match the published values, including the sign convention — Monitoring and Evaluation must never report opposite signs for the same model.
verification.result_2026_09_14: LIVE. Every sum matched its hand-computed value exactly (sum_se 5, sum_ae 3, sum_signed 3, sum_actual 80.5, sum_actual_sq 3240.25 at n=2; 7.5/5/5/163.5/6685.25 at n=4). residual = predicted - actual confirmed against lib/model-evaluation.ts's own convention, and the tolerance boundary held: a sample 15 minutes from the nearest prediction under a 10-minute tolerance was dropped, not snapped.

verification.description: A window whose truth join FAILS must not starve the sweep. findDueWindows treats a window with no truth row as eligible and orders windowStart ASC, so a window that can never join (a ModelVersion whose sourceRun.targetY is null, a deleted DataSource, an unsupported source type -- each throws before any upsert) sits at the head of every later pass. At the default 168h horizon and hourly cadence that is up to 168 permanently-failing windows against a batch of 25: newer joinable windows are never reached, and the only symptom is a log line. Unit tests cannot see this; it is a property of the candidate query plus the ordering, not of any one function.
verification.result_2026_09_14: LIVE against the real dev Postgres (7/7 PASS, fixtures ms005t03b-* created and removed). Three eligible windows A<B<C, batch size 1, running the candidate query VERBATIM from findDueWindows. (1) sweep 1 picks A, as designed. (2) A gets the failure row backOff now writes -- the migration accepts it with targetColumn NULL and failureReason set. (3) sweep 2 picks B: the batch head moved. (4) With the failure row DELETED, the same query picks A again -- the bug reproduced directly, B and C never reached. (5) With nextJoinAfter in the past, A is eligible again -- a failure row delays a retry, it does not cancel one. (6) A batch of 25 still returns A,B,C oldest-first. Publishing is unaffected: poolTruthStats skips n<=0 and getTruthService filters the same rows before any metric, so a failure row can never be read as a real empty join -- failureReason is the only thing that separates 'the lab has not reported yet' from 'we could not ask'.

verification.description: The backend must actually BOOT with the new provider and both new routes. tsc proves the types; it does not prove Nest resolves the graph or that Fastify matches the paths -- MODEL-SERVE-003's /predict:batch route is this ledger's own precedent for a route that type-checked and still matched the wrong thing.
verification.result_2026_09_14: LIVE. `nest start` reached 'Nest application successfully started' with InferenceTruthSweeperService resolved and logging 'Ground-truth join sweep scheduled every 900000ms.' RouterExplorer mapped both {/api/authorized/model/:modelId/inference/truth, GET} and {/api/authorized/model/:modelId/inference/truth/rejoin, POST} at version 1. Unauthenticated probes returned 401 on both (matched, guard refused) against 404 on a deliberately nonexistent sibling path -- so the routes match rather than falling through.

features.implementation:
Built 2026-09-03, T01+T02 only — T03 stays blocked per this feature's own scope_correction (no persisted ground truth exists anywhere in this system; see T03's own note below). No InferenceWindow dependency taken: T02 compares against column_stats.json directly, which already exists per-artifact and needed no new production step.

REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE BUILDING ON IT, not part of the original task list: schemas/preprocess.py's TagColumnStats never declared `median`/`std`, so FastAPI's own response_model silently stripped both from every GET .../column-stats response even though column_stats.json has carried them since DS-LAKE-005B-A-T07 and three downstream layers (dataset-version.authorized.dto.ts's TagColumnStatsSchema, the client's ArtifactTagColumnStats type, dataset-detail-sheet.tsx's own rendering) already assumed they arrived. Verified live against a real sidecar (artifact 66173c35-…, 22 tags): the object carried std=0.249702/median=0.779 for AI001A2.PV, the HTTP response did not. `std` is the denominator of T02's own z-score — left unfixed, every column would have reported UNKNOWN and the drift signal would not have existed. Fixed at the source (added both fields), additive, verified with a direct construct/dump round-trip.

Design, decided with the user before building: bytes in MinIO (serving-logs/{modelId}/{modelVersionId}/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/hour=HH/{uuid}.parquet, one object per SAMPLED request), index+aggregates in Postgres (new PredictionLog model — objectKey?, objectChecksum?, rowCount, loggedRows, samplingRate, featureStats Json, predictionStats Json, requestedAt). Write path is serving -> backend -> python: apps/serving holds no Postgres/MinIO credentials by design (decisions already on record for MODEL-SERVE-002), so it computes its aggregates locally over the SAME model-ready frame `to_model_ready` already produced (rows_to_predictions now returns `(predictions, scaled)`, not `predictions` alone — its one caller and its tests moved with it) and POSTs a capped raw-row sample plus the aggregates to a new ServingTokenGuard route; the backend forwards only the capped rows to python for the actual object write (apps/python's new prediction_log_service.append/series, plus ObjectStore.list_object_keys, added because nothing public exposed listing before this) and stores the aggregates straight to Postgres itself — python never sees or computes an aggregate. Logging is scheduled via FastAPI BackgroundTasks AFTER the /predict response would already be built, and every step from there is wrapped so a broken/unreachable log sink can never fail or delay the response — live-verified in the unit suite by monkeypatching the log POST to raise a real requests.ConnectionError and asserting /predict still returns 200 with correct predictions.

T02's drift math (apps/backend/src/lib/prediction-drift.ts, pure functions, no I/O): poolFeatureStats combines many requests' sufficient statistics into one exact pooled mean/variance; computeDrift compares that against column_stats.json's mean/std (exact z-score) and ESTIMATES an out-of-range rate via a Normal-CDF approximation against the baseline's own empirical p1/p99 bounds — stated as an estimate, not a count, because PredictionLog stores sufficient statistics, not raw values, so an exact per-value out-of-range rate would need either every raw value (defeats the point of aggregating) or a running histogram this schema does not carry. Thresholds (warnSd 1.5 / criticalSd 3.0 / outOfRangePct 10) reuse the wizard's own field names (MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's list) but are system-wide env defaults in this pass, not persisted per model — MODEL-SERVE-006-T09 is explicitly where those atoms get a real per-model home.

Client: `apps/client/hooks/model/use-monitoring-data.ts` (the existing mock Actual-vs-Predict/Residual charts) was deliberately NOT swapped — SCOPE CORRECTION from the plan's original 'swap the generator' wording. `EvalPoint` requires `actual`/`residual` as non-optional numbers, and both charts' SD-band/residual math structurally depends on them; T03 (ground truth) is blocked, so satisfying that shape would mean fabricating an `actual` value — exactly the plausible-wrong-answer failure this ledger's own global_definition_of_done forbids. A REAL BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED DURING THIS PASS, not by inspection: apps/serving/services/prediction_log.py built `requestedAt` via Python's `datetime.isoformat()`, which emits a `+00:00` offset — the backend's `z.string().datetime()` (no `{offset:true}`) rejects that with a 400, and because the whole ingest call is deliberately wrapped so a logging failure can never break /predict, EVERY logged request was being silently dropped with no symptom anywhere. 1. THE SCOPE CORRECTION THIS FEATURE MADE ON 2026-09-03 IS NOW REVERSED, deliberately. That pass refused to wire the Monitoring page's Actual-vs-Predict/Residual charts because EvalPoint's actual/residual are non-optional and satisfying that shape would have meant fabricating an `actual`. The fix was never to relax the type: those charts now receive ONLY joined rows, so EvalPoint stayed non-optional, the chart components were not modified, and the series simply renders sparsely — one point per lab measurement. The mock generator (lib/mock-lab-data.ts) was left in place because the Evaluation tab still uses its sibling.
