A PRE-EXISTING LIMITATION FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, FLAGGED NOT FIXED: the SQL connector binds a query's start/end as VARCHAR (intergrations/sql_connect.py, `time_col >= start_time` with a python str), so Postgres refuses the comparison against a genuinely TIMESTAMP-typed time column — 'operator does not exist: timestamp without time zone >= character varying'. This is NOT introduced here and is not specific to this feature: materialize_window builds its own widened query the identical way, so MODEL-SERVE-006's SQL window path has the same constraint. Live verification used a text-typed time column, as MODEL-SERVE-006-V03's own fixture must have. Whoever owns the SQL connector should decide whether to cast.

3. RETENTION: truth.parquet is a FOURTH object under the window's own hour prefix, so it inherits whatever reclaims `inference/` — which today is nothing. `inference/` has no sweeper at all, the same gap MODEL-SERVE-004 recorded for models/{modelId}/runs/. This belongs to MODEL-SERVE-007, which should treat a window's own outputs (input.parquet, predictions.parquet, metrics.json, truth.parquet) as one retention class rather than four.

FOLLOW-UP PASS, 2026-09-14 (same day, after review): three gaps the first pass's own gates could not see.

4. BATCH-HEAD STARVATION, FOUND AND FIXED. backOff() returned early when no truth row existed, so a FAILED first join left the window `truth: { is: null }` -- still eligible, still oldest, still at the head of every sweep. backOff now WRITES a row (n=0, all sums 0, targetColumn NULL, failureReason set, nextJoinAfter backed off geometrically); an existing row keeps every statistic it earned and only has its attempt counter, backoff and failureReason updated, so a source that goes down after a successful join cannot erase the pairs that join produced. A successful join clears failureReason, so the field always describes the row's CURRENT state. Migration 20260914160000_model_serve_005_t03_truth_failure_row drops NOT NULL from targetColumn (resolving the target is itself one of the things that can fail) and adds failureReason TEXT -- both widenings, no backfill. Applied live. Proven by MODEL-SERVE-005-V05, which reproduces the bug directly by deleting the row.

5. THE READ SIDE HAD NO TEST AT ANY LEVEL. The live pass drove python and Prisma directly and never entered the service, so the version-grouping refusal -- the rule deciding whether a published RMSE is a number about anything -- shipped unexercised. Nine cases added to inference-window.authorized.service.spec.ts: pooled metrics under one version; TWO versions with different targets -> metrics null, mixedVersions true, each group keeping its own target; nothing joined -> null, not zero; a failure row excluded from metrics but counted in coverage.windowsFailed; the target surviving with zero pairs; maxMissingPct as a max not a mean; metrics and coverage surviving an unreadable pairs object; and rejoinTruthService driving the sweeper once per window, reporting a failed window instead of abandoning the range. Backend jest 643 passed (was 634), 9 failed -- the same nine in untouched modules (auth, plan, workspace, nodes, workspace-plant, model-run controller).

6. READ SHAPE, two additions the fix made necessary: coverage.windowsFailed (windows the sweeper could not ask about, distinct from windows the lab has not reported on -- both show zero pairs, only one is a problem) and a range-level targetColumn. windowsAwaitingTruth now SUBTRACTS the failed windows and floors at zero, so the two counts are disjoint and the coverage strip cannot show one window as both waiting on the lab and failed. The Monitoring tab previously read its target pill from versions[0], and `versions` holds only groups WITH pairs, so a model awaiting its first lab result lost a label that was knowable all along; it now reads the range-level field. joinedThrough is still always the window's own windowEnd -- it carries no information beyond the window row today, and is kept because an incremental join that reads past windowEnd would need it.

features.title: Scheduled Hourly Inference — Windows, Logs, and the Monitoring Record
features.description: Run a promoted model on a fixed cadence, writing one predictions parquet and one metrics document per time window, with per-run logs readable afterwards. This is the feature that makes 'deployed' mean something. It needs no serving process — see decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference.

dependency_notes.MODEL-FLOW-004: SATISFIED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000 re-audit). ORIGINAL: 'HARD, not conventional. Step 4 currently computes its own metrics client-side (see findings), so until it reads the run's real metrics there is no surface on which a metric registry or a monitoring series means anything. Building the schedule first would produce a correct monitoring record beside a screen showing unrelated numbers.' MODEL-FLOW-004 is now in_progress 90 with all 5 tasks completed; phase-5-evaluation.tsx reads real predictions via useDraftRunEvaluation/mpTrainingResultAtom, not a client-side computeFit. T08 can proceed.
dependency_notes.MODEL-FLOW-011: SATISFIED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000 re-audit). ORIGINAL: 'Specifically T04, orphaned-RUNNING reconciliation. MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 observed ONE stranded RUNNING row from ONE nest restart. At 24 windows a day that stops being an incident and becomes a background rate, and every stranded row is a permanent hole in the monitoring record. Reconciliation must exist before the cadence does, not after.' MODEL-FLOW-011 is completed 100%, including T04 (reconcileOrphanedRuns() at boot, trainning-container.authorized.service.ts:53-123) and T05 (never reclaim an adopted run's prefix).
dependency_notes.MODEL-SERVE-002: NOT a dependency, deliberately. Synchronous /predict is a different requirement; this feature must not wait on it and must not build a serving process to get a scheduled run.

findings: THE UNIT IS A TIME WINDOW, NOT A TICK. A scheduler written as 'every hour, read the latest values, predict' loses data permanently on every miss, cannot say which hours are missing, and has no backfill path. A scheduler written as 'ensure a row exists for every window' gets gap detection, backfill and idempotency from one UNIQUE constraint. This is the single decision the whole feature rests on.

SCHEDULED WORK HAS NO CALLER, WHICH CHANGES WHAT FAILURE MEANS. A sync request that fails returns an error to someone who is waiting. A window that fails is observed by nobody. So the feature is not complete when windows succeed — it is complete when a window that DOESN'T run is visible. Hence T10, which is the one task here that must not be cut.

setInterval().unref() IS ADEQUATE HERE, BUT FOR A DIFFERENT REASON THAN IT WAS ADEQUATE FOR THE SWEEPER. MODEL-FLOW-011-T03 chose it because a missed sweep costs nothing — next tick does the work. A missed inference window is a permanent gap. It is still adequate, but ONLY because the tick's job is an idempotent insert keyed on window_start, so a later tick recovers what an earlier one missed. If the tick ever predicts directly, this mechanism becomes wrong.

PI TAGS DO NOT ARRIVE TOGETHER AND THE LAB TARGET ARRIVES MUCH LATER. window_end = now() yields a frame that is structurally complete and factually empty in places — and the model will score it without error, because the columns exist. This is the same mechanism MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 records for the holdout (no imputation, so a hole reaches predict() and depresses the result with no trace), except it recurs every hour instead of once. Hence a deliberate lag (T04) and a per-window missing rate (T05).

A PROMOTE MID-SERIES IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PROCESS CHANGE UNLESS THE VERSION IS PINNED PER WINDOW. Two adjacent points from different model versions render as a step change on the same axis as a real process shift, and someone will spend days on the wrong hypothesis. Pinning also yields shadow evaluation for free: two rows, same window, different versions.

tasks.title: InferenceWindow entity, keyed on (modelVersionId, windowStart)
tasks.detail:
Fields: modelId, modelVersionId, windowStart, windowEnd, status (PENDING|RUNNING|SUCCEEDED|FAILED|SKIPPED), predictionsKey, metricsKey, inputRows, missingPct, imageDigest, runId, startedAt, finishedAt, failureReason.

UNIQUE (modelVersionId, windowStart) IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. It is the idempotency mechanism, so this feature needs no idempotency key of the kind MODEL-SERVE-003-T02 requires — windowStart is the natural key and a repeated insert is a no-op. It also makes gaps queryable (status != 'SUCCEEDED') and makes backfill an insert rather than a code path.

SKIPPED is a real terminal status, not a synonym for FAILED: a window with too few input rows to score was correctly not attempted, and conflating it with a failure would make the staleness alarm cry wolf on a quiet plant.

tasks.title: The tick inserts windows and nothing else
tasks.detail:
setInterval(...).unref() in onModuleInit, matching MODEL-FLOW-011-T03's mechanism and PreprocessingJobService.scheduleStragglerSweep's precedent. Env-configurable, <= 0 disables.

The tick does exactly two things: insert PENDING rows for windows that have none, and reconcile rows stuck in RUNNING past a timeout. IT MUST NOT SCORE ANYTHING. Scoring in the tick reintroduces every property this design exists to avoid — a missed tick becomes a lost window, the interval becomes load-bearing, and a slow run delays the next one. Errors logged and swallowed; anything the tick missed is still eligible next time, which is only true because of T01's key.
tasks.dispatch_order_2026_09_14: BACKFILL STARVED LIVE INFERENCE. dispatchDue claimed PENDING windows `orderBy: { windowStart: 'asc' }` -- oldest first -- with no model scoping and take = INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY, which defaults to 1. A freshly enabled schedule inserts INFERENCE_BACKFILL_HORIZON_HOURS of windows (48 by default) and the tick runs every 5 minutes, so the system replayed two days of history one window at a time -- about four hours -- before it ever scored the CURRENT hour. Two consequences, both observed live: (1) deriveDeployStatuses measures staleness from the most recent SUCCEEDED window, so replaying oldest-first holds that maximum in the past and a perfectly healthy model reports STALE for the entire drain; (2) the claim is global, so ONE model's backlog monopolised the single slot while every other model's live window waited behind it -- the same batch-head starvation MODEL-SERVE-005-V05 had to fix in the ground-truth sweeper, in a second place. Changed to `desc`. Current-hour windows are the newest rows in the table for every model, so live inference always wins the slot and backfill fills in behind it. The trade, taken deliberately: a permanently saturated queue would leave the oldest backfill windows unclaimed -- acceptable because in a monitoring system a fresh reading is worth more than an old one, and a healthy model that looks STALE is a worse failure than a late backfill. INFERENCE_BACKFILL_HORIZON_HOURS and INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY are deliberately UNCHANGED: with live windows no longer queued behind history, the 48-hour backfill is no longer harmful, and lowering the horizon would silently discard monitoring history the operator may want.

tasks.title: infer.py as a second entrypoint on the existing trainer image
tasks.detail:
Reads its window spec from a /claim-style callback exactly as train.py does, resolves the model object and scaler state (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 must have answered where scalers live — this task is blocked in practice until it has), scores, writes predictions.parquet and metrics.json, reports through /log and /complete.

Same image as the trainer so both entrypoints unpickle with the same library versions, and so image_digest provenance works identically. HEED MODEL-FLOW-000-T04's warning: nothing in CI builds images/trainer/Dockerfile, so a correct repo and a stale deployed image are indistinguishable today. Adding an entrypoint makes that worse, because a deployed image without infer.py fails in a way that looks like a scheduler bug. Add the CI build in this task, not later.
tasks.audit_2026_09_01: UNBLOCKED: MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 answered where scalers live — feature_spec.json's scalingParams, one hop off ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey, applied via the existing to_model_ready(..., fitted_params=...). infer.py resolves scaler state the same way T05/T06 above do. Also inherits the serving-host finding: the Docker-daemon spawn this entrypoint runs under is now verified adequate for short-lived containers (decisions.serving_host_undecided, closed for MODEL-SERVE-006).

tasks.title: Window boundaries from a chosen ingestion lag
tasks.detail:
windowEnd = now() - lag, where lag is a configured value someone decided, per model. Do NOT default it to zero and do not derive it from the cadence — freshness and completeness genuinely trade against each other here and the trade must be made deliberately.

Measure before choosing: the 8 tags in the observed run's feature_columns (AI001A2.PV, AI206.PV, TI202/203/205/206/207.PV, Spgr_in_feed_Header_1) against RYGPDH01, worst-case arrival. The lab target's own latency is a different and much longer number and belongs to T08, not here — inference needs features only.
tasks.diagnosis_2026_09_14: AN EMPTY FETCH USED TO HAVE ONE MESSAGE FOR TWO OPPOSITE CAUSES. materialize_window raised 'The source returned no rows for this window's fetch range [...] -- check the schedule's fetch config and tag selection' whenever the frame came back empty, whether the historian had answered with no samples or had never been reached at all. The second case is the common one on a dev machine and on any host outside the plant network, and the message sent the reader to audit a config that was correct. The information was never missing: DataService.fetch already records a per-tag status of ok/partial/failed and keeps the first error string for every failed tag, and _run_job converts a transport exception into exactly that -- but from_pi_response builds the frame from datapoints alone, so the diagnosis was discarded one call before it was needed. Added _diagnose_empty_pi_fetch, which reads those per-tag statuses and, when the SOURCE reported failures, raises 'Could not read the source ... the source failed for every tag: <connector's own error, verbatim>'. Deliberately not pattern-matched into categories: any guess layered on top is the very thing being removed. Errors are de-duplicated (one unreachable host produces the same sentence once per tag) and capped at three distinct reasons, comfortably inside the scheduler's existing 2000-char failureReason slice. When every tag ANSWERED and simply had no data, the message stays a no-data message -- that case is a legitimate empty window and must not be dressed up as an error.

tasks.title: Record inputRows and missingPct per window
tasks.detail: On the row, not only inside the output object, so a series query can join them without opening parquet. Without this, a prediction series that starts wandering is indistinguishable between real process drift and a sensor that stopped reporting — and the second is far more common. Same rule and same reason as MODEL-FLOW-010-T06's insistence that the holdout's missing rate be published beside every figure.

tasks.title: Partitioned output layout for the monitoring record
tasks.detail:
inference/{modelId}/{modelVersionId}/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/hour=HH/predictions.parquet, plus metrics.json alongside. Hive-style so a date range reads without listing everything.

KEPT SEPARATE FROM drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/predictions.parquet ON PURPOSE: that object is the test-split prediction, immutable and backward-looking; this one is an append-only operational record with different retention and a different access pattern. Also a different root from drafts/, which the findings note is already shared by two entities.

Do not couple the read path to one-file-per-hour. 8,760 objects per model-year is fine for MinIO and slow to scan; daily compaction is not needed on day one but becomes needed, and a reader that assumes hourly files has to be rewritten then.

tasks.title: Pin modelVersionId at window creation, and expose version boundaries
tasks.detail: Already in T01's key; this task is the read side. Any series rendering must be able to say where a version changed, because the alternative is a step change attributed to the process. Falls out for free: two rows for one windowStart under different versions is a shadow comparison, which is the safe way to exercise a candidate — including the current r2 = -2.4068 model — without promoting it.
tasks.pass_b_note_2026_09_10: Write side (pinning modelVersionId at window creation) was already completed in Pass A. The READ side named in this task's own detail ('the change is the read side... must be able to say where a version changed') is NOT built this pass — no client UI renders a version-boundary marker on a monitoring series yet. Left open; the seam it would read from (PredictionSeriesPoint/ LivePredictionPoint's modelVersionId, already carried through and explicitly ignored by LivePredictionChart per MODEL-SERVE-005's own exploration) still exists unchanged.

tasks.title: Metric registry — derived from predictions, recomputable, selectable from the UI
tasks.detail:
Per decisions.metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not_computed_at_fit. One definition set, applied to test-split predictions for evaluation and to window predictions for monitoring, so the two are the same number computed the same way.

Each registry entry declares whether it is BACKFILLABLE from (actual, predicted) plus run_manifest scalars, or requires inputs not retained. That flag is not documentation — it is what stops a comparison table silently mixing metrics that exist for all history with metrics that exist only for new runs.

mpSelectedMetricsAtom becomes a real selection over this registry instead of a filter over browser-computed values. THAT SUBSTITUTION IS ONLY MEANINGFUL AFTER MODEL-FLOW-004 (see findings): applied to today's phase-3-evaluation.tsx it would change which locally-computed numbers are displayed and nothing else.

tasks.title: Persist the schedule, and adopt the existing deploy atoms rather than new ones
tasks.detail:
Per-model schedule config: enabled, cadence, lag (T04), and the five fields phase-4-deploy.tsx already holds unpersisted in the store — autoRetrain, warnSd, criticalSd, driftMonitor, driftThresholdPct (per MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's field list). USE THOSE NAMES. A parallel set means the wizard and the scheduler describe the same setting in two vocabularies, and reconciling them later is worse than adopting them now.

This is the change that lets phase-4-deploy.tsx render those controls honestly, which its own comment declines to do today for the stated reason that nothing persists them.

tasks.title: Staleness alarm on the absence of successful windows
tasks.detail:
If no window has reached SUCCEEDED for longer than a configured multiple of the cadence, raise it. DO NOT CUT THIS TASK. Every other task in this feature makes the monitoring record trustworthy; this is the only one that reveals when the record has stopped being written. A drift dashboard with no incoming data looks calm, and calm is exactly the wrong signal.

SKIPPED windows must not silence the alarm and must not trigger it either — they are a legitimate quiet plant, and treating them as either extreme makes the alarm useless in one direction or the other.

tasks.title: Backfill by inserting windows, with no separate code path
tasks.detail: A range request inserts PENDING rows for windows that have none. The worker cannot distinguish backfill from live, which is the point — a second code path is a second set of bugs, and it would be exercised only during incidents. T01's UNIQUE constraint means over-requesting a range is harmless.

tasks.title: Derive deployStatus from the last successful window
tasks.detail:
Per decisions.deploy_status_currently_asserts_something_untrue. Today `updateModel(modelId, { deployStatus: 'running' })` writes a claim nothing backs. Once windows exist, that claim has a real referent and must be READ from it, not written beside it. Leaving both means two sources of truth for 'is this deployed', and the stale one wins whenever someone forgets to update it.

Phase-4-deploy.tsx's own structure survives this change unharmed: deploy stays a second write after save, and a failed deploy still leaves a saved model. What changes is that the second write enables a schedule instead of setting a string.
tasks.warmup_2026_09_14: A BROKEN SCHEDULE LOOKED LIKE A HEALTHY WARM-UP. classifyDeployStatus returned 'initializing' for any enabled schedule that was stale and had never succeeded, regardless of whether its windows were already coming back FAILED. The only escape was `failing`, which requires THREE consecutive failed terminal windows -- the right bar for a mature schedule with history behind it, and the wrong one for a new one, which reaches three failures only after three cadences (three hours at the default). Until then a completely broken source was indistinguishable from a warm-up. Added a required `hasFailedWindows` input: for a schedule that has NEVER succeeded, one failed window is already evidence it is not warming up. Required rather than optional-with-a-default precisely so a future caller cannot silently reinherit the old behaviour. Computed free from the take-3 query deriveDeployStatuses and getStatusService already run -- no extra round trip -- and sound because a never-succeeded schedule's terminal windows are all FAILED by definition. Status stays derived at read time, so a later success heals it to 'running' with no sticky error.

acceptance_criteria: A promoted model produces one predictions object and one metrics document per window, on the configured cadence, with no manual action.
Every window is queryable by its own boundaries, and windows that did not succeed are listable as gaps.
A missed or failed window can be backfilled by requesting its range, through the same worker that runs live windows.
Requesting an already-present window is a no-op — enforced by a unique constraint, not by a service check.
Each window records the model version that scored it, pinned at creation, and a series can show where the version changed.
Each window records its input row count and missing rate on the row itself.
Window boundaries respect a configured ingestion lag; the lag is a chosen value, not a default of zero.
Per-window logs are readable after the container exits, through the same path training logs already use.
The absence of successful windows raises an alarm; SKIPPED windows neither raise nor suppress it.
Evaluation and monitoring metrics come from one registry applied to stored predictions, and each entry states whether it is backfillable.
Adding a metric to the registry requires no retraining and no refit to populate it for past runs — for backfillable entries.
deployStatus is derived from the last successful window; no caller sets it directly.
The schedule reuses the field names the wizard's existing deploy atoms already use.

verification.description: THE ONLY TEST THAT DISTINGUISHES A WORKING SCHEDULER FROM ONE THAT HAS NOT YET MISSED: stop the scheduler for three cadence periods, restart it, and confirm all three absent windows are (a) visible as gaps, (b) backfillable, and (c) that backfilling them produces output indistinguishable from live windows. A test that only asserts normal windows succeed cannot tell these apart.

Kill the backend mid-window, restart, and confirm the row reaches a terminal status rather than staying RUNNING. This is MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's observed orphan, reproduced deliberately at a cadence where it will recur. If MODEL-FLOW-011-T04 has not landed, this verification fails by design and is the evidence that the dependency is real.

Run a window against data with a KNOWN hole in one feature tag, and confirm both that missingPct records it and that the prediction is not silently produced as if the frame were complete. Running against clean data proves only that the happy path works, which is not what T05 exists for.
verification.result_2026_09_10: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-10, at the python materialize_window layer (the layer this verification is actually about): a SQL fixture carrying 60 rows/60 minutes with ONE deliberate NULL in TI202.PV was fetched, feature-computed, and trimmed; missingPct came back 0.0794% (1 Bad cell / 1260 total, exact), the held row was DROPPED (60 -> 59), and the written parquet — read back from real MinIO — confirmed zero rows carrying a Bad TI202.PV status. Never imputed: verified by absence, not by a null-check. features.title: Retention Classes in Object Storage — the Storage Foundation
features.must_land_before: MODEL-SERVE-006-T06. That task writes the first inference/ object; whichever layout is chosen, deciding after it lands turns a free choice into a migration.
features.description: Make an object's RETENTION CLASS legible to storage tooling, so that 'may be reclaimed' is not knowable only from application code. Moves no existing bytes.
features.audit_note: REVISED 2026-08-25 after reading apps/python/.../object_store.py. Three claims made when this feature was first drafted were wrong and are corrected in the findings below, not silently edited: the key layout (a), the cost of multi-bucket (b), and what a bucket lifecycle rule can actually express (c). The correction to (c) weakens this feature's original headline rationale, which is why T01 is now a decision to be made rather than a layout to implement.
findings:
CORRECTED (a) — `datasets/` IS THE BUCKET NAME, NOT A PREFIX. The module docstring renders the layout as `datasets/{datasetId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/data.parquet`, which reads as a prefixed key and is what an earlier draft of this feature assumed. The key helpers disagree: artifact_prefix returns f"{dataset_id}/artifacts/{artifact_id}/", version_key returns f"{dataset_id}/{version_id}.parquet", tmp_key returns f"{dataset_id}/tmp/...". Dataset keys begin with a BARE UUID and have no named root at all. The only named roots in the store are models/, drafts/ and feature-presets/.

CONSEQUENCE: a key-to-bucket resolver cannot dispatch on the first segment, because dataset keys have nothing there to dispatch on. It must dispatch on the roots that DO exist and treat rootless keys as the dataset default. The docstring should also be fixed to say `bucket / key` — it is the direct cause of this misreading and will cause it again.

CONFIRMED — `drafts/` IS SHARED, AND THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE THIRD SEGMENT. Previously inferred from one observed gold_object_key; now confirmed against the code. drafts/{id}/runs/{id}/… is a model run output (draft_run_key, MODEL-FLOW-003-T08) and drafts/{id}/artifacts/{id}/… is a dataset draft artifact (the observed gold_object_key). is_draft_run_key already tests exactly this shape — 4 segments after the root with parts[1] == 'runs' — so the discriminator a resolver needs is a predicate that already exists and is already tested.

CORRECTED (b) — THERE ARE NO HARDCODED BUCKET LITERALS, AND THE CONSTRUCTOR ALREADY TAKES A BUCKET. An earlier draft budgeted an audit for scattered literals. There are none: self.bucket is set once in __init__ from settings.S3_BUCKET and every method reads that one attribute (~15 sites, all reads). ObjectStore.__init__ already accepts an explicit `bucket` argument.

So multi-bucket is NOT a signature change threaded through fifteen methods — it is a FACTORY returning a per-bucket instance, plus a change at the few places that construct or hold an ObjectStore. _presign_minio is already an instance-level cache, which fits per-bucket instances rather than fighting them. This is materially cheaper than the earlier estimate and is the single biggest correction in this pass.

CORRECTED (c) — A BUCKET LIFECYCLE RULE CANNOT EXPRESS THE `models` RETENTION RULE, AND THE CODEBASE ALREADY SAYS SO. ensure_tmp_lifecycle_rule's own docstring: committed artifact prefixes are never expressed there because they need a reference check 'which a bucket lifecycle rule cannot do — only application-level cleanup is authoritative'. 'Retained while referenced' is exactly that kind of check.

This feature's original rationale — separation makes retention expressible at the bucket level — is therefore HALF WRONG and is restated: separation does not express the right rule, it prevents a wrong rule from REACHING the wrong objects. That is still worth having, and it is a narrower claim than the one first made.

THE TAG MECHANISM FOR THIS PROBLEM ALREADY EXISTS AND WAS BUILT FOR THE SAME REASON. TMP_LIFECYCLE_TAG_KEY's doc comment explains that S3/MinIO Prefix filters are literal and anchored, never wildcards, so 'tmp/ under any dataset' is not expressible as a prefix rule — hence an object TAG plus one bucket-wide rule. The identical constraint applies to a models bucket holding BOTH models/… and drafts/…/runs/… : two roots, so no single Prefix rule covers it, so a tag is needed there too. Any option chosen in T01 should reuse this mechanism rather than invent a second one.

PRIOR DECISION AGAINST A SECOND BUCKET, WITH A STATED REASON. PRESET_ROOT's comment: a prefix inside the existing bucket 'rather than a bucket of its own: ensure_bucket() has no runtime caller in this service, so a second bucket would need new bootstrap while a prefix needs none.' Confirmed: ensure_bucket has no automatic caller, and ensure_tmp_lifecycle_rule's comment records that docker-compose.yml does not declare MinIO at all — it runs as an uncommitted minio-local container. So every bucket is a manual, undocumented per-environment ops step.

This feature must engage with that decision rather than step around it. What presets did not have, and inference does, is a DIFFERENT RETENTION CLASS — presets and datasets are both reclaimable-with-a-reference-check, whereas an inference record is never reclaimable. That is a reason the earlier decision did not weigh, not a reason to overrule it.

`models/` MAY HAVE NO LIVE OBJECTS AT ALL. MODEL_ROOT, model_run_prefix and model_run_key all exist, but MODEL-FLOW-003-T08 routed live writes to draft_run_key, and MODEL-FLOW-007-T10 adopts by pointer without moving bytes — so nothing may ever write under models/. UNVERIFIED (needs a bucket listing), but if true, a 'models' bucket would hold only drafts/…/runs/… keys, which is confusing enough to be worth knowing before naming anything.

tasks.title: DECIDE the retention-class mechanism — three options, one recommendation
tasks.detail:
DECIDED: OPTION B - one bucket, retention-class object tag on every write. Implemented as RETENTION_TAG_KEY plus RETENTION_SWEEPABLE / RETENTION_REFERENCED / RETENTION_PERMANENT in object_store.py, mirrored in artifact-keys.ts.

REJECTED OPTION C (tags plus a dedicated `inference` bucket), which this task originally recommended: its entire advantage was that `inference/` held no objects yet. It held 31 by the time this was decided - MODEL-SERVE-006-T06 landed first - so C had become a copy migration plus a bucket-aware read path, for the one class that is never swept anyway.

REJECTED OPTION A (three buckets): moves every dataset read behind a per-bucket factory and reverses PRESET_ROOT's recorded reasoning (a prefix needs no bootstrap, a bucket does) without evidence that would justify reversing it. Note the `models` bucket already exists and is EMPTY, and `S3_BUCKET_MODEL` in .env is read by no code - a dangling env var that makes the store look split when it is not. Recorded in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.

CONSEQUENCE: T04 (per-bucket factory) is not applicable and V05 is out of scope. Both are marked so rather than deleted.

ORIGINAL TASK TEXT:
This was drafted as 'define three buckets'. Findings (c) and the PRESET_ROOT precedent make that a choice rather than a conclusion, so it is recorded as one.

OPTION A — three buckets (datasets / models / inference). Strongest isolation: a lifecycle rule or access grant scoped to a bucket cannot reach another class even if authored carelessly. Costs what PRESET_ROOT's comment names: two more manual bucket-creation steps in an environment where MinIO is not even in docker-compose, plus the factory from T02.

OPTION B — one bucket, retention-class OBJECT TAG on every write, lifecycle rules keyed on tag. Matches the mechanism already proven here for tmp/, needs no bootstrap, no factory, no resolver. Weaker: nothing stops a rule authored against a prefix or against no filter at all from reaching every class, and the tag is only as good as the writer that sets it.

OPTION C (RECOMMENDED) — tag everything by retention class per Option B, AND give `inference` its own bucket. inference is the one class that is never reclaimable, grows without bound, and has zero existing objects — so its bucket is free, needs no migration, and is the one place where 'an operator cannot accidentally point a rule at this' is worth a manual bootstrap step. datasets and models stay co-located under tags, which keeps faith with the PRESET_ROOT decision instead of quietly reversing it.

WHICHEVER IS CHOSEN, RECORD IT AS A DECISION WITH ITS REJECTED ALTERNATIVES. The next person to face 'new bucket or new prefix' will read whatever is written here, the way this task read PRESET_ROOT's comment.

tasks.title: Tag every write with its retention class
tasks.detail:
POST-REVIEW CORRECTION: there are THREE write paths, not the two this task was completed against. `copy_prefix` mints a new object via `copy_object`, which never goes through `put_object_stream` and which carries the SOURCE object's tags - so a legacy untagged source produced an untagged object written AFTER this feature shipped, contradicting the acceptance criterion outright. Not hypothetical: DS-LAKE-025's Save Dataset copy is an active caller. Now tags from the DESTINATION key (a copy out of drafts/ into a dataset namespace is a root change and so possibly a class change), covered by test_copy_prefix_tags_the_object_it_mints.

Done in two halves, because one was not enough. SERVER-SIDE WRITES: `_with_retention_tag` merges the class into `put_object_stream`'s tags (covering put_frame and put_object_bytes) and into `put_json`, which calls put_object directly and would otherwise have left every JSON sidecar untagged while every Parquet test passed - V04 exists for exactly that. The tmp `lifecycle` tag is preserved alongside, not replaced.

PRESIGNED UPLOADS - NOT IN THE ORIGINAL TASK, and the larger half: trainer run outputs, batch prediction outputs and an inference window's predictions.parquet are PUT straight to MinIO by a container holding a presigned URL. The server never performs those writes and cannot tag them at write time. `ObjectStore.tag_retention` applies the class on the first server-side touch afterwards, called from presign_run_object / presign_prediction_job_object / presign_inference_window_object. It refuses tmp keys (set_object_tags replaces the whole tag set and would drop `lifecycle=tmp`) and never raises - a missing label must not fail a request.

ORIGINAL TASK TEXT:
Required under all three options in T01 — it is what makes the class legible to tooling at all, and under Option B it is the entire mechanism.

put_frame already sets an object tag conditionally (`if "/tmp/" in key`). Generalise that: derive the retention class from the key and tag every write, in put_object_stream so it covers put_frame and put_object_bytes together. put_json goes DIRECTLY to self._client.put_object and bypasses that path — the module's own comments flag it as un-refactored — so it needs the tag added too, or every JSON sidecar (including run_manifest.json) is written untagged.

Classes: SWEEPABLE (dataset drafts/artifacts, tmp, presets), REFERENCED (model run outputs), PERMANENT (inference records). Note that REFERENCED still cannot be enforced by a lifecycle rule — finding (c) — so its tag is a label for humans and audits, not an enforcement point. Say so where the constant is defined, or someone will write a rule against it and believe it works.

tasks.title: One key-to-class resolver, built on the predicates that exist
tasks.detail:
`class_for_key` in object_store.py, `classForKey` in artifact-keys.ts. Dispatches on the named roots; the drafts/ branch CALLS is_draft_run_key rather than re-deriving its segment test. The TS side had no predicates at all, so `isDraftRunKey` was written there first - a divergence risk named in both files, since only python's is exercised by the live-MinIO suite. Module docstring fixed to render `bucket / key`: it was the direct cause of finding (a)'s misreading.

ORIGINAL TASK TEXT:
class_for_key(key) in object_store.py with its TS twin in artifact-keys.ts. Dispatch on the roots that actually exist, per finding (a) — NOT on the first segment, which is a bare UUID for dataset keys:

  inference/…                    → PERMANENT
  models/…                       → REFERENCED
  drafts/… + is_draft_run_key    → REFERENCED
  drafts/… + /artifacts/         → SWEEPABLE
  feature-presets/…              → SWEEPABLE
  anything else (rootless)       → SWEEPABLE

The drafts/ branch MUST call is_draft_run_key rather than re-deriving the segment test — the two would otherwise disagree about the same key and only one of them is under test.

The rootless default is not a fallback: it is the historically correct answer for every dataset object ever written, all of which are bucket-less and root-less by construction.

tasks.title: Per-bucket ObjectStore factory — only if T01 chooses A or C
tasks.detail:
NOT APPLICABLE under T01's Option B - there is one bucket, so there is nothing for a per-bucket factory to resolve. Kept rather than deleted so the next reader sees that it was considered and why it went away.

ORIGINAL TASK TEXT:
Per finding (b) this is a factory, not a refactor: ObjectStore.__init__ already accepts `bucket`, and no method holds a literal. store_for(bucket) caching one instance per bucket name, plus store_for_key(key) composing it with T03's resolver.

THE REAL WORK IS AT THE CONSTRUCTION SITES, NOT IN THIS CLASS. artifact_service and its siblings hold a single ObjectStore today; a flow spanning classes (infer.py reads a model, reads the gold parquet, writes an inference record — three classes) needs the store resolved per key rather than per service. Audit who constructs one before changing anything.

Under Option C only `inference` is separate, so the factory has two entries and the blast radius is small. Under Option A every dataset read moves too, which is the expensive half.

tasks.title: Write inference/ into its chosen home from the very first object
tasks.detail:
Resolved by T01 rather than implemented: under Option B `inference/`'s home is the one bucket it is already in, so the 31 existing objects need no migration and there is no new bucket to bootstrap. They are classed PERMANENT by the resolver and tagged on the first server-side touch (T02's presign half).

Free today, a migration after MODEL-SERVE-006-T06 lands. Nothing has written an inference object yet.

Under Option A or C this means the bucket exists and is bootstrapped BEFORE the first scheduled window runs — and since ensure_bucket has no runtime caller (finding: PRESET_ROOT precedent), 'exists' means someone did it by hand and wrote down that they did. tasks.title: Add bucket and gold_artifact_id to run_manifest.json
tasks.detail:
POST-REVIEW CORRECTION - THIS TASK WAS A NO-OP WHEN FIRST MARKED COMPLETE. `bucket` was added to `artifact_service.presign_artifact`'s returned dict, but the route declares `response_model=ArtifactPresignResponse` and FastAPI DROPS any key that model does not declare, silently and with no error at any layer. The field never reached the wire, so goldBucket was undefined in the claim payload and gold_bucket would have been null in every manifest.

Caught because the only verification run was the ABSENCE case (a legacy manifest without gold_bucket still resolves), which passes identically whether the field works or is being stripped - a test that could not fail. Fixed by declaring `bucket` on ArtifactPresignResponse, proved by round-tripping a real presign response through the response model (returns 'datasets'), and pinned by test_artifact_presign_response_declares_bucket, asserted against the SCHEMA rather than the service because the schema is the boundary that decides whether the field exists at all.

`gold_bucket` and `gold_artifact_id` added to build_run_manifest. The bucket had to be threaded from python: NestJS has no S3 configuration of its own, so presign_artifact now returns `bucket`, the claim payload passes it as `goldBucket`, and the trainer reads it with `.get`. `goldArtifactId` is read off the ModelTrainingRun ROW, not parsed out of the key.

NOT YET VISIBLE IN A WRITTEN MANIFEST: nothing in CI builds images/trainer, so these fields appear only after a manual rebuild and tag bump. Verified instead that a manifest LACKING them still resolves - run 9d194266 (real, pre-feature) reads back with gold_bucket None and its rootless gold key still classes SWEEPABLE.

ORIGINAL TASK TEXT:
gold_bucket makes the manifest self-describing — a reader years later needs no resolver to find the object. gold_artifact_id (b9e25f8d in the observed run) is the durable reference: it is ALREADY IN the key as a path segment, so this promotes a substring to a field. A reference parsed out of a path breaks when the path shape changes; a field does not.

Both, not either. A manifest lacking gold_bucket resolves via T03's default, which is correct for every manifest written so far.

NOTE the naming trap finding (a) created: gold_object_key's value is a KEY relative to a bucket, and the docstring's rendering of it as `datasets/...` is what made an earlier reading treat the bucket as part of the path. Fix that docstring in this task.

tasks.title: Write down each class's rule where an operator will see it
tasks.detail:
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md gained an Object Storage Retention section: the three classes, what tooling can and cannot enforce (referenced CANNOT, stated plainly), the untagged legacy objects, the presigned-upload gap, the manual bucket bootstrap, the unused S3_BUCKET_MODEL, and the trainer-image rebuild requirement.

ORIGINAL TASK TEXT:
Per finding (c), state plainly what tooling CAN and CANNOT enforce: SWEEPABLE is expressible as a tag-filtered lifecycle rule (the tmp/ rule already proves the mechanism); PERMANENT is expressible as the absence of any rule; REFERENCED IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE and depends on MODEL-FLOW-011-T05's run-level guard plus ArtifactCleanupService.

Recording the limit is the point. A retention scheme that looks fully enforced but has one class enforced only by application code is more dangerous than one that admits it, because the next person will trust the appearance.

Also record the bootstrap steps T05 needs, since ensure_bucket has no automatic caller and MinIO is not in docker-compose.

features.ordering_violation: MISSED. This feature carried `must_land_before: MODEL-SERVE-006-T06` and T06 shipped first. features.title: Live prediction surface — continuous predicted series, drift at ingest, and actuals plotted at the rate they genuinely arrive
features.description: The Actual-vs-Predict and Residual charts on the Monitoring tab are correctly empty, not broken: MODEL-SERVE-005-T03 feeds them only JOINED pairs, and a `.lab` target reports hours or days apart, so most windows hold zero pairs. The ask is a real-time comparison. This feature delivers the half that is physically available — a continuously predicted series, drift computed as inputs arrive, and a much shorter prediction cadence — and states plainly that the ACTUAL side cannot be denser than the lab, rather than fabricating one.
features.placement_note: FILED AS ITS OWN FEATURE, DELIBERATELY. The subject spans MODEL-SERVE-005-T03 (the truth join, InferenceWindowTruth), MODEL-SERVE-006 (InferenceWindow, the scheduler) and MODEL-SERVE-002 (synchronous /predict), all of which read completed/100. This ledger's convention for that is a task under MODEL-SERVE-001 with a placement pointer — but T09 through T23 each carry such a pointer apologising for sitting in a feature titled 'Model Version Registry', and this is larger than any of them. Same reasoning DS-LAKE-005B-D used when it refused to file a Python stats service inside a feature titled 'Frontend viewport migration'. NOTE ON NUMBERING: a two-axis deploy/monitoring status proposal earlier in this session drafted MODEL-SERVE-001-T24 through T30 and V18 through V22; if those landed, nothing here collides, but re-check before assuming any id is free.
findings: THE SCREEN IS WORKING. THAT IS THE STARTING FACT, NOT A COMPLAINT ABOUT THE ASK. The rendered message ('Windows have been scored, but no lab measurement has arrived for them yet. The lab has up to 24h to report; the earliest scored window becomes eligible at Sep 18, 08:00') is EmptyTruth's branch 5, with truthLagMinutes and earliestEligibleAt supplied by MODEL-SERVE-001-T18's own fix. The coverage strip reads 0 of 1 windows joined / 0 paired / 1 awaiting — exactly T18's cause (A), NOTHING IS DUE YET. Before building anything, confirm the current state is still (A) and not (B) through (G): T18 enumerates six other causes that produce a visually identical blank chart, and four of them are genuine faults. Its own root-cause pass is the cheapest read in this feature.

RE-FETCHING THE TARGET TAG FOR A LIVE ACTUAL IS THE EXACT TRAP THIS LEDGER CLOSED ON 2026-09-14, AND IT FAILS SILENTLY. decisions.ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_target_tag records it verbatim: the live PI path is a TimeWeighted/Average summary (PIWebAPI.getAverageValue -> streamSet.get_summaries_ad_hoc) and PI HOLDS A SPARSE .lab TAG'S LAST VALUE BETWEEN SAMPLES, so inheriting the schedule's own fetchConfig summary settings returns a plausible number for EVERY interval — including every interval in which no lab measurement was ever taken — and publishes a confident R2 computed against a held value. ground_truth_service.py therefore overrides cal_basis to EventWeighted and runs a Count PROBE first, keeping only intervals an event actually occurred in. A 'real-time actual' built by dropping that probe is not a faster version of this feature; it is the defect the probe exists to prevent.

A RESIDUAL CANNOT BE DENSER THAN THE ACTUAL, BY DEFINITION. residual = predicted - actual (lib/live-error.ts, matching lib/model-evaluation.ts's own sign convention). So 'real-time Residual Analysis' is unachievable at any cadence faster than the lab reports, no matter what is built. What CAN be continuous is the predicted series and a band derived from the model's own recorded error — which is a DIFFERENT chart from a residual, and calling it one would be a metric wearing another metric's name. See openDecisions.

THE PREDICTED SIDE IS ALREADY CONTINUOUS-CAPABLE AND ALREADY LOGGED — THE GAP IS WHAT DRIVES IT. MODEL-SERVE-002 shipped a warm synchronous /predict (apps/serving, port 8100, 30s descriptor TTL) and MODEL-SERVE-005-T01 shipped PredictionLog, sampled per request at SERVING_LOG_SAMPLE_RATE and live-verified (40 requests at rate 0.5 produced exactly 20 rows). The 'Live Predictions (sampled)' section at the bottom of this very screenshot reads that stream. Nothing calls /predict on a cadence, so the stream only fills when something external pushes rows. The scheduled plane fills InferenceWindow instead, hourly.

THE TWO PLANES ARE SEPARATE BY DECISION, AND MERGING THEM IS EXPLICITLY FORBIDDEN. decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference keeps scheduled inference off the serving process entirely; MODEL-SERVE-001-T10 Part A found that Input Data and Monitoring's Live Predictions read the /predict plane which a schedule NEVER writes, measured TM2's PredictionLog at zero rows, and its own item (6) states the rule: 'a console that silently pools /predict logs and window logs into one feed recreates that confusion in a new place.' MODEL-SERVE-001-T17 then made drift and PSI dispatch on InferenceSchedule ROW PRESENCE rather than on which table happens to have rows. So the first real question in this feature is WHICH PLANE feeds a continuous chart — not how fast to run it.

'REAL-TIME' TODAY MEANS HOURLY, AND TWO SEPARATE NUMBERS SET THAT. INFERENCE_TICK_INTERVAL_MS is 300000 (5 minutes) and is only the dispatch sweep; the cadence is per-schedule (cadenceMinutes, 60 in the observed case) and windowEnd = now - (lag + cadence) after MODEL-SERVE-001-T11's fix. So a scored point today lands roughly lag+cadence behind wall clock by construction. MODEL-SERVE-001-T09 already decided against polling the status endpoint faster than the tick on the stated ground that 'anything shorter than that interval is load with no information in it' — the same argument applies to any UI refresh built here, and applies in reverse to shortening the cadence: a shorter cadence is the only thing that actually makes the series denser.

SHORTENING THE CADENCE IS NOT FREE AND HAS A MEASURED FLOOR. Each scheduled window spawns a real container (MODEL-SERVE-006-T03, MODE=infer on the trainer image, cold start 3-5s, which decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference called 'noise at a one-hour cadence' — it is not noise at a one-minute one). INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY defaults to 1, and MODEL-SERVE-006-T02's dispatch_order_2026_09_14 already had to flip the claim to `desc` because a 48-hour backfill monopolised that single slot for about four hours. A short cadence multiplies both the container count and the backfill depth against the same one slot. The synchronous /predict path has no such cost — it is a warm process with an LRU model cache — which is the real argument for which plane should drive a dense series.

INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS SCALES WITH CADENCE AND WILL SKIP EVERY SHORT WINDOW IF LEFT ALONE. MODEL-SERVE-001-T14 made minRows per-schedule (deriveMinRows from fetchConfig.intervalTime), and its own regression test is a 5-minute-interval schedule receiving 10 rows that the old global 30 would have SKIPPED. A 5-minute cadence at a 1-minute interval yields 5 rows; the derivation handles that correctly, but only if the new cadence flows through putScheduleService so minRows is recomputed — it is written unconditionally on every enable/update precisely for this. Changing cadence without re-enabling would leave a stale floor and SKIP every window, which reads as 'no data' and is not.

PSI IS UNKNOWN ON EVERY EXISTING MODEL AND WILL STAY THAT WAY REGARDLESS OF CADENCE. psiRefEdges are computed at GOLD-write time only; MODEL-SERVE-001-T17 confirmed live that TM2's spec is featureVersion 2 with no edges at all, so PSI renders UNKNOWN until the dataset artifact is rebuilt — a user action, not a gap. MODEL-SERVE-001-T27's rule stands: UNKNOWN and INSUFFICIENT_DATA must never fold into Normal. Its sample floor is bin_count x 20, so at 10 bins a 5-minute window contributes 5 rows against a 200-sample floor and PSI stays insufficient for roughly 40 windows whatever the cadence. Z-SCORE IS DIFFERENT and is already per-window (InferenceWindow.featureStats, T17), so it genuinely does get denser with a shorter cadence.

EvalPoint's actual AND residual ARE NON-OPTIONAL ON PURPOSE, AND THAT REFUSAL IS ON RECORD. MODEL-SERVE-005's own implementation note records the scope correction: the Monitoring charts were NOT swapped to real data at first because both charts' SD-band and residual math structurally require ground truth, and 'satisfying that shape would have meant fabricating an actual value, exactly the plausible-wrong-answer failure this ledger's own global_definition_of_done forbids'. T03 then fed them ONLY joined rows, leaving the type non-optional and the series sparse. Any change that puts a predicted-only point into these charts must not relax that type — it needs its own series or its own chart.

THE SQL CONNECTOR CANNOT FILTER A TIMESTAMP COLUMN, AND THAT BOUNDS ANY SHORT-WINDOW SQL PATH. Recorded twice (MODEL-SERVE-005's implementation note, and decisions.ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_target_tag): intergrations/sql_connect.py binds the range as VARCHAR, so Postgres refuses the comparison against a genuinely TIMESTAMP-typed time column. MODEL-SERVE-005-T03's live verification had to use a text-typed column to sidestep it. A denser cadence issues far more range queries, so a SQL-sourced schedule multiplies exposure to a defect that belongs to the connector and is still unfixed.

predicted_gets_denser_actual_does_not.chosen: This feature makes the PREDICTED series and the DRIFT signal near-real-time. The ACTUAL series keeps arriving at the lab's own rate, through the existing event-presence-probed truth join, unchanged.
predicted_gets_denser_actual_does_not.rationale: Per the findings, the actual is a sparse lab measurement and the only way to make it dense is to read PI's held value, which is the specific failure decisions.ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_target_tag exists to prevent. Making the predicted side dense is genuinely useful on its own — it answers 'is the model producing sane output right now', which today has no surface at all between hourly windows.
predicted_gets_denser_actual_does_not.consequence: The Actual-vs-Predict chart becomes a dense predicted line with sparse actual points on it, and the coverage strip must say so rather than letting a reader count the actual points and conclude the model ran that few times. The Residual chart stays exactly as sparse as it is now; see openDecisions.

rejected.Drop the Count probe so every interval y: Publishes a confident R2 against a value nobody measured. Refused once already, with the mechanism recorded.
rejected.Interpolate between lab samples: Same outcome by a different route, and worse because it looks deliberate. This ledger has refused the fabricate-a-plausible-number trade four times (unpersisted scaler params, a Bad cell's 0.0 reading as a measurement, mark-Bad on an operating window, an RMSE over one pair).

the_dense_series_comes_from_the_serving_.chosen: The continuous predicted series is driven through apps/serving's synchronous /predict and lands in PredictionLog. The scheduled InferenceWindow plane keeps its own cadence and its own record.
the_dense_series_comes_from_the_serving_.rationale: The cost comparison is not close: a scheduled point spawns a container with a 3-5s cold start against INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY of 1, while /predict is a warm process with a bytes-bounded model LRU and a 30s descriptor cache, already load-verified at 90/90 requests across a promote (MODEL-SERVE-002-V02). It is also the plane the Live Predictions section and the Input Data tab already read, so the surface exists.
the_dense_series_comes_from_the_serving_.consequence: MODEL-SERVE-001-T10 Part A's finding inverts for these two tabs — PredictionLog stops being structurally empty for a scheduled-only model, so the 'no synchronous /predict traffic has been logged' copy those sections carry becomes wrong and must be revisited in the same pass. The two planes still must not be pooled into one feed: a window's predictions.parquet and a /predict row are different artifacts with different provenance, exactly as T10 item (6) states.

rejected.Shorten cadenceMinutes to a few minutes: Multiplies container spawns and backfill depth against a single concurrency slot, and MODEL-SERVE-006-T02 already had to fix live-window starvation on that slot once. Viable as a smaller separate change for a model that genuinely needs a scheduled record at finer granularity, not as the mechanism for a live chart.

openDecisions: RESOLVED 2026-09-17 by MODEL-SERVE-008-T01 READ 2 — KEPT IN PLACE RATHER THAN DELETED, because the reasoning is what guards the answer. IS THE TARGET EVER A CONTINUOUS TAG RATHER THAN A .lab MEASUREMENT? Schema-wise YES, realized NO. ModelTrainingRun.targetY carries TI202.PV on two runs, so the column genuinely has no .lab constraint and FeaturePreset.targetY's schema comment overstates the case — but BOTH those runs FAILED on "Run targets 'TI202.PV' but feature_spec.json says 'S204FBP.lab'.", no ModelVersion has ever been produced from a continuous target, and the guard that refused them already exists. CONSEQUENCE: the actual side is sparse by physics for every model that exists today (read 3: median lab inter-arrival 24h), T05's continuous-target branch is a GUARD to preserve rather than a per-model join fork to build, and the day a continuous target does get realized the discriminator belongs on the row at join time — the way MODEL-SERVE-005-T03 stores targetColumn rather than re-deriving it. ORIGINAL TEXT: FeaturePreset.targetY's own schema comment says 'The lab measurement this preset predicts. Always a `.lab` tag', and a real run's feature_spec.json records target_y = S204FBP.lab — but the serving path resolves the target through ModelVersion -> sourceRun -> ModelTrainingRun.targetY, which is a plain column with no .lab constraint on it.

WHAT REPLACES 'REAL-TIME RESIDUAL'? A residual needs an actual, so the honest options are: (i) leave the Residual chart exactly as sparse as it is and say why, on the chart; (ii) add a SEPARATE chart of the predicted series against the model's own recorded error band (from the version's holdout or test RMSE), which is a prediction-uncertainty view and must not be labelled a residual; (iii) plot residuals against the model's OWN test-split predictions as a static reference beside the live series, which answers 'how wrong is this model usually' rather than 'how wrong is it now'. RECOMMENDATION ON RECORD, NOT ADOPTED: (i) plus (ii) as a clearly-titled third chart. Collapsing a predicted-uncertainty band into the residual chart is the one-name-two-metrics defect MODEL-SERVE-001-T16 refused when it declined to put PSI in the z-score's table.

WHAT DRIVES /predict ON A CADENCE, AND WHO OWNS THE ROW FLOOR? A live series needs something calling /predict as feature tags arrive. Three shapes: a new short-interval poller in the backend that materializes a narrow window and posts it (reuses materialize_window, inherits the SQL TIMESTAMP-binding limit); a push from whatever already writes the historian, which does not exist here; or apps/serving pulling its own inputs, which would give the credential-free serving process a connector and reverse MODEL-SERVE-002's own deliberate design (its requirements.txt has no psycopg/minio/boto3/prisma, confirmed live). Also decide the minimum-rows question for this path: minRows is per-SCHEDULE (MODEL-SERVE-001-T14) and a /predict call has no schedule, so the floor that protects a window from scoring on 5 rows has no equivalent here.

DOES A DENSE PREDICTED SERIES CHANGE WHAT THE DRIFT THRESHOLDS MEAN? warnSd/criticalSd/driftThresholdPct are per-schedule (MODEL-SERVE-001-T21's thresholdsFromSchedule) and were chosen against hourly windows. The same z threshold evaluated every minute fires far more often on the same process, and T13's own cost (c) already flags that 0.1/0.25 for PSI are credit-scoring conventions rather than measurements on this plant. Decide whether a dense signal needs its own thresholds or a consecutive-breach rule, and record the rejected alternative — do not let the evaluation cadence change the effective sensitivity by accident.

tasks.title: AUDIT FIRST: confirm the screen's blank is still cause (A), and establish whether the target is ever continuous
tasks.scope_note:
FIVE READS. The second one can remove half this feature's scope, and the first one can remove the reason for it.

(1) RE-RUN MODEL-SERVE-001-T18's OWN DIAGNOSIS ON THE CURRENT STATE. It enumerates seven causes of an identical blank chart and its resolution pass found cause (A) — nothing due yet — plus a latent defect where a FAILED PI fetch became a SUCCESSFUL empty join. Query InferenceWindowTruth and InferenceWindow for this model, check the clock against windowEnd + truthLagMinutes, and check failureReason. If the earliest window has since become eligible and STILL has no pair, this is no longer (A) and the fix may be a defect rather than a feature.

(2) IS ModelTrainingRun.targetY EVER A NON-.lab TAG? Read the column across every real run, not the preset schema's comment. openDecisions[0] turns on this. If every target is .lab, the actual side is sparse by physics and T05 is a labelling task. If some are continuous, that class needs its own join branch and T05 becomes a real build.

(3) MEASURE THE REAL LAB CADENCE FOR THIS MODEL'S OWN TARGET. MODEL-SERVE-005-T03's granularity note says most windows hold ZERO lab samples and some exactly one, which is why it stores sufficient statistics rather than per-window metrics. Get the actual inter-arrival distribution for S204FBP.lab (or whichever target this model uses) over a real month. That number is what the UI must state, and it is also the honest answer to 'why is this chart sparse'.

(4) CONFIRM WHICH PLANE EACH OF THE FOUR MONITORING SECTIONS READS TODAY. MODEL-SERVE-001-T10 Part A traced this once and found a MIX — two sections fed by InferenceWindowTruth (which a schedule does fill, once the lab reports) and two by PredictionLog (which it never does). Re-verify rather than inherit: T03's own client work landed after T10 was filed, and T10's result records that it shrank Part A by half on exactly that discovery.

(5) CHECK WHETHER PI IS REACHABLE AT ALL FROM WHERE THIS WILL RUN. MODEL-SERVE-001-V12 is still BLOCKED on nslookup scgc-piwebapi.scg.com returning NXDOMAIN, recorded twice, and MODEL-SERVE-001-T18's own live check found the host intermittently failing (a window materialized 18 real rows at 02:17 and failed at 03:17 against the same host). A dense cadence against an intermittently-unreachable host multiplies failures rather than data.

Write all five answers into this task's result. MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code, and this feature's own starting screenshot is a working screen.
tasks.result:
ALL FIVE READS ANSWERED, 2026-09-17, against the running stack (Postgres up, MinIO :9000, python :8000, serving :8100). THE HEADLINE: the premise HOLDS but its stated cause does not. The screen is no longer cause (A).

READ 1 — NOT (A), BUT HONEST. truthLagMinutes is 1440. The three InferenceWindowTruth rows cover windows ending 2026-09-14 08:00/09:00/10:00, eligible since 2026-09-15 08:00 — roughly 42 HOURS before this read — and they were joined (joinAttempts 1, lastJoinedAt 2026-09-17 01:35) returning truthRows 0, pairedRows 0, failureReason NULL. T18's own trigger says that is no longer (A). It is NOT the T18 latent defect either: ground_truth_service.py _fetch_truth_frame RAISES on a diagnosed fetch, so the sweeper writes the connector's verbatim text into failureReason; NULL therefore means both PI calls answered status ok and the lab genuinely reported nothing. The empty is truthful. What was WRONG was the copy — see finding B below.

READ 2 — openDecisions[0] RESOLVED. ModelTrainingRun.targetY across every real run: S204FBP.lab (391), S204IBP.lab (82), TI202.PV (2). A non-.lab target is schema-permitted, and the ledger's trace is confirmed exactly — ModelVersion has NO targetY column in the database, so serving resolves through sourceRunId -> ModelTrainingRun.targetY (schema.prisma's targetY near line 1405 belongs to the sweep-job model, not ModelVersion). BUT BOTH TI202.PV RUNS FAILED, with failureReason "Run targets 'TI202.PV' but feature_spec.json says 'S204FBP.lab'." No ModelVersion has ever been produced from a continuous target, and an existing guard already refuses the mismatch. RESOLUTION: the schema permits a continuous target, none has ever been realized, and the guard that blocks it already exists. T05's continuous-target half is therefore a GUARD to preserve, not a build — the smallest safe answer, and it keeps the correctness fork off a path no model travels.

READ 3 — THE LAB REPORTS ABOUT ONCE A DAY, AND THE GOLD ARTIFACT ITSELF CARRIES PI'S HELD VALUE. Read from the model's own GOLD parquet (datasets bucket, artifact 66173c35-d0e5-4e92-a66b-bbc7a90ed112) rather than PI, which answers 401 unauthenticated: 8350 rows on a 5-minute grid spanning 2026-01-25 08:05 to 2026-02-27 08:00. S204FBP.lab holds only 32 DISTINCT VALUES across those 8350 rows — median inter-arrival between value changes EXACTLY 24h, p95 24h, max 4d03h, with 26 of 31 gaps in the 24-48h bin. Zero nulls and status Good on all 8350 rows, which is the held-value signature itself: the training table's target column is PI's last value carried forward, so 391 runs trained against a held target. Contrast TI202.PV in the same artifact: 8042 value changes of 8350 rows, genuinely continuous. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS FEATURE: at a 24h measurement rate against a 60-minute cadence, at best ONE window in 24 can ever hold a pair, and truthLagMinutes (1440) is the same size as the inter-arrival itself. This is the number T04's coverage strip must state.

THAT MEASUREMENT SETS THE CADENCE FLOOR AND SETTLES THE STORAGE QUESTION TOGETHER. Driving faster than the SLOWEST tag refreshes (~9 min) re-scores inputs that have not changed and manufactures precision the historian does not have, so the default cadence is 10 MINUTES and anything lower is a deliberate override. At 10 minutes one model writes ~144 PredictionLog rows and ~144 serving-logs/ objects per day, not the ~1,440 a one-minute cadence implied — which is why SERVING_LOG_SAMPLE_RATE 1.0 is affordable here. tasks.scope_note:
BLOCKED ON openDecisions[3].

The machinery exists and must be reused, not rebuilt: poolFeatureStats + computeDrift (lib/prediction-drift.ts) are pure and plane-agnostic, and MODEL-SERVE-001-T17's whole point was that only the QUERY feeding them differs by plane — it extracted resolveBaseline/resolvePsiReference into lib/artifact-baseline.ts precisely so a second plane reads the identical sidecar the identical way. PredictionLog.featureStats is already the right shape ({n, sum, sumsq, min, max}) and poolFeatureStats already combines many requests exactly.

UNKNOWN NEVER FOLDS INTO NORMAL, AND ONE UNKNOWN COLUMN NEVER MASKS ANOTHER'S CRITICAL. Both rules are already pinned by tests in prediction-drift.spec.ts; a new call site is a new place to break them.

PSI STAYS ON THE ROLLING WINDOW BASIS AND DOES NOT BECOME DENSE. Its floor is bin_count x 20 and its edges are frozen at GOLD-write time — at 10 bins a 5-minute contribution is 5 rows against a 200-sample floor, so a dense PSI figure would be INSUFFICIENT_DATA for a long warm-up and then an average over a window whose cadence differs from the z-score's. MODEL-SERVE-001-T16 already refused to put two metrics with different cadences in one table for this exact reason; the same refusal applies to computing them on the same trigger.

RECORD THE BASELINE DILUTION RATHER THAN INHERITING IT SILENTLY. MODEL-SERVE-001-T13 measured it: column_stats.json is computed over the WHOLE committed artifact, not the train split, so the z-score reference is systematically wider than the learned distribution and the signal under-flags — always in that direction. A denser signal does not fix that and should not be described as more sensitive than it is.
tasks.result:
openDecisions[3] ANSWERED (user, 2026-09-17): a CONSECUTIVE-BREACH RULE. The existing per-schedule warnSd/criticalSd keep their meaning; what changes is how much evidence a STATE CHANGE needs. REJECTED and recorded in the code itself, not only here: separate dense thresholds (two numbers per schedule that can silently disagree about one process) and reusing the thresholds unchanged (simplest, and precisely the accidental sensitivity change openDecisions[3] existed to prevent — the same numbers evaluated every 10 minutes instead of hourly fire about six times as often on an unchanged process).

SHIPPED: `applyConsecutiveBreachRule` in lib/prediction-drift.ts — a PURE function over DriftBucket[], so it is testable without a database, a plane or an HTTP hop. It consumes `computeDrift`'s existing output rather than re-deriving anything: T03's own instruction was that the machinery is reused and only the QUERY feeding it differs by plane, which is why MODEL-SERVE-001-T17 extracted resolveBaseline/resolvePsiReference in the first place. Nothing in computeDrift, poolFeatureStats or artifact-baseline.ts was modified.

IT REUSES THIS MODULE'S OWN SEVERITY SCALE AND REDUCE CONVENTION (UNKNOWN 0 < OK 1 < WARN 2 < CRITICAL 3, seeded at UNKNOWN). The first draft introduced a second scale and the module refused to compile with a duplicate `SEVERITY` — which was the right failure: a second severity order is a second thing to disagree with computeDrift about what 'worse' means.

THE RULES IT HOLDS, EACH WITH ITS OWN TEST (10 new cases; prediction-drift.spec.ts went 15 -> 25, whole backend lib + inference-window + prediction-log suites 345 passing):
  - A single breach does NOT change state when the rule asks for three; the run must reach the required length, and the report names WHEN it began (`since`).
  - A clean bucket BREAKS the run, so an intermittent spike never accumulates into an alert.
  - A CRITICAL is not promoted on the back of preceding WARNs (conservative direction), while a WARN preceded by CRITICALs IS a sustained WARN.
  - UNKNOWN NEVER FOLDS INTO OK and an UNKNOWN bucket BREAKS a run rather than counting as a breach — a missing or degenerate baseline is the absence of a verdict, never evidence of health. One UNKNOWN column still cannot mask another column's CRITICAL.
  - No buckets at all reports UNKNOWN, never OK, which would claim health from nothing.
  - The acted-on status can be OK while `instantStatus` is CRITICAL — the breach stays VISIBLE. Hiding it would make the panel read OK while z sits above the line, which is the confident-wrong-answer this ledger keeps refusing. `consecutive`, `instantStatus`, `since` and `consecutiveRequired` are all on the response so a reader never has to guess which threshold produced the status.

PSI WAS NOT TOUCHED, AS INSTRUCTED: it keeps its rolling-window basis and its bin_count x 20 floor. Computing it on the dense trigger would put two metrics with different cadences in one table, which MODEL-SERVE-001-T16 already refused.

WHAT IS NOT DONE — THE WIRING, AND IT IS BLOCKED ON A REAL DISPATCH QUESTION. The rule is not yet called by any endpoint. `getDriftService` SHORT-CIRCUITS to the window plane whenever an InferenceSchedule row exists (MODEL-SERVE-001-T17 chose dispatch on ROW PRESENCE deliberately, and its own tests assert PredictionLog is never touched when a schedule exists). Model 3991c43f now has BOTH a schedule and a live driver, so its dense rows are currently invisible to the drift panel. Choosing a dispatch for that case is exactly the question MODEL-SERVE-008-T06 already carries — 'confirm which plane the drift panel should read for that case and state it, or the panel silently answers a different question than its caption claims' — so the wiring belongs with T06's decision and is NOT taken here. Also still unmeasured: the BASELINE DILUTION MODEL-SERVE-001-T13 recorded (column_stats.json is computed over the WHOLE committed artifact, not the train split, so the z-score reference is systematically wider and the signal under-flags). The consecutive rule does not fix that and must not be described as more sensitive than it is.

=== WIRED AND LIVE-VERIFIED, 2026-09-17. T03 COMPLETE. ===

THE READOUT IS ITS OWN ROUTE: GET /authorized/model/:modelId/live-drift -> getLiveDriftService. `/drift` is UNCHANGED and keeps MODEL-SERVE-001-T17's dispatch on schedule row presence, per T06's decision — so the existing panel still answers exactly the question its caption claims, and the dense signal never silently replaces it. Two cadences must not share one table (MODEL-SERVE-001-T16), so they do not share one route either.

BUCKETING IS THE PART ONLY THE SERVICE COULD GET WRONG, and it is what makes the rule meaningful: rows are grouped into one bucket per THIS MODEL'S OWN livePredictCadenceMinutes, so 'consecutive bucket' means one scoring interval rather than an arbitrary server-side number. Pooling the whole range into a single computeDrift — which is what /drift does — answers 'was the average of this range drifted' and hides a breach that began twenty minutes ago inside hours of healthy traffic.

THE BASELINE IS THE SAME SIDECAR THE WINDOW PLANE READS, through the same resolveColumnBaseline over the production version's own goldObjectKey — T17 extracted it so a second plane reads it the identical way and the two signals cannot disagree about what 'training distribution' means. The T13 DILUTION IS INHERITED AND SAID SO IN THE CODE: column_stats.json spans the whole committed artifact rather than the train split, so the reference is systematically wider and this signal UNDER-flags. A denser cadence does not fix that.

A THIRD PLANE LABEL, `predict-live`, not a reuse of `predict`: these are the SAME ROWS as /drift's predict plane but evaluated on a different cadence under a different rule, and a caller that cannot tell them apart will eventually render one as the other. `consecutiveRequired`, `bucketMinutes` and `livePredictEnabled` all ride on the basis so a reader never guesses which rule produced the status, and can tell 'no breach' from 'the driver is off and this readout describes nothing'.

TESTS SPLIT BY WHO OWNS THE RISK: the RULE is exhaustively covered in lib/prediction-drift.spec.ts (10 cases, every UNKNOWN path); the SERVICE tests (8 new, spec 9 -> 17) own bucketing, dispatch and labelling — four rows ten minutes apart are four buckets not one pool; rows inside one cadence pool into one bucket; the route NEVER dispatches to the window plane even with a schedule present; the plane label is neither `predict` nor `window`; an empty range reports UNKNOWN rather than OK; no PRODUCTION version 404s; and a model with no schedule row falls back to a 10-minute bucket. 353 passing across lib + prediction-log + inference-window; backend tsc at its pre-existing baseline of 6.

tasks.title: Actual vs Predict: dense predicted line, sparse actual points, and a coverage strip that explains the difference
tasks.scope_note:

The predicted line is its OWN series over PredictionLog; the actual points stay the joined-pairs series over InferenceWindowTruth. Two series, two provenances, one chart — never one series with holes in it.

THE COVERAGE STRIP IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART, NOT THE LINE. With a dense predicted series and sparse actuals, a reader counting the actual points will conclude the model ran that few times. State both counts and both rates: predictions in range, lab samples in range, and the measured inter-arrival from T01 read 3. This is the same discipline MODEL-SERVE-005-T03 applied when it published the WORST window's missingPct rather than a mean, on the stated ground that 'a mean hides the one window whose sensor stopped'.

KEEP THE VERSION GROUPING. T03 groups metrics by version and returns null at the top level when a range mixes versions, because two versions can resolve different targets through their own source runs and one pooled RMSE over them is a number about nothing. A dense series crosses a promote more often, so this matters more here, not less. MODEL-SERVE-006-T07's read side — marking where the version changed on the series — is still open and is what stops a promote reading as a process shift.

EVERY BRANCH KEEPS ITS OWN SENTENCE. EmptyTruth already discriminates five causes and MODEL-SERVE-001-T11 added a sixth (N windows SKIPPED). Adding a dense predicted series adds a seventh state — predictions present, no actual yet — which is precisely the screenshot's current state and must not collapse into 'no data'. One flat sentence across the tab is the defect, not the absence.

THE COVERAGE-STRIP HALF IS DONE AND LIVE-VERIFIED. THE DENSE PREDICTED LINE IS NOT, AND STAYS BLOCKED ON T02 (which is blocked on openDecisions[2]) — this task is IN PROGRESS, not completed.

WHAT SHIPPED. The strip was reporting only `pairedRows` and `truthRows`, so on this model it read '0 paired / 0 lab samples' over a range in which the model had actually scored 68 predictions across 11 windows. The strip therefore states the rate it can prove (this model's own cadence) and says the lab reports on its own schedule, rather than asserting a number it has not read. EvalPoint WAS NOT RELAXED, AND THE TYPE SYSTEM NOW ENFORCES THAT RATHER THAN A COMMENT. A dense predicted point has no lab counterpart, so it CANNOT be a MonitoringRow — `actual` and `residual` are non-optional there for MODEL-SERVE-005's recorded reason (the SD-band and residual math structurally require ground truth, and satisfying the shape without it means fabricating an actual). tasks.title: FIXED: a window past its truth lag is a state, not a wait — stop naming a deadline that has already passed
tasks.scope_note:
FOUND BY T01 READ 1, FIXED IN THE SAME PASS BECAUSE IT IS THE SCREEN THIS FEATURE EXISTS TO CORRECT. getTruthService built `stillAwaiting` as every SUCCEEDED window with no truth row OR a truth row with n = 0 and no failureReason — which is exactly the shape a window that joined HONESTLY and found nothing keeps forever. So such a window never left 'awaiting', and `earliestEligibleAt` (correctly min(windowEnd) + lag) named a time in the PAST: live, three windows 42h past a 24h lag rendered 'the earliest scored window becomes eligible at Sep 15, 08:00' indefinitely. The reader was told to wait for a check that had already happened.

THE FIX SPLITS THE TWO STATES RATHER THAN ADDING A SENTENCE. `pendingLag` is the windows whose deadline is still ahead of the clock and is the ONLY input to `earliestEligibleAt`, so that field can no longer carry a passed time. `coverage.windowsLapsedTruth` counts the rest — a SUBSET of windowsAwaitingTruth, never a second count of the same windows, and disjoint in meaning from windowsFailed because the sweeper DID reach the source here. EmptyTruth gains a branch checked BEFORE the truth-lag branch, and the coverage strip splits its 'awaiting lab results' chip so a permanent state stops being displayed as a pending one.

THIS IS THE SEVENTH EMPTY STATE V05 ASKS FOR, ARRIVING FROM THE TRUTH SIDE RATHER THAN THE PREDICTION SIDE. V05's own case — predictions present, no actual yet — still needs the dense series and stays open. Copy is neutral, not a status colour: per read 3 the lab reports about once a day against an hourly schedule, so most windows END here and this is the measurement rate, not a fault (DESIGN_SYSTEM section 5 reserves red/amber for deployment status).

FILES: apps/backend/src/api/v1/inference-window/authorized/inference-window.authorized.service.ts (getTruthService), apps/client/services/inference-window.ts (LiveErrorCoverage), apps/client/app/(default)/models/[id]/components/monitoring/model-monitoring-tab.tsx (EmptyTruth + coverage strip).

What is left, and why none of it is bookkeeping:
