Needs a range containing a genuine gap between lab samples, asserting zero pairs for the gap and a pair for an interval with a real event. A fixture whose every interval has a measurement cannot tell the event-presence probe from no probe, and the wrong answer is a confident R2 rather than an error.
V02 — the dense series MATCHES THE MODEL, not merely that points appear. Take a row from the model's own test split through the dense path and assert the logged prediction matches to numerical tolerance. MODEL-SERVE-002-V01 got max diff 2.66e-15 over 1000 real rows; a synthetic-input test proving a float came back is not the claim. The live run proved a REAL prediction (0.6598) was produced and logged, never that it is the RIGHT one.
V03 — PARTIAL. The round-trip half passed live (a logged row reached the backend and its parquet landed in MinIO). The fault-injection half did not run: no real transport failure was injected into the ingest call under the dense cadence.
V04 — the drift signal still DISCRIMINATES at the new cadence, both directions: in-distribution rows assert OK, then two named columns shifted by a known multiple of the training SD assert CRITICAL on exactly those columns with every other column still OK. The consecutive-breach rule is unit-proven in both directions, but the END-TO-END discrimination at the dense cadence against real data is not.
V05 — the seventh empty state as THIS feature framed it (predictions present, no actual yet) rendered and asserted distinct from all six EmptyTruth branches. T07 closed the truth-side seventh state (lag lapsed, no report) with tests, and T06 added the driver-on empty copy with tests — but the specific dense-line-with-no-actual render is not asserted.
V07 — measure the storage the dense path writes over a REAL DAY. One object was measured at 14,463 bytes and the rate was DERIVED (~144/day/model at a 10-minute cadence); the day-long measurement that would confirm the derivation has not been taken. This is what the retention decision rests on, so it is worth taking.

ALSO OUTSTANDING, NOT A VERIFICATION: a client panel for the live-drift readout (route and contract exist and are live-verified) and an enable/cadence UI for the driver (today livePredictEnabled is set in the database).

features.title: Per-tag last value and last seen, kept across fetches — the evidence Sensor Frozen reads, and the state that makes a held .lab value legible
features.description: Keep a per-tag last value, its status, and when it last CHANGED, updated on every scheduled fetch rather than recomputed from scratch. Three things fall out of one row: Sensor Frozen gets first-class evidence instead of a three-window inference, the Input Data tab stops depending on synchronous /predict traffic a scheduled model never produces, and a .lab target held flat by PI becomes visibly held rather than silently paired.
features.placement_note: FILED AS ITS OWN FEATURE. The subject spans MODEL-SERVE-006 (the scheduler and InferenceWindow), MODEL-SERVE-005-T03 (the truth join and its Count probe), and MODEL-SERVE-001-T15/T29 (per-tag PI status, and Sensor Frozen). Same reasoning as MODEL-SERVE-008: every task under MODEL-SERVE-001 from T09 onward carries a placement pointer apologising for sitting in a feature titled 'Model Version Registry', and this is larger than any of them.
features.dependency_note: CORRECTED 2026-09-17 BY MODEL-SERVE-009-T01 READ 4. THE ORIGINAL TEXT WAS WRONG AND IS KEPT BELOW SO THE CORRECTION IS AUDITABLE. MODEL-SERVE-001-T27, T29 AND T30 ARE ALL COMPLETED AND SHIPPED: sensor-frozen.ts's `detectFrozenColumns` (five guards, 302-line spec), model-health.ts's FROZEN status / SENSOR_FROZEN reason / frozenColumns field / five-state precedence, and InferenceSchedule.frozenWindows + .frozenTolerancePct as live columns. Sensor Frozen is not merely built but ACTIVE — it badges four genuinely-pinned tags on model 3991c43f today. THEREFORE T03 IS A REPLACEMENT OF EXISTING EVIDENCE, NOT A BUILD, and must be justified as one: what a lastChangedAt timestamp adds over the shipped three-window pooled range is HOW LONG a tag has been flat and cadence-independence, not detection that does not exist yet. ORIGINAL TEXT: 'MODEL-SERVE-001-T29 (Sensor Frozen) IS PENDING, NOT BUILT. classifyModelHealth (lib/model-health.ts, MODEL-SERVE-001-T21) today returns OFF / UNKNOWN / OK / WARN / CRITICAL and has no frozen value; T27's five-state monitoring enum and T29's detection recipe are both drafted and unstarted. So T03 below either lands T29's own work or lands after it — decide the order, do not assume the value exists. This feature's contribution is the EVIDENCE and the per-tag badge, not the classifier.'
findings: THE .lab FETCH ALREADY RUNS ON THE SCHEDULE'S OWN TERMS, AND SHORTENING ITS LAG DOES NOT PRODUCE MORE MEASUREMENTS. decisions.ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_target_tag: truth arrives by RE-FETCHING THE TARGET TAG from the window's own source (InferenceSchedule.sourceId + fetchConfig) on a second, much longer lag (truthLagMinutes, default 1440), driven by InferenceTruthSweeperService's own setInterval at 900000ms. The screenshot's 'earliest scored window becomes eligible at Sep 18, 08:00' is that lag, working. What the lag does NOT control is how often the lab measures: PI holds a sparse .lab tag's last value between samples, so an hourly fetch returns an hourly VALUE and roughly a daily MEASUREMENT. Lowering truthLagMinutes to 60 would produce about 23 pairs a day against a held value and one against a real one, indistinguishable in the metric.

THE COUNT PROBE IS WHAT SEPARATES THE TWO, AND IT IS THE THING THAT MUST NOT BE WEAKENED HERE. ground_truth_service.py overrides cal_basis to EventWeighted and runs a Count PROBE FIRST, keeping only intervals an event actually occurred in — two sequential calls, not one, because from_pi_response builds one value per (tag, timestamp) and a single call asking for both Count and Average would collide two summaries into one column. That is the mechanism this feature builds ON, by recording what the probe finds rather than discarding it.

A HELD VALUE IS EVIDENCE, NOT NOISE — WHICH IS WHY THE USER'S THIRD ASK ANSWERS THEIR SECOND. Today the Count probe's zero-event verdict is used and thrown away: the interval is skipped and nothing records that the tag was asked about and found unchanged. Keep it, and 'last changed at' is a direct measurement of how long a tag has been flat — which is exactly what MODEL-SERVE-001-T29's Sensor Frozen currently has to INFER from three windows of pooled min/max. One row replaces an inference.

T29's OWN RECIPE IS A THREE-WINDOW INFERENCE OVER AGGREGATES, AND IT CANNOT SEE A FLAT RUN SHORTER OR LONGER THAN THREE WINDOWS. Its definition is pooled range = max(max) - min(min) across the last three windows carrying featureStats, taken from the take-3 sample deriveDeployStatuses already reads. That is a good cheap fit and it quantises hard: a tag flat for 2h50m reads as moving, a tag flat for six days reads the same as one flat for three hours. A last-changed timestamp answers both, and answers 'for how long' — which is the question an operator actually asks about a stuck instrument.

T29's FOUR GUARDS STILL APPLY AND ONE OF THEM GETS CHEAPER. (1) A tag flat in TRAINING (a setpoint, a valve held closed) must be skipped via column_stats.std near zero — unchanged, still needed. (2) Define it in windows not rows, per MODEL-SERVE-001-T14's measured lesson that a global row count is the wrong axis — a last-changed TIMESTAMP is cadence-independent by construction, so this guard dissolves rather than needing care. (3) eps as a fraction of the training range because featureStats are in SCALED units and T17 measured a real scaled value at -1.17, so [0,1] cannot be assumed — still applies, and applies to the raw comparison too. (4) A minimum n per window so a one-row window does not read flat — still needed.

THE INPUT DATA TAB'S PER-TAG STATUS IS A LIVE PI SNAPSHOT TAKEN ON DEMAND, WITH NO HISTORY AT ALL. MODEL-SERVE-001-T15 built GET .../input-status against tag_service.current_values (selecting items.value.good/questionable/substituted — the ONE path in this system carrying PI's own quality flag) and returns unavailableReason with a 200 rather than throwing. It answers 'is this tag healthy right now', asked at page load. It cannot answer 'when did this tag last move' or 'what was it an hour ago', and it goes blank whenever PI is unreachable — which T15's own result records as unverified for exactly that reason (nslookup NXDOMAIN, the same blocker as V12).

AND THAT SNAPSHOT IS NOT THE SAME QUALITY FLAG THE PIPELINE USES. MODEL-SERVE-001-T15's own headline finding: `{tag}__status` is NOT PI's quality flag. convertAverageDicttoDataFrame builds rows from .value.timestamp and .value.value only, so good/questionable/substituted are never selected on the historical path; frame_service.from_pi_response then derives __status from _coerce_value (is this a parseable finite number) plus a per-tag status == 'failed' check. That is PARSE/ARRIVAL health. So a stored last-status must state WHICH flag it is — the snapshot's PI quality, or the fetch path's arrival health — because the two answer different questions and STATUS_QUESTIONABLE is defined but produced by no live path.

THE FETCH THAT WOULD FEED THIS ALREADY DROPS BAD ROWS BEFORE ANYTHING IS STORED. materialize_window's order is fetch -> apply_features -> trim -> select_columns -> missing_pct -> drop_bad_feature_rows -> put_frame, and drop_bad_feature_rows discards a row when ANY kept tag's status is not Good. MODEL-SERVE-001-T15 measured the consequence when it evaluated input.parquet as a per-tag-status surface: that object has ZERO Bad cells surviving by construction. So a last-status must be captured BEFORE that drop, from the fetch's own per-tag result, or it will always read Good.

THE FIRST HOUR AFTER ENABLING IS A REAL STATE AND MUST NOT READ AS FROZEN. A last-changed timestamp starts at the first fetch, so every tag has 'changed 0 minutes ago' and then nothing to compare against until a second fetch lands an hour later. MODEL-SERVE-006-T12's warmup_2026_09_14 amendment records the mirror-image mistake on the deploy axis — a broken schedule looked like a healthy warm-up because the escape required three failures — and fixed it by making the warm-up state require positive evidence rather than absence. Same discipline: unknown-yet is its own state, never Frozen and never OK.

PI IS INTERMITTENTLY UNREACHABLE FROM THIS ENVIRONMENT, AND AN ABSENT FETCH IS NOT A FLAT TAG. Recorded repeatedly: nslookup scgc-piwebapi.scg.com returns NXDOMAIN (V12 blocked on it, twice), and MODEL-SERVE-001-T18's own live check found the same host succeeding at 02:17 and failing at 03:17. If last-seen is not updated when a fetch FAILS, a multi-hour outage looks identical to a multi-hour freeze — a source fault reported as an instrument fault, which sends an operator to the wrong place. MODEL-SERVE-006-T04's diagnose_empty_pi_fetch exists to tell those two apart and must be the discriminator here too.

STORING ONE ROW PER TAG PER FETCH IS A TIME SERIES IN POSTGRES, AND THIS PROJECT HAS A STANDING RULE AGAINST THAT. feature_list.preprocessing's architecture.storage_authority is explicit: MinIO is the single source of truth for rows, Postgres holds metadata and pointers only, and 'not one of the 18 Prisma models stores timeseries rows'. At 21 tags x 24 fetches x 365 days that is ~184,000 rows per model per year. The shape that respects the rule is ONE CURRENT row per (model, tag), updated in place, with the history already living in the window objects — see decisions.one_row_per_tag_updated_in_place.

AN UPDATE-IN-PLACE ROW CANNOT BE BACKFILLED AND WILL READ 'UNKNOWN' FOR EVERY EXISTING MODEL UNTIL ITS NEXT FETCH. Same shape as MODEL-SERVE-001-T17's PSI note — psiRefEdges are written at GOLD-write time only, so PSI reads UNKNOWN on every existing model until the artifact is rebuilt, and T27's rule is that UNKNOWN must never fold into Normal. State the same rule here: a model with no per-tag row yet is unknown, not healthy.

one_row_per_tag_updated_in_place.chosen: One TagObservation row per (modelId, tag), updated on every fetch. It carries lastValue, lastStatus, lastSeenAt (the most recent fetch that returned this tag at all), lastChangedAt (the most recent fetch whose value differed from the one before it), and lastFetchOutcome. No per-fetch history row.
one_row_per_tag_updated_in_place.rationale: architecture.storage_authority forbids timeseries rows in Postgres, and the history already exists — each window's own input.parquet holds the frame, and featureStats holds its aggregates. What is missing is the CURRENT state, which is exactly one row per tag. It also makes the read free for the surfaces that need it: MODEL-SERVE-001-T30's binding constraint is that buildAlerts is a pure function over the models list, so a signal must ride the batched read or one page becomes N requests, and a bounded per-model row set does.
one_row_per_tag_updated_in_place.consequence: lastChangedAt requires comparing against the previous value, so the update is read-then-write rather than a blind upsert — and the previous value is the row's own lastValue, so no extra query. Nothing is backfillable: every existing model reads unknown until its next fetch.

rejected.A row per tag per fetch: A timeseries table in Postgres, against this project's own stated storage authority, to answer a question one current row answers.
rejected.Derive last-changed from the window obje: Reconstructs a timestamp from pooled min/max across N objects, which is T29's three-window inference with more I/O. The whole point of storing it is that a timestamp is exact where an aggregate range is quantised.

held_is_recorded_not_paired.chosen: The Count probe's zero-event verdict is RECORDED against the target tag (its own lastSeenAt advances, lastChangedAt does not) and still produces no pair. The join's behaviour is unchanged.
held_is_recorded_not_paired.rationale: decisions.ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_target_tag's rule stands: a truth value must be EVIDENCED BY AN ACTUAL LAB EVENT in the interval, never by a held or interpolated summary. But throwing away the verdict is what makes today's screen unable to distinguish 'the lab has not reported' from 'the lab reported the same number again' — the first is waiting, the second is worth investigating. Recording it changes what the UI can say without changing what the metric counts.
held_is_recorded_not_paired.consequence: A .lab target can now itself be flagged frozen, which is a genuinely useful signal (a stuck lab instrument or a stalled LIMS feed) and is NOT the same as a frozen feature tag: it does not corrupt a prediction, it starves the evaluation. Keep the two distinguishable in the UI.

rejected.Lower truthLagMinutes toward the cadence: Produces about 23 held-value pairs a day against one real one, and publishes an R2 computed mostly against a value nobody measured — the exact defect the Count probe exists to prevent.

arrival_health_and_pi_quality_are_two_fi.chosen: lastStatus records the FETCH PATH's arrival health (the __status the pipeline actually uses). PI's own good/questionable/substituted flag, available only on the snapshot path, stays where MODEL-SERVE-001-T15 put it and is not merged into this row.
arrival_health_and_pi_quality_are_two_fi.rationale: T15's own finding is that these are different flags answering different questions, that STATUS_QUESTIONABLE is defined but produced by no live path, and that the historical fetch never selects PI's quality at all. One column holding whichever flag happened to be available would be a field whose meaning depends on which code path last wrote it — the pipelineVersion-with-a-default defect DS-LAKE-022's own findings record, in a new place.
arrival_health_and_pi_quality_are_two_fi.consequence: The Input Data tab shows both: PI quality now (when reachable, from T15's existing snapshot) and arrival health as of the last fetch (always, from this row). Two columns, each labelled with which it is.

openDecisions: WHAT COUNTS AS 'CHANGED' FOR A FLOATING-POINT READING? Exact inequality makes a tag with dither in its last significant digit never frozen, which is the common real case and would make the whole signal useless on a live instrument. A tolerance needs a basis: T29 already chose a fraction of the TRAINING range for its own eps because featureStats are scaled, and the same basis works here for a raw value via column_stats min/max. RECOMMENDATION ON RECORD, NOT ADOPTED: a fraction of the training range, per tag, with the fraction stated on screen — and the same near-constant-in-training guard T29 needs, so a setpoint does not read frozen forever. Note the interaction with precision: _round_to(x, 3) is applied at scaling time (DS-LAKE-025-T06 measured the consequence as +/-0.001*span), so a tolerance below that is meaningless for any value read post-scale.

HOW LONG FLAT IS FROZEN, AND IS IT ONE NUMBER OR PER TAG? T29's own recipe is three windows, which at a 60-minute cadence is three hours and is cadence-relative by accident rather than by design. A duration is the honest unit for a timestamp-based signal, but different tags legitimately move at different rates — a lab target holding for 20 hours is normal, a flow reading holding for 20 minutes is not. MODEL-SERVE-001-T14's measured lesson is that one global constant derived from an assumed interval is the wrong axis, and MODEL-SERVE-001-T28 is where per-schedule thresholds get a home. Decide whether frozenAfterMinutes is one per schedule or one per tag, and record the rejected alternative.

DOES A FROZEN TAG CHANGE THE MONITORING STATUS, GATE ANYTHING, OR BOTH? The user asks for the status to become Frozen, which MODEL-SERVE-001-T27's proposed precedence puts at Offline > Alert > Sensor Frozen > Warning > Normal. But MODEL-SERVE-001-T21's own user decision was that the health axis is PURELY INFORMATIONAL — it does not block a promote, does not pause a schedule, does not trigger autoRetrain — with the rejected alternatives recorded. A frozen FEATURE tag arguably should gate something, since a prediction computed from a stuck input is a confident wrong answer, which is a different case from a drift warning. Do not let it become a gate by accident: decide, and record the rejected alternative as T21 did.

RESOLVED 2026-09-17, AND NARROWER THAN THE QUESTION ASSUMED. The question was whether a frozen .lab TARGET should read as the same status as a frozen FEATURE tag. It does not arise as a status question at all, because MODEL-SERVE-009-T03's decision left detection entirely with MODEL-SERVE-001-T29, which classifies FEATURE columns only — the target is not a feature and never enters that set. So no status collapse is possible and none was introduced. What the target gets instead is its own surface: `targetHeld` on the truth read, carrying the last reported value, when it was actually measured, and how long it has read the same. That honours the distinction the question was protecting — a stuck FEATURE corrupts predictions, a stuck TARGET starves evaluation and leaves predictions perfectly valid — by giving them different fields rather than one status with two meanings, which is the shape MODEL-SERVE-001-T21 refused when it kept health off classifyDeployStatus's enum. REVISIT if the target is ever admitted to detectFrozenColumns' input, which would put both back on one enum.

tasks.title: AUDIT FIRST: where per-tag status is captured before the Bad-row drop, and what the Count probe already knows
tasks.scope_note:
FIVE READS. The first two decide where the write goes; the third can shrink this feature.

(1) WHAT DOES DataService.fetch RETURN PER TAG, BEFORE drop_bad_feature_rows? MODEL-SERVE-006-T04's diagnose_empty_pi_fetch reads a per-tag status of ok/partial/failed and keeps the first error string for every failed tag — that is the arrival-health signal decisions.arrival_health_and_pi_quality_are_two_fields wants, and it already exists. Establish exactly where in materialize_window it is still available and whether it survives to the response, or is discarded like the diagnosis was before T04 promoted it.

(2) DOES THE COUNT PROBE'S PER-INTERVAL VERDICT REACH THE CALLER? ground_truth_service.py runs the probe then filters. Read whether the zero-event intervals are enumerable after the filter or thrown away inside it — decisions.held_is_recorded_not_paired needs them, and if the probe result is already returned this task is smaller than it looks.

(3) IS THERE ALREADY A PER-TAG CURRENT-STATE ROW ANYWHERE? MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code. Grep for any existing tag-level table or any place lastValue/lastSeen is persisted, including in Model.data's untyped Json blob — MODEL-SERVE-000-T02 found deployStatus living there with no column behind it, so an untyped blob is a real place for a field to already exist.

(4) CONFIRM MODEL-SERVE-001-T29's STATUS BEFORE BUILDING AGAINST IT. It is pending as of this filing, and lib/model-health.ts has no frozen value. If T29 has since landed, this feature supplies its evidence and T03 is a swap; if not, T03 lands both and the ordering matters. Check T27 too — the five-state monitoring enum is where 'Sensor Frozen' as a VALUE comes from.

(5) MEASURE THE REAL FLAT-RUN DISTRIBUTION FOR THIS MODEL'S OWN TAGS. Read the last month of window objects and compute, per tag, how long it actually goes without changing. That number answers openDecisions[1] with a measurement instead of a guess, and it is the same discipline MODEL-SERVE-001-T11 applied when it read 24 real InferenceWindow rows rather than reasoning about the 20-of-60 shortfall. MODEL-SERVE-006-V08 has been pending for months precisely because nobody measured a comparable number.

Write all five answers into this task's result.
tasks.result:
ALL FIVE READS ANSWERED, 2026-09-17, against the running stack (backend/python/serving all responding; PI resolving to 10.43.38.60). THE HEADLINE: THIS FEATURE'S OWN dependency_note IS STALE AND ITS SCOPE SHRINKS.

READ 4 FIRST, BECAUSE IT RESHAPES EVERYTHING ELSE — MODEL-SERVE-001-T29 IS BUILT, NOT PENDING. This feature's dependency_note says 'T29 (Sensor Frozen) IS PENDING, NOT BUILT' and that sentence is now false: T27, T29 and T30 are all completed. apps/backend/src/lib/sensor-frozen.ts (156 lines) plus a 302-line co-located spec ship `detectFrozenColumns` with five guards; lib/model-health.ts already carries the 'FROZEN' status, the 'SENSOR_FROZEN' reason, a `frozenColumns` field and the precedence Offline > Alert > Frozen > Warning > Normal; InferenceSchedule.frozenWindows and .frozenTolerancePct are real columns live in the database. So T03 below is NOT a build — it is a proposal to REPLACE a shipped, tested signal's evidence, which is a different decision needing a different justification. `detectFrozenColumns` is column-level only and returns string[]: no timestamps, no last-changed. That is the genuine gap this feature could still fill.

AND IT IS FIRING RIGHT NOW, ON TRUE POSITIVES — A PLANNING CLAIM OF MINE, CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT. While planning I asserted from the schema that Sensor Frozen was 'effectively inert' because frozenTolerancePct is 0 and eps = frozenTolerancePct x (p99-p1) therefore reduces to exact float equality. THE LIVE READ DISPROVED THE CONCLUSION: GET /inference/status for model 3991c43f returns status FROZEN, reason SENSOR_FROZEN, frozenColumns [FIC107R.PV, FIC114A.PV, FIC114B.PV, FY107.CPV]. Checked against the windows' own featureStats, those four columns have max - min EXACTLY 0 in every recent window (scaled values -5.804, 0, 0, 0.647 held flat for hours), while TI202.PV and AI206.PV move by ~0.1 and are correctly NOT badged. The signal discriminates. What survives of the original concern is narrower and still true: eps = 0 catches only EXACTLY constant tags and would miss a stuck instrument whose last digit dithers, which is openDecisions[0]'s real subject. Filed separately as MODEL-SERVE-010-T04 rather than changed here.

READ 1 — PER-TAG STATUS EXISTS IN THE FRAME AND NOTHING PER-TAG SURVIVES TO THE CALLER. inference_window_service.py:204 materialize_window, order confirmed: fetch (:257) -> from_pi_response (:265) -> apply_features (:306) -> trim (:310) -> select_columns (:326) -> missing_pct (:329) -> drop_bad_feature_rows (:341) -> histograms/stats -> put_frame (:363). The {tag}__status columns exist from :265 through :341 and ARE written into the parquet, but the response dict (:365-373) returns only object_key, row_count, scored_rows, missing_pct, checksum, feature_histograms, feature_stats — NO per-tag field — and drop_bad_feature_rows' own `_dropped` count is discarded at :341. The file says so itself at :260-264: the per-tag status/error the PI payload carries is the only record of it, and building the frame discards it. CONSEQUENCE FOR T02: it cannot be done backend-side alone. Writing the row where decisions.one_row_per_tag_updated_in_place requires (before the Bad-row drop) needs python to RETURN a per-tag summary first — a real python change, not a Prisma migration plus a service.

READ 2 — THE COUNT PROBE'S VERDICT IS COMPUTED AND THROWN AWAY, exactly as decisions.held_is_recorded_not_paired assumed. ground_truth_service.py:215-222 computes `evidenced` (the intervals a lab event actually occurred in) and filters the values frame by it; join_window_truth's return (:358-372) carries no per-interval and no per-tag verdict. So the information T05 wants already exists at the point of use and is discarded one line later — recording it is a plumbing change, not a new measurement, and the join's behaviour need not change.

READ 3 — WHAT T29 ALREADY COVERS IN PRACTICE, measured rather than inferred: four of this model's 21 feature columns are badged frozen today at frozenTolerancePct 0 and frozenWindows 3, and they are genuinely pinned (range exactly 0 across every window in the take). A last-changed TIMESTAMP would say the same thing about the same four tags, with two differences that are the whole argument for this feature: it would say HOW LONG (findings[3]'s quantisation — a tag flat 2h50m currently reads as moving at a 60-minute cadence), and it would survive a cadence change without re-tuning frozenWindows. Neither difference is visible on this model today, because all four tags have been flat far longer than three windows.

READ 5 — THE INPUT DATA TAB DERIVES LAST VALUE AND LAST SEEN IN THE BROWSER, AND MODEL-SERVE-008 HAS ALREADY PARTLY CLOSED THE GAP THIS FEATURE CITES. apps/client/lib/model-input-features.ts:133-141 scans points[].features (from PredictionLog) to compute lastValueRaw/lastSeen; InputFeatureRow (:24) has NO lastChanged field at all. Per-tag PI status comes from a separate live snapshot (model-input-status.authorized.service.ts:43), a current-value read with no history. T04's stated motivation is that this tab is 'empty by construction' for a scheduled model — MEASURED TODAY, IT IS NOT: GET /predictions for model 3991c43f returns 2 points carrying all 21 features, written by MODEL-SERVE-008-T02's live prediction driver. Same correction shape as MODEL-SERVE-008-T06. WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY MISSING: lastChanged (nowhere in the system), the fact that these values come from SAMPLED /predict rows rather than from the authoritative scheduled fetch, and that the tab goes empty again for any model whose driver is off.

tasks.title: TagObservation: one row per (model, tag), updated on every fetch, including a failed one
tasks.scope_note:
Per decisions.one_row_per_tag_updated_in_place. Additive table, no backfill.

lastChangedAt ADVANCES ONLY ON A DIFFERENT VALUE; lastSeenAt advances on every fetch that returned the tag at all. That distinction is the whole feature — collapsing them gives back exactly the aggregate-range inference T29 already has.

WRITE THE ROW BEFORE drop_bad_feature_rows, per T01 read 1, or lastStatus reads Good forever — MODEL-SERVE-001-T15 measured that exact outcome when it evaluated input.parquet as a status surface and found zero Bad cells surviving by construction.

A FAILED FETCH IS ITS OWN OUTCOME AND MUST NOT LEAVE THE ROW UNTOUCHED. If a source outage simply skips the write, a multi-hour NXDOMAIN period is indistinguishable from a multi-hour freeze, and PI is intermittently unreachable from this environment as a matter of record. Store lastFetchOutcome from diagnose_empty_pi_fetch's own verdict — its own design point is that a source failure and a genuinely empty range get different messages, and it de-duplicates and caps the reasons so the text fits the existing 2000-char slice.

REDACT AT THE READ BOUNDARY IF ANY CONNECTOR TEXT IS STORED. MODEL-SERVE-001-T09 and T10 each had to close this once: the container's own str(err) reaches failureReason verbatim and can carry a presigned URL's X-Amz-Signature, and lib/redact-urls.ts was applied read-side so stored rows keep full evidence. Reuse it; do not add a second redaction.

UNKNOWN IS A STATE. A model with no row yet reads unknown, never OK and never Frozen — T27's own rule for PSI's UNKNOWN, and MODEL-SERVE-006-T12's warmup amendment is the recorded precedent for what happens when a warm-up state is inferred from absence instead of stated.
tasks.rescope_2026_09_17:
RE-SCOPED BY T01 READ 1 — THIS IS A PYTHON CHANGE FIRST, NOT A PRISMA MIGRATION PLUS A SERVICE. decisions.one_row_per_tag_updated_in_place requires the row be written BEFORE drop_bad_feature_rows, or lastStatus reads Good forever. But materialize_window's response returns NO per-tag field at all (inference_window_service.py:365-373) and the frame that holds {tag}__status is discarded after :341. The join's behaviour is UNCHANGED — no pair is produced for a held interval, the Count probe still runs first, and metrics/points/pairedRows are still driven by joined rows alone. A test asserts exactly that: a range with a held value present and no pairs publishes the number while metrics stay null.

RENDERED AS 'Actual', BY OPERATOR DECISION, WITH THE SAFETY PROPERTY KEPT. The operator's instruction was to label this series Actual and to leave genuinely-measured lab to Model Evaluation. Done — and the held number travels under its OWN data key (`held`), never merged into `actual`. That separation is the whole safety argument: `actual` is what the residual, the SD band and every error metric read, and a held number entering those publishes a confident error against a value nobody measured in that interval. A test asserts `actual` and `residual` are untouched when a held value is applied. The line is drawn stepped and dashed because that is what it IS — one reading carried forward — and the caption states the value, when it was MEASURED, and how long it has been unchanged, so a flat line cannot read as a steady process.

THE TARGET HAD TO BE CAPTURED BEFORE IT COULD BE PUBLISHED. `_tag_observations` ran after `select_columns`, which narrows the frame to feature_columns — and the target is not a feature, so it had already been dropped. The read moved to BEFORE `select_columns` (still before the Bad-row drop, which is the other ordering constraint) and materialize gained an optional `target_column`, supplied by the scheduler from the descriptor it already resolves. The target still never enters the scored frame.

A REAL GAP FOUND BY ITS OWN TEST: `targetHeld` was resolved from a joined row's targetColumn, so it was null exactly when `rows` was empty — which is the state this surface exists for, and the state where a reader most wants to know what the lab last said. It now falls back to the PRODUCTION version's own sourceRun.targetY. Found because the test asserted the no-pairs case rather than only the happy path; a second test caught an arithmetic error of mine (44h is 2640 minutes, not 2880).

TESTS: 3 backend cases (held value published with its measured-at; never a pair, metrics stay null; null when no fetch has recorded the target) and 4 client cases (held applied across the axis; NEVER written into `actual`, with the residual asserted intact; omitted when the lab has never reported; borrows the prediction axis rather than inventing timestamps). Backend 109 passing in inference-window, client 24 in lib/monitoring; both tsc at their pre-existing baseline of 6.

=== FOLLOW-UP 2026-09-17: THE CHART WAS STILL SHOWING THE WAITING MESSAGE, AND THE DENSE SERIES NOW READS AS 'Predict'. TWO OPERATOR-REPORTED FIXES. ===

(1) THE RENDER GATE WAS WRONG, AND IT WAS MY OMISSION. T05 added the Actual series but left the gate on joined `points`, so with zero pairs EmptyTruth won every time and the operator still saw 'no lab measurement has arrived ... eligible at Sep 18, 00:00'. That message was true ABOUT PAIRS and false ABOUT THE SCREEN: there were 8 live predictions and a known lab value sitting unused. The gate now asks what the chart can actually DRAW — it carries three series (sparse joined actual, dense prediction, held target) and only the first needs a pair. The RESIDUAL chart deliberately keeps the `points` gate, because a residual genuinely cannot exist without a measured actual; that is the limit MODEL-SERVE-008-T05's own sentence states and it is unchanged.

(2) A HELD-ONLY VALUE HAD NO AXIS. A carried-forward reading has no timestamps of its own, so with no prediction series to borrow from there was nothing to plot it against and the line silently did not exist. `mergeLivePredictions` now accepts the visible range and, ONLY when the held value is the sole thing to draw, emits two endpoints across it — the constant over the window the user is already looking at. Tests assert those endpoints carry NO actual, NO predict and NO live: the axis is borrowed, never a measurement invented.

(3) THE DENSE SERIES NOW WEARS THE 'Predict' IDENTITY (operator decision). MODEL-SERVE-008-T04 had named it for its PLANE — 'Live predict', its own colour — on the reasoning that a window's predictions.parquet and a sampled /predict row are different artifacts. That provenance argument still holds and is UNCHANGED IN THE DATA: the two keys stay separate, nothing pools them into one series, and MODEL-SERVE-001-T10 item (6) is untouched. What changed is the LEGEND: both series are the model's own predictions, so the chart carries ONE 'Predict' entry rather than asking a reader to hold two names for one idea. The dense line is dashed against the window line's solid so the two provenances remain distinguishable when a range carries both. The 'Live Predictions (sampled)' section below is unchanged, as instructed — same heading, same chart, same caption.

VERIFIED LIVE on model 3991c43f over a real 24h range: 8 live predictions (first 2026-09-17T03:23 -> 0.6598, last 04:53 -> 0.7322) now feed the Predict line, and targetHeld { S204FBP.lab, value 196, measured 2026-09-15T05:59 } feeds Actual — while joined points stay 0 and metrics stay null, so nothing was turned into a pair to make the chart render. 4 new client cases for the held-only axis (28 in lib/monitoring, 60 across the monitoring suites); client tsc at its pre-existing baseline of 6; the Live Predictions section confirmed still present and rendering.

=== RESIDUAL CARD, 2026-09-17 (operator request: use Actual from PI and Predicted from model here too). ===

WHAT WAS BUILT, AND WHAT IT IS NOT. The card now draws `live - held` when no lab pair exists in range: the model's prediction minus the lab's LAST MEASURED value. THAT IS NOT A RESIDUAL and is not called one anywhere — a residual is predicted minus an actual measured IN THAT INTERVAL, and this subtracts a number carried forward from the last time the lab reported, which on this plant is roughly daily. It answers a real operational question ('how far has the model drifted from the last thing we actually know') and it is deliberately excluded from RMSE, R2 and the SD band, every one of which assumes a measured actual per point.

THREE SEPARATIONS KEEP THAT TRUE RATHER THAN MERELY STATED:
  - ITS OWN KEY. `heldDeviation`, never `residual`. Nothing that reads `residual` — sdCoverage, the SD band, RMSE, R2 — can pick it up by accident, and a test asserts `residual` and `actual` stay undefined on a deviation-only row.
  - A REAL RESIDUAL ALWAYS WINS. The deviation renders ONLY when no measured residual exists in range. It is the fallback that keeps the card informative while the lab is quiet, not a second opinion competing with the real one; a test asserts a genuine pair's residual survives untouched with a held value also present.
  - IT LOOKS DIFFERENT. Dashed and unfilled against the measured residual's solid filled area, so the two can never read as the same measurement.

THE GATE MOVED FOR THE SAME REASON THE OTHER CHART'S DID. It was on joined `points`, so the card showed the waiting message even when a prediction and a last-known lab value both existed. MODEL-SERVE-008-T05's sentence — a residual can only ever be as dense as the lab — is UNCHANGED and still rendered; what is added beneath it, only when a deviation is being drawn, names the quantity, gives the lab value and WHEN IT WAS MEASURED, and says plainly that it is excluded from RMSE, R2 and the SD band. A deviation is only as current as the number it is measured against, which is why the measured-at date travels with it.

CAVEAT THAT APPLIES TO THE CURRENT MODEL AND NOT TO THE FEATURE: model 3991c43f still emits SCALED predictions (0.64-0.73) against a raw lab value (196), per MODEL-SERVE-010-T05, so its deviation is currently ~-195 and meaningless. The operator is building a new dataset with the fixed pipeline; once a model is trained with an unscaled target both the Actual line and this deviation become interpretable. The code is correct; the existing artifact is not.

TESTS: 4 new cases (deviation computed from prediction minus last measured value; NEVER written into `residual`/`actual`; a measured residual left untouched when both exist; no deviation where there is no prediction). 32 passing in lib/monitoring, 60 across the monitoring suites, client tsc at its pre-existing baseline of 6.

acceptance_criteria: Every scheduled fetch updates one row per tag, and a tag whose value did not change has its lastSeenAt advanced while lastChangedAt stays put.
A failed or unreachable fetch records its own outcome and does not leave the row looking like an unchanged reading.
lastStatus records the fetch path's arrival health, captured before the Bad-row drop, and is labelled as arrival health rather than as PI quality.
Sensor Frozen is derived from lastChangedAt, names the frozen tags and how long they have been flat, and never fires for a tag that was already flat in training.
A model with no per-tag row yet reads unknown, never OK and never Frozen.
The monitoring status becomes Frozen when a tag is frozen, carrying a reason distinguishing a frozen feature tag from a frozen .lab target, and the deploy axis is untouched.
The Input Data tab shows last value, last seen and last changed for every tag without requiring synchronous /predict traffic, with the refetch cadence stated.
A stored last value renders in engineering units untouched — never inverse-scaled.
A held .lab value still produces no pair, and the Monitoring tab distinguishes 'the lab has not reported' from 'the lab reported the same value again'.
No per-fetch history row is written to Postgres; storage stays one current row per tag.

verification.description: PROVE lastChangedAt AND lastSeenAt DIVERGE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT: run three fetches where the value is identical and assert lastSeenAt advances three times while lastChangedAt does not move; then land a changed value and assert both advance. A fixture whose value changes every fetch cannot distinguish the two fields, and a single-fetch test cannot distinguish either from a blind upsert.

PROVE AN OUTAGE DOES NOT READ AS A FREEZE: simulate an unreachable source for three consecutive fetches and assert the row records the failure outcome and the model does not report Sensor Frozen. This is not hypothetical — PI returns NXDOMAIN from this environment as a matter of record, and MODEL-SERVE-001-T18's own live check caught the same host succeeding and failing an hour apart.

PROVE lastStatus IS CAPTURED BEFORE THE BAD-ROW DROP: run a fetch whose tag returns a non-Good status and assert the row records it. MODEL-SERVE-001-T15 measured that input.parquet has zero Bad cells surviving by construction, so a test reading the stored frame instead of the fetch result would assert Good and pass against the defect.

BOTH SIDES OF THE TRAINING-CONSTANT GUARD: a tag flat in training (near-zero column_stats.std) is NOT badged after any duration, and a tag that genuinely stops moving IS. A fixture containing only stuck tags passes against an implementation that badges every flat column, which would mark every setpoint frozen forever — MODEL-SERVE-001-T29's own V21 makes the negative half the more important one.

PROVE THE HELD .lab VERDICT IS RECORDED AND STILL UNPAIRED: run a truth join across a range where the lab reported once and PI held the value for every other interval, and assert exactly one pair AND that the target's row shows its lastSeenAt advanced with lastChangedAt unmoved. Asserting only the pair count cannot tell a recorded verdict from a discarded one; asserting only the row cannot tell the probe still holds.

PROVE THE EIGHTH EMPTY STATE READS DIFFERENTLY: render Monitoring for a model whose target was fetched and found unchanged, and assert the copy names that case distinctly from the seven other branches. The screenshot's current message is the seventh-adjacent one and is correct for cause (A); a test asserting merely that some message renders passes against the flat sentence T10 and T11 each had to replace once.

PROVE THE STORAGE SHAPE HOLDS: run a day of fetches for a 21-tag model and assert the Postgres row count for this table is 21, not 504. architecture.storage_authority's claim that no Prisma model stores timeseries rows is a property worth keeping true, and an update-in-place that accidentally inserts is invisible until the table is large.

PROVE THE LIST PAGE DID NOT BECOME N+1: assert the models-list query count is unchanged with the frozen signal rendering. MODEL-SERVE-001-T23 had to design around exactly this for lastFailure, and T30's constraint is that buildAlerts is pure over the list payload — a per-model fetch satisfies every shape assertion and fails this one.

features.title: A transient infrastructure error is a terminal window status — one outage permanently holed 45 windows
features.description: `fail()` writes status FAILED for EVERY cause, so a DNS resolution failure and an unresolvable target end the same way: terminally, with no attempt counter and no re-queue. A two-day historian outage therefore did not degrade the record, it permanently holed it — 45 windows that will never be re-attempted unless a human presses retry on each one. The data is recoverable; the automation is not.
features.placement_note: FILED AS ITS OWN FEATURE RATHER THAN A MODEL-SERVE-006 TASK, for one specific reason: 006 is status completed / progress 100, and appending a pending task to it would make that status a lie — the same objection this ledger's own feature-status rules state (never mark completed while work remains, and by symmetry never leave completed standing over new pending work). Same convention MODEL-SERVE-008 and 009 used when their subject spanned an already-closed feature. The SUBJECT is unambiguously 006's: `fail()` and `dispatchDue` both live in inference-window-scheduler.service.ts.
findings: MEASURED 2026-09-17, NOT ESTIMATED. 71 of 117 windows FAILED. By cause: DNS resolution 45, container-vanished (server restarted mid-flight) 18, backend-cannot-reach-python 4, source-returned-no-rows 3, reconcile timeout 2. The DNS text is verbatim `Failed to resolve 'scgc-piwebapi.scg.com' ([Errno 8] nodename nor servname provided, or not known)` wrapped in urllib3's Max-retries envelope.

THE 61% RATE IS A HISTORICAL ARTIFACT AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS A CURRENT ONE. 44 of the 45 DNS failures landed on 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-15 — the same outage MODEL-SERVE-001-V12 was BLOCKED on, when the host returned NXDOMAIN. Exactly one DNS failure has occurred since (2026-09-17 02:05), against 11 successes the same day. The host now resolves to 10.43.38.60 and answers HTTP 401, verified ten consecutive times from the python service's own interpreter. Any argument that rests on a 61% live failure rate is resting on an outage that is over.

QUERY TRAP, RECORDED SO THE NEXT READER DOES NOT REPEAT IT: grouping failures with a LIKE '%exceeded%' bucket collides with `Max retries exceeded` inside the DNS message and reports 28 reconcile timeouts. The real count is 2. Classify on `exceeded 1800000ms` or on the resolution text, never on `exceeded` alone.

`attempts` IS A DEAD COLUMN ON THIS PATH. InferenceWindow.attempts exists and is 0 on every DNS-failed row; the scheduler never increments it. So there is no record of how many times a window was tried, and no state a bounded-retry policy could read without adding one.

THE DATA IS NOT LOST, ONLY THE AUTOMATION. `retryService` already returns a FAILED window to PENDING with failureReason cleared and a fresh run token, and `backfillService` covers a range. So the ledger's own definition of done — 'a window that did not run is visible as a gap and backfillable through the same path a live window uses' — is SATISFIED today. What is missing is that nothing does it automatically, and nothing tells the user 45 windows are sitting there retryable.
openDecisions: AUTO-RETRY, OR SURFACE-AND-LET-THE-USER-RETRY? The smaller option by far is the second: the recovery path already exists, so the change is a count and a button — 'N windows failed transiently in this range' with a bulk retry through the EXISTING retryService — and it touches no dispatch code at all. Auto-retry means classifying error strings (fragile, and the classifier is the whole correctness of the feature), writing `attempts` for the first time, choosing a backoff, and proving a retrying window cannot starve the live one against INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 1. RECOMMENDATION ON RECORD, NOT ADOPTED: surface-and-retry first, and only then decide whether automation earns its risk.

WHAT COUNTS AS TRANSIENT? DNS resolution, connection reset and the reconcile timeout plainly are. Container-vanished (18 rows, 'the server restarted while this window was in flight') is transient in cause but its window may have partially run, so re-queueing it is not obviously safe. Unresolvable target and missing featureSpecKey are terminal and must stay terminal. Below-minRows is already SKIPPED rather than FAILED and is not in scope. Get this list wrong toward 'transient' and the scheduler retries a window that can never succeed, forever, on one concurrency slot.

DOES A PERMANENT HOLE NEED TO BE VISIBLE AS A GAP? 45 windows in the record simply do not exist as scored points. MODEL-SERVE-008-T04's coverage strip states counts for the range it renders; a reader looking at a sparse chart currently cannot tell 'the lab was quiet' from 'the historian was unreachable for two days and nobody retried'. Those are different sentences and this ledger has refused to pool that kind of pair before.

tasks.title: Decide the transient/terminal split and surface the retryable backlog — do not start with auto-retry
tasks.scope_note:
BLOCKED ON openDecisions[0] AND [1]. Both are decisions about risk, not about code, and the cheap half of this feature does not depend on either being answered in the ambitious direction.

REUSE, DO NOT REBUILD: retryService (inference-window.authorized.service.ts) already performs the exact state transition, including minting a fresh run token — a second implementation would be a second thing to disagree with it, which is the objection MODEL-SERVE-005-T03 raised against a parallel join path.

IF AUTO-RETRY IS CHOSEN LATER, IT INHERITS MODEL-SERVE-006-T02's CONSTRAINT WHOLE. Dispatch is newest-first over a single slot precisely so a deep backfill cannot starve the live window; a retry queue is another backfill by another name. Verified 2026-09-17 that the existing order does drain a backlog (36 PENDING -> 32 across successive ticks while the newest window still landed on its own cadence), so the order is not the thing to change.

tasks.title: A test hardcoded a copy of env.INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS and failed when the default moved — assert the constant, not a literal
tasks.scope_note:
FOUND BY MODEL-SERVE-008-T01 AS UNRELATED PRE-EXISTING BREAKAGE, FIXED HERE. `inference-window.authorized.service.spec.ts`'s case 'falls back to env.INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS for a source with no interval concept (e.g. SQL)' asserted the literal 30 while env.config.ts line 186 defaults INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS to 15. So the case failed on the DEFAULT'S VALUE rather than on the FALLBACK BEHAVIOUR it is named for — a permanently red test that said nothing about its own subject, and red tests that are known-ignorable are how a real regression gets waved through.

DECISION, FROM THE USER, 2026-09-17: 15 IS CORRECT AND STAYS. The production default is not changed. Only the test moves.

THE FIX IS NOT s/30/15/. Substituting the new literal reproduces the same defect and it would drift again the next time the default moves. The case now reads `env.INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS` — the same constant the production path reads — so the assertion states its actual claim, 'the SQL fallback IS the env default', and cannot go stale. It remains a real test rather than a tautology because its sibling case above asserts a DERIVED floor of 6 from a real intervalTime (deriveMinRows, lib/inference-windows.ts): the two together prove derivation and fallback take different paths and produce different numbers.

VERIFIED: the inference-window suites now run 93 of 93 green. They had been 92 of 93 with this one case red since before MODEL-SERVE-008 began.

tasks.title: `prisma migrate dev` is unusable on this database — it reports drift and offers only a full reset
tasks.scope_note:
FOUND 2026-09-17 while adding MODEL-SERVE-008-T02's three additive columns. `pnpm db:migrate:dev` refuses with: migration `20260825030923_model_flow_005_fine_tuning_job` WAS MODIFIED AFTER IT WAS APPLIED (its checksum no longer matches the recorded one), therefore Prisma distrusts the whole history, reports a drift summary, and offers exactly one remedy — `prisma migrate reset`, which DROPS THE DATABASE. This database holds 391 real ModelTrainingRun rows and the entire inference-window record, so reset is not an available option for adding a column.

THE REPORTED DRIFT LINE IS A SYMPTOM, NOT THE CAUSE. The summary names `DatasetArtifact.droppedBadRows` as present in the database but not expected — yet that column IS in schema.prisma (line ~520), IS in the live table, and IS referenced by three migration files. It only appears because the checksum mismatch makes Prisma replay history it cannot trust. Fixing the modified migration is the actual work; chasing droppedBadRows is not.

WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD, so T02 was not blocked: the migration was written by hand from `prisma migrate diff --from-config-datasource --to-schema`, whose output was exactly and only the three intended ADD COLUMNs (confirming nothing else diverges), applied with psql, and recorded with `prisma migrate resolve --applied`. All three columns are additive with defaults, so this is safe on a populated table. The pre-existing drift is UNCHANGED and will block the next developer's `migrate dev` in exactly the same way.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING: whether to repair history (restore the modified migration to its applied form, or re-baseline) — and that is a decision about a shared database, not a local one, so it is not taken here. UNTIL THEN, EVERY SCHEMA CHANGE ON THIS REPO MUST USE THE DIFF-AND-RESOLVE PATH ABOVE AND MUST NEVER ANSWER PRISMA'S RESET PROMPT.

tasks.title: Sensor Frozen's tolerance is 0, so it detects only EXACTLY constant tags and cannot see a stuck instrument that dithers
tasks.scope_note:
FOUND BY MODEL-SERVE-009-T01 READ 4, FILED HERE RATHER THAN FIXED THERE (user decision 2026-09-17): choosing a non-zero default is a signal-SENSITIVITY decision and must not arrive as a side effect of a different feature.

MEASURED: InferenceSchedule.frozenTolerancePct is 0 on the live schedule, which is also the schema default (@default(0)). sensor-frozen.ts computes eps = frozenTolerancePct x (p99 - p1) from the baseline, so eps = 0 and the comparison reduces to EXACT FLOAT EQUALITY.

DO NOT READ THIS AS 'THE SIGNAL IS BROKEN' — THAT CLAIM WAS MADE DURING PLANNING AND MEASUREMENT DISPROVED IT. At eps = 0 the signal is live and correct on this plant: model 3991c43f reports FROZEN with four badged columns (FIC107R.PV, FIC114A.PV, FIC114B.PV, FY107.CPV) whose featureStats show max - min of exactly 0 in every recent window, while moving tags are correctly not badged. These are TRUE POSITIVES.

THE REAL GAP IS NARROWER AND IS openDecisions[0]'s OWN SUBJECT: exact equality catches a tag pinned to one bit-identical value and MISSES a stuck instrument whose last significant digit dithers — which on real hardware is the common failure. A transmitter frozen at 42.0001 / 42.0002 / 42.0001 is stuck and would never be badged.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING, AND ON WHAT EVIDENCE: a non-zero default expressed as a fraction of the training range (the basis T29 already chose, so the same setting means the same thing on a tag spanning 0.01 and one spanning 400). Pick it from a MEASUREMENT of this plant's real per-tag noise floor — the distribution of window ranges for tags known to be healthy — not from a round number. Raising it also trades in the other direction: too large and a slow-moving but live tag reads as frozen, which is why T29's guard (1) skipping training-flat columns stays load-bearing whatever value is chosen.

tasks.title: THE TARGET IS SILENTLY MIN-MAX SCALED AND DECLARED UNSCALED — every prediction is in scaled units while every actual is in engineering units
tasks.scope_note:
FOUND 2026-09-17 by an operator asking why the Actual line would not render on the Actual-vs-Predict chart. It is not a chart defect. THE MODEL'S PREDICTIONS AND THE LAB'S MEASUREMENTS ARE IN DIFFERENT UNITS.

THE EVIDENCE, ALL MEASURED ON THE LIVE SYSTEM:
  - GOLD target column S204FBP.lab ranges min 0.0000 / max 1.0000 — the artifact the model trained on carries a SCALED target.
  - The descriptor reports target_scaled FALSE, and scalers[targetY] is absent/None.
  - The descriptor nonetheless carries scalingParams[S204FBP.lab] = {min 198.5, max 210.6}, which is exactly what a fitted min-max scaler for the target would store.
  - Live /predict returns 0.66-0.73. The SCHEDULED plane's own predictions.parquet returns 0.6441-0.6598. BOTH PLANES AGREE, so this is not a serving or driver bug.
  - The real lab value from PI is 196, and the training range is 198.5-210.6.
  - Inverse min-max of a live prediction closes the loop exactly: 198.5 + 0.6598 x (210.6 - 198.5) = 206.48, a plausible lab value.

ROOT CAUSE, LOCATED: `to_model_ready` (packages/py-scaling/src/softsensor_scaling/scaling.py:168) reads `method = scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER)` and DEFAULT_SCALER is 'minmax' (:39). `artifact_service.scale` calls it over `tag_columns(source)`, which INCLUDES the target. So a target absent from the `scalers` map is min-max scaled ANYWAY — silently, with its fitted params recorded in scalingParams. Meanwhile `feature_spec_service.build_feature_spec` (:355) computes `spec['target_scaled'] = scalers.get(target_y, 'none') != 'none'` from that SAME absent entry, and therefore reports False. One missing map entry produces both the scaling AND the claim that it did not happen.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: no lab pair has ever existed for this model (truthRows 0 across every joined window), so no residual was ever computed. The first real lab sample would have produced residual = 0.66 - 206 ~= -205 and an R2 about nothing. MODEL-SERVE-008-V02 is the verification written to catch exactly this ('take a row from the model's own test split, send it through the dense path, assert the logged prediction matches to numerical tolerance') and it is still PENDING — recorded there as unproven, and this is what it would have proven.

BLAST RADIUS — everything that compares a prediction to a measurement: the Actual-vs-Predict chart, the Residual chart, live-error metrics (r2/rmse/mae/sd from InferenceWindowTruth's sufficient statistics), the batch prediction path, and any alert or retrain trigger keyed on error. All are currently comparing scaled predictions to raw actuals. Note the chart's yDomain bug is SEPARATE and real (computed from joined pairs only, so it returns [0,1] when there are none and puts 196 off-scale) — but fixing it alone would render a wrong number convincingly, which is why it is not being fixed on its own.
tasks.result:
BOTH FIXES LANDED 2026-09-17 (operator instruction: stop scaling the target AND make the flag honest). NEW ARTIFACTS ARE CORRECT; EXISTING ONES ARE NOT REPAIRED — see the limitation at the end, it matters.

FIX 1 — THE PIPELINE NO LONGER SCALES THE TARGET, AND THE EXCLUSION IS BY NAME. `_scalable_tags(df, target_y)` returns every logical tag except the target, and all FOUR `to_model_ready` call sites in artifact_service now use it: the features+scale commit, the scale commit, `replay_holdout` and `replay_holdout_for_run`. By NAME rather than by omitting it from the scaler map, because the map is exactly what proved untrustworthy — `to_model_ready` reads `scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER)` with DEFAULT_SCALER 'minmax', so an unmapped tag is scaled anyway. All four sites, not just the GOLD writer: a holdout replayed with a scaled target against a GOLD written with a raw one would disagree about what the model's own y means, which is the same class of silently-different transform those call sites already warn about for the FEATURES.

FIX 2 — `target_scaled` NOW REPORTS WHAT HAPPENED, NOT WHAT WAS REQUESTED. It was `scalers.get(target_y, 'none') != 'none'`, read from the same map that drove the scaling — so it could never contradict it, and in production reported False over a target min-max scaled to 0-1. It now derives from `scaling_params`, which only carries tags that were actually FITTED. The flag can still be True: an artifact written before this fix carries fitted params for its target, and reading that is precisely what lets a consumer inverse-transform such a model's predictions rather than compare scaled output to engineering units.

TESTS: the existing case asserting `target_scaled is True` 'because TI-101 has a minmax scaler in BASE_SCALERS' was REWRITTEN rather than deleted — it encoded the old requested-not-actual contract, which is the defect itself. Added: True when the target really was scaled, False when only features were, `_scalable_tags` excluding the target (and excluding nothing when there is no target), and a NEGATIVE CONTROL asserting `to_model_ready` WOULD min-max an unmapped target to exactly [0.0, 1.0] — so a future change to DEFAULT_SCALER cannot quietly make the exclusion look unnecessary. Python 902 passing (was 897 with 1 failure), backend 364 passing across inference-window, model-serving and lib.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, STATED PLAINLY. Model 3991c43f is UNCHANGED and still wrong: its GOLD artifact was written with a scaled target, its stored feature_spec.json still says `target_scaled: false`, and it still emits 0.64-0.73 against a lab measuring in the 196-211 range. `feature_spec.json` is written once at GOLD-write time, so the corrected flag reaches a model only when its artifact is rebuilt — the same shape as MODEL-SERVE-001-T17's psiRefEdges note (UNKNOWN on every existing model until the artifact is rebuilt). RECOVERING THE EXISTING MODEL NEEDS A DECISION THAT IS NOT MINE: re-materialise GOLD and retrain (clean, invalidates the current artifact and version), or leave it and have consumers inverse-transform using the scalingParams already on the descriptor (no retrain, but every consumer must remember). Until one is taken, the Actual-vs-Predict chart, residuals, r2/rmse/mae, the batch path and any error-keyed alert remain apples-to-oranges FOR THAT MODEL.

THE CHART'S yDomain BUG IS STILL OPEN AND DELIBERATELY SO: it is computed from joined pairs only, so it returns [0,1] when there are none and puts a 196 actual off-scale. Fixing it before the units agree would render a wrong number convincingly, which is the opposite of what this defect is about.

A range whose windows are missing because the source was unreachable does not read as a range whose lab was quiet.
