features.title: Run Predict — one button, both prediction planes, on request
features.description: An operator watching a running model had no way to get a prediction NOW: windows are created and dispatched only by the scheduler sweep (INFERENCE_TICK_INTERVAL_MS, 5 min in this deployment), so the wait between wanting a reading and having one was up to a full tick on top of the window's own lag. This feature adds ONE affordance -- a Run Predict button on models/[id] -- that runs the SAME window the tick would have run, through the SAME dispatch path. It is a bypass of the WAIT, not of the rules: the schedule must exist, be ENABLED, and have a PRODUCTION version, exactly as the sweep requires. Chosen over the live-predict plane (LivePredictDriverService.scoreOne) deliberately, per the 2026-09-17 decision: the operator wants the full window artifact -- visible in Monitoring, Logs and health, retryable on failure -- not a chart point with no window row behind it. INCREMENT 2 (same day, user request): the window half answers in MINUTES, so the button changed nothing an operator could see. Run Predict now ALSO scores the live plane through the warm /predict, which is what puts a point on the Actual vs Predicted chart within seconds. The two halves are independent and reported separately -- a quiet source can leave the live half with no point while the window run is genuinely underway. Note what this does NOT do: only the PREDICTED series moves on click. LiveOverlayRow carries no actual and no residual by design (a dense predicted point has no lab counterpart), so the ACTUAL series still moves later, when ground truth joins on the window plane's own schedule.

tasks.title: InferenceWindowSchedulerService.dispatchOne made public, body unchanged
tasks.scope_note: Its own 'status !== PENDING' guard is what makes a second caller safe: a window already claimed by a sweep or by a double-click is a no-op, so one row never spawns two containers. The 'enabled: true' filter lives in dispatchDue and does NOT cover this path -- runNowService enforces enabled itself.

tasks.title: runNowService on InferenceWindowAuthorizedService
tasks.scope_note: 404 no schedule / 409 stopped / 422 no PRODUCTION version, in that order, with backfillService messages reused verbatim. The boundary comes from windowStartsBetween over the same now-lag-cadence upper bound insertDueWindows uses -- never computed inline, because (modelVersionId, windowStart) is the unique constraint the whole feature rests on. createMany+skipDuplicates then dispatchOne fire-and-forget: an HTTP request must not block on a container spawn. A non-PENDING window is REPORTED, not re-run; FAILED points at the explicit retry route rather than becoming a second, undeclared retry path that loses attempts.

tasks.title: POST /inference/run-now
tasks.scope_note: No body and no DTO: nothing is chosen by the caller. The window is always the latest fully-elapsed one, computed server-side from this schedule own cadence and lag.

tasks.title: inferenceWindowService.runNow on the client
tasks.scope_note: Returns the server message alongside the data: success answers two ways (202 queued, 200 already ran) and only the server own wording distinguishes them. dispatched is the machine-readable half of the same fact.

tasks.title: useRunPredict hook
tasks.scope_note: Page holds no logic. The toast says QUEUED, never that a prediction exists -- the response cannot prove the second, the same optimistic-write discipline MODEL-SERVE-001-T09 removed from handleToggleDeploy. Errors print the server text verbatim; one merged sentence for several distinct refusals is what sent people after the wrong cause before.

tasks.title: Run Predict button on models/[id]
tasks.scope_note: Header action row, next to Start/Stop. Disabled while stopped (the server refuses with 409 regardless, and a button that always fails is worse than one plainly unavailable) and while the first status read is outstanding, for the same reason Stop carries that guard. On success it runs the same refreshModels/refresh/refetchInferenceStatus trio the deploy toggle uses -- without it the new window reaches no tab.

tasks.title: LivePredictDriverService.scoreOne returns a discriminated outcome
tasks.scope_note: Was Promise<void> with seven silent returns -- correct for a background sweep, wrong for a button: Run Predict would report success and produce nothing, with the reason only in a server log (the defect MODEL-SERVE-001-T26 refuses). Now {ok:true,predicted,at} | {ok:false,reason}, every path still fail-soft and livePredictLastRunAt still stamped in the same finally. 'at' is the scored ROW's timestamp, never Date.now() -- the reading is as old as the data. 'predicted' comes from the /predict RESPONSE, never a read-back of PredictionLog: that row is written afterwards by the serving process's own BackgroundTask and may be sampled out by SERVING_LOG_SAMPLE_RATE, so the response is the only value that is true either way. tick()'s call site ignores the return, unchanged.

tasks.title: runNowService awaits one live score; the chart reads it back
tasks.scope_note: AWAITED, unlike the window dispatch -- scoreOne is a warm /predict (seconds, no container), and firing it and forgetting would let the client's refetch race the write, which is the whole point of the increment. It cannot fail the request: by then the window is queued, so a throw degrades to {ok:false,reason} carrying the server's own text. livePredictEnabled is deliberately NOT consulted and NOT set -- that flag governs the background sweep; this is one operator-initiated score (2026-09-17 decision). Client: runNow's data widens with 'live'; the toast names the predicted value and reports the two halves separately; usePredictionMonitoring gains a refreshKey folded into its three cache keys (the same tick mechanism use-inference-status uses -- its keys carried only model id and range, so a fresh point was invisible until the range toggle moved), passed down from the page through ModelMonitoringTab. onRan fires twice, immediately and once ~2s later, because the PredictionLog write is a BackgroundTask that runs after /predict answers -- one late read, not a poll.

tasks.title: MonitoringTooltip reads the three keys the chart already draws (both charts)
tasks.scope_note: FOUND LIVE 2026-09-17 once Run Predict started producing live points: the Actual vs Predict crosshair sat on a VISIBLE point and read 'Actual -- / Predict --'. The cause was not missing data. LiveOverlayRow keeps live, held and heldDeviation under their OWN keys deliberately (held must never reach the residual or the SD band; a window's prediction and a /predict row are different artifacts) and the chart draws all three -- the tooltip was the one reader still typed to MonitoringRow alone, so it had no row for any of them. Fixed at the READ only; no key was merged. Labels are QUALIFIED where the identity on screen is broader than the number's provenance: 'Actual (last reported)' for held (carried forward by PI, not measured in that interval) and 'Predict (live)' for the serving-plane point. heldDeviation gets 'Vs last reported' and is never called a residual. The measured pair renders unchanged, and a row carrying nothing still shows the dashed pair rather than an empty box. RESIDUAL CHART, same defect, same fix: Residual and Error % exist only for a MEASURED pair, so a live-overlay point showed two dashes -- saying 'this could not be computed' about a point that was never in that calculation. They now render only when the measured error exists, or when there is nothing else on the row (so an empty row still shows the dashed pair rather than an empty box).

tasks.title: Run Predict shows an in-flight state
tasks.scope_note: The button awaits a warm /predict round trip (materialize the last few minutes, read the newest row, score it) before the request answers, so a greyed-out button alone read as a press that did nothing. Spinner + 'Predicting...' label, the same Loader2 treatment settings/account.tsx already uses for an in-flight mutation. The disabled set is unchanged -- busy was already in it; what was missing was only the affordance saying WHY.

tasks.title: One identity mapping across the Monitoring tab: Actual = chart-1, Predict = foreground
tasks.scope_note: The Actual vs Predict LEGEND already said Actual = chart-1 / Predict = foreground while the chart drew the opposite; the 'actual' and 'predict' lines were swapped to match (file mtime 14:22, outside this session). Three readers still carried the old mapping and were finished here: 'held' (wears the Actual identity -- now chart-1, kept distinguishable by its dashed STEP, not by a second hue), 'live' (wears the Predict identity -- now foreground, kept distinguishable from 'predict' by solid-vs-dash, which is the provenance separation, not decoration), and the 'actual' dot/activeDot fills (still filled foreground; activeDot's stroke is now --background so the halo reads on either theme). MonitoringTooltip's swatches were swapped to match, and the RESIDUAL section's legend too -- it had kept the pre-swap colours, so one tab named the same two series in opposite colours in its two halves. NOT touched: the residual chart strokes themselves (residual and heldDeviation both draw chart-1 while the tooltip swatches them chart-5) -- a pre-existing mismatch on a different axis, recorded here rather than folded into a colour swap it is not part of.

tasks.title: The scheduled plane gets a read path that does not require a ground-truth join
tasks.scope_note: FOUND BY INSPECTION 2026-09-17 while explaining the chart: a scheduled window's predictions reach the Monitoring chart ONLY through GET /inference/truth, which serves the JOINED pairs. On this plant the lab target reports roughly daily, so every InferenceWindowTruth row reads truthRows=0, no pairs object is written, and an hour's 60 predictions sit correctly computed in object storage and render NOWHERE. Right for an Actual-vs-Predict PAIR; wrong as the only way to see the plane at all -- everything the operator saw as Predict was the live /predict series. NEW READ PATH, metrics.json ONLY, never predictions.parquet: the infer container already computed predictionMean/Min/Max/Std over the rows it scored, so an hourly series is one small JSON read per window rather than a Parquet open plus a second aggregation that could disagree with the first (user chose hourly resolution over 60 pts/hour, 2026-09-17). python ground_truth_service.metrics_series + POST /inference-window/metrics-series take EXPLICIT keys like truth-series does (the database is the index); an unresolvable key is COUNTED and skipped, and the count is surfaced in the UI so a reclaimed window reads as a gap rather than as a model that did not run. NestJS getScheduledSeriesService restricts to SUCCEEDED windows with a metricsKey, carries each window's pinned modelVersionId onto its point (a promote mid-range means adjacent points came from different models), and degrades to an empty series with the reason on a python/object-store failure. Client: useScheduledSeries + mergeScheduledPredictions fold the points in at each window's own windowStart, on their OWN key -- an hour summarised by its mean is neither a joined pair's predict nor a single instant's live, and the user's decision was both series visible and distinct (chart-4, dotted, its own legend entry 'Predict (hourly)' and tooltip row 'Predict (hour avg)').

tasks.title: Actual vs Predict becomes the WINDOW plane only
tasks.scope_note: User decision 2026-09-17: the live serving-plane series is removed from this chart and the window plane's series takes the plain 'Predict' identity, so the chart compares an actual and a prediction that came from the SAME window at the SAME time -- both out of predictions.parquet -- rather than putting a per-instant series and an hourly one on one axis. Removed: the live Line from actual-vs-predict-chart.tsx and the 'Predict (live)' tooltip row. Renamed: legend 'Predict (hourly)' -> 'Predict' (chart-4, dotted line with visible dots, since it is hourly against the rest); tooltip 'Predict (hour avg)' -> 'Predict'. The paired per-row predict Line was recoloured from foreground to chart-4 to sit under that one legend entry -- both series behind it ARE the same plane's predictions, so one label hides no second provenance; the dash still separates a per-row pair from the hourly summary. THE ONE QUALIFICATION KEPT: when a paired prediction and an hourly summary land on the same row, the hourly one reads 'Predict (hour avg)' -- two identical labels holding different numbers is worse than a longer one. NOT removed: LiveOverlayRow.live and mergeLivePredictions, which the Residual chart still populates, and the Live Predictions section below, which is unchanged.

tasks.title: The held Actual step is applied over the FINAL axis, not a partial one
tasks.scope_note: FOUND ON SCREEN by the operator, not by a test: Actual appeared only across 14:13-14:23 local -- the few minutes three Run Predict live scores happened to occupy -- while the hourly Predict points sat at 14:00 and 15:00 with no Actual beside them, so there was nothing to compare at the only timestamps that mattered. CAUSE, introduced by T12: the held value was applied INSIDE mergeLivePredictions, which was correct while that function produced the final axis and became wrong the moment mergeScheduledPredictions began adding hourly rows afterwards -- those rows carried no held. FIX: extracted applyHeldValue and called it LAST in the tab (live merge, then scheduled merge, then held). Second defect in the same place: heldDeviation read row.live ?? row.predict and did not know about scheduled, so with the live series now off this chart an hourly point -- often the ONLY prediction on its row -- had a blank deviation exactly where a reader looks. Now live ?? predict ?? scheduled, preferring a real pair over a summary. applyHeldValue is idempotent so the path through mergeLivePredictions and a second call over a widened axis cannot compound.

tasks.title: A band the chart can draw before the lab joins
tasks.scope_note: Operator reported the SD area not working. It was not broken, it was UNDEFINED: sd1/2/3 are built only in buildMonitoringRows, as [actual +/- k*sd] where sd is the RESIDUAL SD from windowStats -- both inputs come from joined pairs, and windowStats returns 0 below 2 pairs, so with zero pairs no row carries a band at all while the legend kept promising one. The operator asked for it computed from Actual and Predict out of the parquet rather than from a lab join; stated plainly first that predictions.parquet holds no actual (timestamp + prediction only, input.parquet is features only), so the only pre-join actual is the HELD tag value. Added heldDeviationStats (spread of predicted - held across the visible range) and applyHeldDeviationBand (that spread drawn around the held Actual). NOT the residual SD and never merged with it: it measures distance from a value carried forward since the lab last reported, so it is model CONSISTENCY, not model error, and it feeds no metric -- RMSE, R2 and the residual SD still read joined pairs only. A row that already carries a real band keeps it, so a range gaining its first lab sample shows the true band there and this one elsewhere. The legend switches to plus/minus 1 SD (vs last reported) while there are no pairs, because one band shape meaning two different things must say which is on screen.

tasks.title: Residual Analysis draws its SD guardrails before the lab joins, and binds its own colours
tasks.scope_note: The monitoring ResidualChart already MATCHED the evaluation-flow reference structurally (SdBackground layers, SdGuard pairs labelled with each band own coverage counted from zero outward, zero baseline, filled residual Area) -- it drew nothing because sd came from stats.sd, the residual SD, which is 0 until there are two measured pairs, and sdCoverage counted r.residual only. Now the tab passes the SAME held-deviation spread the Actual-vs-Predict band uses when no residual SD exists, with a new sdBasis prop (residual | held) so the two meanings behind one identical picture are stated rather than inferred; sdCoverage reads the series the guardlines were computed FROM, never a mix -- counting measured residuals against a held-based SD would put a percentage under a line it does not describe. heldSd and the banded rows were lifted into shared memos so the band on one chart and the guardlines on the other are ONE number. Also ported the reference own colour-binding discipline (its MODEL-FLOW-019-T17): RESIDUAL_COLOR/SD1/SD2/SD3_COLOR are exported from the chart and consumed by both its marks and the tab legend, which had carried the same five literals a second time.

tasks.title: The held-deviation line gets both readouts, and a percent mode to live in
tasks.scope_note: Two gaps behind one request. (1) The Residual chart PERCENT mode excluded the held-deviation series entirely, because those rows carry no percentageError -- that needs a measured actual -- so switching to Percentage emptied the chart for exactly the ranges this series exists to cover. Added heldDeviationPct (deviation as a share of the held value, computed in applyHeldValue beside heldDeviation) and the series now draws in both modes. (2) The tooltip showed only the absolute gap; it now shows both forms, mirroring Residual / Error % above, because a 4-unit gap on a 114 reading and one on a 12 reading are not the same thing. Undefined rather than Infinity when the held value is 0. Neither figure is a residual or an error and neither enters a metric -- the labels stay Vs last reported / Vs last reported %. Also bound the tooltip Residual swatch to the chart own exported RESIDUAL_COLOR, finishing T16 binding.

tasks.title: Held-deviation readouts use the measured pair own wording
tasks.scope_note: User decision 2026-09-17, overriding the qualifier this ledger had argued for: the tooltip rows read Residual and Error %, not Vs last reported. The collision is prevented by EXCLUSION rather than by a longer label -- they render only when no measured residual is on the row, mirroring the chart, where showHeldDeviation draws the series only when no measured residual exists in range, so two rows named Residual holding different numbers cannot appear. Legend drops its conditional suffix for the same reason. Meaning moved to the captions, which is also where two STALE claims were corrected: the residual caption said the deviation is excluded from RMSE, R2 AND THE SD BAND, which stopped being true at T15 when the band began to be computed from these very deviations (now: excluded from RMSE and R2, and the guardrails are the spread of these deviations, not of measured error); and the Actual-vs-Predict caption asserted the shaded band is plus/minus 1 SD OF THE RESIDUAL unconditionally, so with no pairs it described a band that was not on screen.

tasks.title: The Actual-vs-Predict Y domain spans every series it draws
tasks.scope_note: Operator asked for the chart to span its values with the lines centred. The centring arithmetic was already right -- the domain is symmetric about the data midpoint -- but it was computed from the WRONG INPUT: actual/predict read out of rows, the JOINED pairs alone. Two consequences once the chart grew other series. With no lab pair in range the value list was empty and the domain fell back to [0, 1], putting lines that live around 110 entirely off screen -- which is what the operator was seeing. And even with pairs, the hourly scheduled series and the held step could not influence the domain at all, so they could sit outside it. Now read from rowsWithBand across actual, predict, scheduled and held. The zero-height guard also had to follow T15: it sized the domain with stats.sd, the residual SD, while the band on screen may have been drawn from the held-deviation spread -- it now uses whichever spread the band actually came from.

tasks.title: Brush removed; ChartZoomControls is the only zoom affordance
tasks.scope_note: Removed the recharts Brush from both monitoring charts. THE BRUSH WAS THE ONLY THING APPLYING THE WINDOW: the charts received `brush` and handed its indices straight to the Brush component, so deleting it alone would have left the zoom buttons changing state with nothing happening on screen. Each chart now slices its own data over [startIndex, endIndex] -- endIndex INCLUSIVE, the convention the controls and the Brush both used, hence the +1. The dead `onBrush` prop is gone from both components and both call sites. The zoom controls total was `points.length` (joined pairs) while the charts draw `rowsWithBand`; indexing a window over one array and slicing another is off-by-however-many-unpaired-rows, so it now counts the rows actually drawn. The Residual section lost its only zoom affordance with its Brush, so it gains a ChartZoomControls of its own -- writing the SAME brush state, which is not a second window: the two charts already share a recharts syncId.

tasks.title: Y-axis ticks in four significant digits, in a gutter wide enough to hold them
tasks.scope_note: The Actual-vs-Predict Y axis had NO tickFormatter at all, so recharts printed the raw float -- 110.05700050354004 -- into width 44 and clipped it. Added formatAxisValue (shared, lib/monitoring.ts) and widened both axes to 68. SIGNIFICANT DIGITS, NOT DECIMALS: this axis carries a process value whose magnitude is unknown to the component (110.1, or 0.4821, or 1204) and a fixed decimal count is either noise or nothing depending on which; four significant digits keep the same information density at every scale. Trailing zeros are kept (110.0, not 110) so the tick column stays one width and the labels align. Non-finite returns an empty label rather than NaN. The residual axis kept its percent suffix and now formats the number the same way.

tasks.title: Live RMSE against the held actual, so the header stops reading a dash
tasks.scope_note: The header KPI had read -- awaiting lab results -- since the model started: its only source is liveMetrics.rmse, pooled from JOINED lab pairs, and this plant has none (truthRows 0 everywhere; the sweeper runs 24h after a window closes). Now falls back to the same basis the band, guardrails and Residual line use: predictions squared against the last reported lab value. NO FOURTH RMSE FORMULA -- heldEvalPoints maps the rows into the pairs computeMetrics already consumes (lib/model-evaluation.ts, the canonical client math the backend live-error.ts says it mirrors), so the header and the evaluation screen cannot drift. Rows with a MEASURED actual are excluded: they already feed the real pooled metric and mixing the two yields a number that is neither. Prediction precedence matches applyHeldValue (predict, then scheduled, then live) so the deviation on screen and the header agree row by row. ONLY rmse is read -- R2 against a near-constant held actual is degenerate (ssTot tends to 0) and would render a confident meaningless number. The real metric always wins; n>1 required. Basis stated via a new rmseBasis prop on MonitoringRangeBar, riding the suffix that already existed (units, vs last reported, N windows). Computed client-side by decision: the deviations are already in memory, so it is one pass over 24-720 rows with no request, versus a round trip plus an object re-read per range change.

tasks.title: The model detail header names the algorithm
tasks.scope_note: Rendered under the model name beside plant and node, from model.data.config.algorithm through ALGORITHM_LABELS -- the SAME map the wizard Step 3 and the deploy summary render from, so Random Forest cannot come to mean two different things on two screens. A candidate sweep also shows chosen from N candidates, from config.algorithms, so a primary that was SELECTED reads differently from one that was the only option. SOURCE CAVEAT, recorded rather than hidden: data.config is the saved wizard configuration. The version actually serving traffic carries its own sourceRun.algorithm, which is the stronger answer, but NO client endpoint exposes it today (checked model-version authorized controllers). Verified in the database that the two agree on both live models (TM2 and TM3, both random_forest, config and PRODUCTION sourceRun); they can only diverge if a retrain lands a different algorithm than the one configured. Exposing the running version algorithm on input-schema would retire the caveat and is the obvious follow-up.

features.title: Residual-SD health axis, and ONE Monitoring Status badge
features.description: Every health signal watched the model's INPUTS or its plumbing; nothing graded whether the model was still RIGHT, so a model fetching cleanly from live instruments with un-drifted inputs rendered a green pill while predicting badly. Adds the output-error axis: the pooled live residual SD over joined truth pairs, measured against the run's own test-split residual SD, reported as Warning at 1-2x and Alert beyond 3x. Also collapses the separate Health pill into the Monitoring Status badge (normal/warning/alert/frozen/offline), which until now was driven by the hand-set prodStatus column and could read Normal beside a Health pill reading Alert.

tasks.title: baselineResidualSd resolver (lib/model-version-residual-sd.ts)
tasks.scope_note: Precedence sd -> residual_sd -> rmse. The rmse fallback is safe in one direction only: rmse = sqrt(sd^2 + bias^2) >= sd, so a fallback baseline is WIDER, the ratio SMALLER and the verdict QUIETER. It can miss a real degradation; it cannot invent one. Null (no usable metric) maps to UNKNOWN, never OK.

tasks.title: Record the reference residual SD at training-run completion
tasks.scope_note: Written in ModelRunAuthorizedService.complete, best-effort after the durable write, from python run_predictions' residual_sd. NOT in the trainer (it emits r2/rmse/mae only and nothing in CI builds that image, so a trainer-side addition is a silent no-op) and NOT at Save Model (an HTTP round trip inside the one atomic commit boundary). Reaches ModelVersion.metrics for free through model-version-from-run.ts.

tasks.title: classifyResidualSd (lib/residual-sd-health.ts) + spec
tasks.scope_note: Grades liveSd/baselineSd against the schedule's own warnSd/criticalSd. REJECTED: share-of-points-outside-the-band, which is scale-invariant when the SD is recomputed from the residuals being graded (10x the error, identical verdict); and counting window MEANS, whose null spread is baselineSd/sqrt(n), making a >32% threshold unreachable dead code at ~60 rows per window. Computes no error math of its own - poolTruthStats/computeLiveError own that. MIN_RESIDUAL_SD_PAIRS = 30.

tasks.title: RESIDUAL_SD_WARN / RESIDUAL_SD_CRITICAL folded into classifyModelHealth
tasks.scope_note: Ranks BELOW DRIFT_* in both tiers: drifted inputs EXPLAIN a widened error, so the upstream cause leads. BAD_DATA and STALE keep outranking both - an error computed from bad or stale readings measures nothing. NOT gated behind driftMonitor (false by default), for the same reason liveness is not. A measured in-spec error returns OK even with drift watching off, rather than falling through to OFF.

tasks.title: getHealthStatus pools InferenceWindowTruth and returns residualSd
tasks.scope_note: One query over the production version already resolved for drift. No object read and no second HTTP round trip - InferenceWindowTruth carries sufficient statistics. Return type ANNOTATED and present on every branch, per the T29 follow-up that found an inferred type let a branch omit a field the client required. TRUTH_POOL_TAKE is 720 windows (30 days hourly), DELIBERATELY NOT PRODUCTION_WINDOW_TAKE (24): a residual needs a measured lab actual, those arrive roughly daily, and MIN_RESIDUAL_SD_PAIRS is 30 - so a 24-window horizon would have made the axis structurally unable to fire, a silent no-op no test would catch since every test supplies its own rows.

tasks.title: ONE Monitoring Status badge: monitoringStatus() replaces the Health pill
tasks.scope_note: monitoringStatus() derives normal/warning/alert/frozen/offline from the MEASURED health axis; the hand-set prodStatus column stops driving the badge. UNKNOWN maps to offline, never normal. Infra-first precedence kept verbatim from effectiveProdStatus. The reason suffix survived the merge and renders as 'Monitoring: Warning - residual 1-2SD'. The badge reads inferenceStatus.health.status, NOT model.data.monitoring.status: the list payload carries liveness only, so reading it would badge a healthy running model 'Offline' and a warning one 'Offline - residual 1-2SD'. monitoringStatusFromHealth() is the shared mapping; monitoringStatus() wraps it for the list and carries that warning in its own doc.

tasks.title: Model LIST payload carries the residual-SD verdict
tasks.scope_note: TWO batched queries for the WHOLE page, never per-model: modelVersion.findMany over the production versions, then ONE inferenceWindowTruth.groupBy summing their sufficient statistics. That batchability is exactly why this axis can ride the list path while DRIFT cannot - drift needs a gold-artifact baseline read per model. Bounded by the SHARED TRUTH_POOL_DAYS (30) horizon, a TIME bound rather than a row count, because a row-count take cannot be expressed as a group-by bound and two different bounds would let the list badge and the detail badge grade the same model from different samples. getHealthStatus was switched to the same bound in this task (it briefly used a 720-row take). Covered by a spec asserting the aggregate runs ONCE for three models, and that a model with 40 pairs at 4x its reference SD reaches ALERT/RESIDUAL_SD_CRITICAL on the LIST payload - which before this task could only ever emit OFF or a liveness ALERT.

global_definition_of_done: A scheduled model produces one record per time window; a window that did not run is visible as a gap and backfillable through the same path a live window uses.
Evaluation and monitoring read one metric registry over stored predictions — adding a backfillable metric never requires a refit.
'Deployed' is derived from the monitoring record, never asserted by a caller.

A production model's fitted artifact and feature spec are retained and pinned for as long as any version references them — the model object and the spec it needs are two objects in different places, and losing either is the same outage.
A saved Model can be promoted to production and rolled back without building or deploying an image.
At most one PRODUCTION version exists per model, enforced by the database.
The transform applied at inference is the same code as the one applied at training — proven by scoring a training-set row through the live endpoint, not by inspection.
A model that cannot be served correctly (target-derived features without history, framework mismatch, bad checksum) is refused at load or at request, never served with a plausible wrong answer.
Batch results are delivered by reference; no result bytes and no presigned URLs pass through a log.
Job state survives a process restart.
Retrain produces a candidate; a human promotes it.
No feature in this ledger writes to any MODEL-FLOW wizard path, and no MODEL-FLOW feature is reopened to accommodate one.
